profile: Cory Dodds, a junior political science major from Smithland, Kentucky, was elected SGA president for 2012-13 in spring 2012 over Austin Wingate and Corey Johnson, after two years as SGA's director of information technology, during which he built a legislation and minutes archive for the SGA website that he said promoted transparency and accountability. Under the merged offices, Dodds also served as the student regent representing students on WKU's Board of Regents.

In office, Dodds led SGA in unanimously opposing an administration proposal to shift tuition to a per-credit-hour, bi-term model, which Provost Gordon Emslie dropped in February 2013 after student and faculty pushback. His administration also drafted a teaching assistant evaluation program the senate passed in February 2013, worked to restart a dormant student government at WKU's Glasgow campus, donated cameras to the Teaching and Learning Resource Center, and passed a resolution opposing a new $150 Study Abroad application fee; a Dodds amendment to bar SGA members from receiving SGA-awarded study-abroad scholarships, after 11 of 125 such awards had gone to SGA members that year, failed.

Dodds's term ended amid a contested succession: his successor, Keyana Boka, was elected in April 2013 but disqualified five days later by the Judicial Council 3-2 over a campaign email, then reinstated after appealing to Vice President for Student Affairs Howard Bailey. Later in 2012 Dodds was named a finalist for the Harry S. Truman Scholarship and, that November, WKU's first finalist for the George J. Mitchell Scholarship, the only Kentuckian among 20 national finalists. He went on to earn a law degree from Georgetown University, worked as directing attorney of the Children's Law Center and as a legal services staff attorney representing low-income clients in public benefits, housing and family law matters, and by the mid-2020s was a visiting professor at the University of Kentucky's J. David Rosenberg College of Law teaching Civil Procedure and Children and the Law, with research on rural "legal deserts" and the attorney shortage.

events.title: SGA worked to restart a student government for the Glasgow campus
events.body: SGA officials traveled to WKU's Glasgow campus to help restart its dormant student representative body and connect it to main campus. Dodds said Glasgow students had no mechanism for their voices to be heard except contacting main-campus SGA. Roy Ratliff, nominated interim president of the Glasgow student body, said its top priority was establishing a writing center, for which the group had set aside $2,700.

events.title: Provost Emslie cancelled the bi-term proposal SGA had opposed
events.body: Provost Gordon Emslie announced at the Feb. 21 University Senate meeting that he was dropping his bi-term emphasis proposal and had no plans to revive it, citing input from students and faculty. Both SGA and the University Senate had passed resolutions against it. Dodds said the revocation was in the student body's best interest, saying "I strongly opposed it."

events.title: Executive candidates debate ahead of spring election
events.body: Outgoing President Cory Dodds opened a candidates' debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium by describing to the audience how much influence the students elected to SGA's executive positions would actually have on WKU's campus, ahead of the election that would choose his successor.

events.title: Boka, Reeves and Seay won the spring executive elections
events.body: Executive vice president Keyana Boka was elected 2013-14 SGA president with 626 votes, 47 percent, over administrative vice president Cain Alvey with 419 votes and Austin Wingate with 300. Mark Reeves won executive vice president with 632 votes, 57 percent, over Brad Cockrel, and Nicki Seay ran unopposed for administrative vice president. Twenty-six student senators were also elected.

events.title: Judicial Council disqualified president-elect Boka, 3-2
events.body: In an emergency meeting, SGA's Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify president-elect Keyana Boka after runner-up and outgoing administrative vice president Cain Alvey complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at Boka's request, sent by Honors College graduate assistant Destiny Savage, violating the election code. The disqualification would have made Alvey, who had placed second in the April 4 vote, the incoming president; Boka said she would appeal.

events.title: Judicial Council declined to contest Bailey's reinstatement of Boka
events.body: In an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council unanimously decided not to challenge Bailey's memorandum reinstating Boka, saying it did not believe it had the power to do so, while expressing official disapproval. Chief Justice Seth Church called the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and said it set a bad precedent. Boka said the council had conflicts of interest and needed to be held accountable by a neutral party in the administration.

events.title: Fall senate seats filled after two resignations
events.body: Two senators resigned over time commitments and student Shea Wyatt was named to fill in. New freshman senators Barrett Greenwell, Taylor Ruby, Cole McDowell and Paige Settles were sworn in along with Gatton Academy senator Linda Cruz and graduate senators Mark Reeves and Katie Martin.

events.title: Senate reviewed its budget and heard a retention pitch
events.body: Speaker of the Senate Christopher Costa opened the floor to Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for Retention and Student Services, who asked senators for ideas on keeping students enrolled to graduation, and SGA's current budget balance was distributed to members.

events.title: Senate amended the constitution, adding regional-campus seats
events.body: After two to three years of executive discussion, the senate passed most of a package of constitutional amendments, replacing class-year senate seats with college-based representation and guaranteeing seats for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro. A bylaw that would have made SGA members permanently ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships was stripped out and did not pass.

events.title: Costa stepped down as speaker; Settles elected to succeed him
events.body: Christopher Costa did not seek another term as speaker of the senate, and senators elected Paige Settles to replace him. The same meeting confirmed presidential appointments Roy Ratliff as senator-at-large and Jackie Stewart as associate justice, with Chief of Staff Travis Taylor and public relations chair Mac Mullins giving reports.

events.title: Senate opposed automatic athletic-fee increases ahead of C-USA move
events.body: The senate passed a resolution against the annual automatic increase in the student athletic fee, arguing the revenue-sharing WKU would gain on joining Conference USA that July would outweigh the roughly $40,000 the university lost annually in the Sun Belt. Executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who introduced it, said the resolution set a precedent against automatic fee increases generally.

events.title: Senate creates a long-term goals committee by executive action
events.body: SGA voted unanimously on an executive action establishing a special long-term goals committee of at least eight members, including students from outside SGA appointed by President Cory Dodds. Dodds said the committee could draw up a set of goals to focus on for the next few years. A bill to distribute $800 in senate funding as eight $100 Study Away scholarships received its first read.

events.title: ID voucher pilot program introduced covering 80 student IDs
events.body: A bill in first read would have SGA pay $10 toward each regular-priced student identification card under an identification voucher pilot program, partially covering the cost of 80 cards. A second bill sought $225 for the Sigma Gamma Rho sorority's Hair Show Spectacular. A resolution setting the fall campus clean-up date was held over because it had not reached the Legislative Research Committee.

events.title: SGA adopts a new voting system and holds the South Campus food court resolution
events.body: At its eighth meeting SGA implemented a new voting system and gave a first read to an organizational aid bill covering the Student Veteran's Alliance ($175), the WKU chapter of the American Society for Microbiology ($150) and the Academic Competition Club ($275). A resolution supporting a food court at South Campus, due for a second read, was instead held in new business.

events.title: Retention official addresses SGA and gets no senator feedback
events.body: Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for retention and student services, spoke to SGA about keeping students enrolled through graduation and asked what student leaders could do to help. No senators offered feedback during the meeting, and she encouraged members to contact her later. SGA's current budget was circulated at the start of the meeting showing the remaining balance and money spent.

events.title: Glasgow campus ratifies its own student government constitution
events.body: Glasgow's Associated Student Body ratified its constitution on Nov. 16 by unanimous vote with no abstentions. Interim president Roy Ratliff said the goal was to give SGA a presence on the regional campus and give regional students a vote in student government. The Glasgow body adopted the same bylaws as SGA and began selecting committees for the spring.

events.title: Provost pitches value-added grading to SGA at final fall meeting
events.body: Provost Gordon Emslie and University Senate member Guy Jordan addressed SGA on a proposed value-added grading system under which students in the top third of B and C grades would receive an extra quality point and a plus designation. Emslie said an earlier plus-minus proposal had taken several years to develop "only to be dashed at the last minute." Jordan argued the value-added version worked because faculty gave something up and students did not.

events.title: Senate rejects the value-added grading resolution in a close vote
events.body: The value-added grading resolution failed on a close vote, disappointing President Cory Dodds, who called it a tangible benefit that increased student competitiveness and said it was "a real shame that our senate didn't see that." Provost Gordon Emslie had introduced the system to SGA and the University Senate in fall 2012. Some senate members opposed the change.

events.title: Constitution overhaul passes but senate strips the scholarship conflict rule
events.body: SGA adopted a package of constitutional and bylaw amendments with one exception: the senate rejected the bylaw that would have made serving SGA members ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships. Administrative Vice President Cain Alvey said executives had been discussing changes for two to three years and had gone through the constitution article by article, first presenting the changes on Feb. 19. Alvey said an amendment guaranteeing representation for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro was the one he liked most.

events.title: Four SGA leaders publicly accuse the senate of rejecting accountability
events.body: President Cory Dodds, Travis Taylor, Brittany Crowley and Drew Mitchell wrote a commentary attacking the senate for rejecting the amendment that would have barred serving SGA members from SGA-sponsored scholarships and grants. They wrote that 11 SGA members had received such scholarships or grants since the spring of 2011. The authors said this amounted to a breach of student trust and a conflict of interest.

events.title: Regents committee approves SGA's teaching assistant evaluation policy
events.body: SGA announced that the Board of Regents had unanimously approved the teaching assistant evaluation resolution at its March 29 committee meeting, with the full board to take it up on April 26. President Gary Ransdell said he had recommended approval and that there was little discussion because students and faculty were in agreement. The policy would require departments to provide a way for students to evaluate teaching assistants.

events.title: SGA votes to end the automatic annual athletic fee increase
events.body: The senate passed a resolution supporting an end to the automatic annual increase in the student athletic fee once WKU joined Conference USA on July 1, 2014. Senator and executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who initiated it, argued that increased revenues made the automatic increase unnecessary. The resolution stated that WKU athletics paid $80,000 in the Sun Belt Conference but received only $40,000 back in revenue sharing.

events.title: Budget cuts strip SGA's automatic inflation increase
events.body: University budget cuts announced that week removed the automatic increases that SGA, the Campus Activities Board and leadership programs normally received under the Higher Education Price Index, saving the university $8,000. Charley Pride, director of Student Activities and SGA's adviser, said no money was taken away, which was better than losing money. Incoming President Keyana Boka said the loss could affect new programs SGA had wanted to start.

events.title: Former officer defends SGA's stance as administrators rename DUC anyway
events.body: Former Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan wrote after the Administrative Council decided the building would be called Downing Student Union. He wrote that former President Cory Dodds had correctly told campus officials students preferred Downing University Center, noting the student assembly had voted against the change in 2011 when asked to do so by administrators. Bryan wrote that student opinion had not changed since that vote.

events.title: Senate bought T-shirts for the autumn Campus Clean-up
events.body: The senate unanimously approved funding on 9 October 2012 for promotional T-shirts for volunteers at the Campus Clean-up on 23 October, timed with Make a Difference Day. Committee chairman Mallory Chaney said dark grey shirts with the SGA logo would read something like "Tops making a difference" and would give students an incentive to turn out. Executive vice president Keyana Boka called the twice-yearly clean-up an important tradition, one the Herald traced back to WKU president Henry Cherry.

src.label: Herald, 12 Oct 2012 - "SGA bill funds Campus Clean-up"

events.title: Picnic with the president in the Ransdells' back garden
events.body: Gary and Julie Ransdell hosted SGA's executive board, student senators and the WKU Administrative Council for a cookout at their home on 22 October 2012, business casual. Ransdell said he had come up with the idea after months of talks with SGA president Cory Dodds about connecting his office to SGA. Dodds said the picnic had been running for several years and was an SGA tradition.

src.label: Herald, 17 Oct 2012 - "Picnic with the president a SGA tradition"

events.title: iPad lending programme opened with the Educational Resources Center
events.body: SGA and the Educational Resources Center launched an iPad-lending programme giving students, staff and faculty access to tablets loaded with test preparation applications such as MCAT materials. ERC coordinator Roxanne Spencer said SGA had approached the centre wanting the iPads available for a pilot project. Executive vice president Keyana Boka said SGA had bought the iPads the previous year but could not start lending until they were secured against tampering.

src.label: Herald, 30 Nov 2012 - "SGA, ERC collaborate for iPad program"

events.title: Dine with Decision Makers moved to the Kentucky Museum
events.body: SGA held Dine with Decision Makers at the Kentucky Museum on 5 December 2012, seating officials from across Kentucky and WKU administrators at tables matched to students by interest or field. President Cory Dodds opened the evening and executive vice president Keyana Boka said the prayer. Wadsworth, Ohio senior Sarah Brazier gave the keynote, arguing that higher education built a productive economy and an informed citizenry rather than only advancing individuals.

events.title: Safe Rides purple line returned for the spring
events.body: SGA's Safe Rides service, known on campus as the purple line, continued into spring 2013 after autumn 2012 became the first semester WKU ran a fixed-route late-night bus rather than a taxi contract. President Cory Dodds said the consistency of set pick-up points and times was why it worked where Provide-A-Ride had not. Administrative vice president Cain Alvey said Provide-A-Ride had been an unreliable taxi service by comparison.

src.label: Herald, 8 Feb 2013 - "SGA's safe rides program will continue for the spring semester"

events.title: ID voucher programme halved the cost of a replacement card
events.body: SGA's ID voucher programme, running since the middle of the autumn 2012 semester, let students pay $10 rather than $20 for their first replacement student ID. The bill behind it allocated $800 to part-cover 80 cards. Administrative vice president Cain Alvey said the idea came from his job as a resident assistant in McCormack Hall, and that SGA covered only the first loss so as to teach responsibility and spread the benefit. Vouchers were collected from the SGA office in Cravens Library room 13.

src.label: Herald, 12 Feb 2013 - "SGA provides vouchers to replace lost IDs"

events.title: Eight Study Away scholarships funded as transcript vouchers ran on
events.body: The senate passed a bill on 12 February 2013 allocating $800 for eight $100 Study Away scholarships covering the spring and summer 2013 programmes. SGA reported that 30 of the semester's transcript vouchers had been used, with 70 left. Campus improvements chair Mallory Chaney set the spring Campus Safety Walk for 26 February.

src.label: Herald, 13 Feb 2013 - "SGA approves bill for Study Away scholarships"

events.title: Senate unanimously opposed the bi-term calendar and per-credit-hour tuition
events.body: SGA unanimously passed a resolution opposing the administration's proposal to emphasize bi-term courses and shift tuition to a per-credit-hour model. The bi-term plan would have put students in 80-minute classes on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, and President Gary Ransdell had said it would let a student carry a full load plus a summer or winter course and graduate in three years. President Cory Dodds objected chiefly to the per-credit-hour shift, arguing it would charge students more because full-time students then paid for 12 hours but could enroll in up to 18. He called it a financial burden students should not have to bear.

events.title: Senate tabled Hannah Garland's plus-minus grading resolution
events.body: Academic Affairs chair Hannah Garland's resolution to add plus and minus grades to As, Bs, Cs and Ds was tabled at the Tuesday meeting after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal and more student input first, and most of the senate agreed. Garland said the system would make GPAs more exact and might make WKU more competitive. President Cory Dodds said the executive board had discussed putting the question directly to students on the spring ballot. A similar plan had drawn SGA resistance when the provost proposed it in 2007.

events.title: Senate passed the teaching assistant evaluation resolution
events.body: On 5 February the senate passed a resolution creating teaching assistant evaluations, a program President Cory Dodds had campaigned on and developed with his executive officers before pitching it to Provost Gordon Emslie. Nicki Seay, chair of the Legislative Research Committee, wrote the measure, which aimed to make TA evaluation uniform across departments. Dodds said the idea had been worked on for many years. The resolution next needed review by the Academic Quality Committee and approval by the University Senate.

events.title: SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 study abroad application fee
events.body: The senate passed a resolution opposing a new $150 application fee for Study Abroad and Global Learning, due to begin with summer 2013 programs, arguing it could put program costs out of reach. Executive Vice President Keyana Boka said SGA took a formal stance because the fee had come up so suddenly, and the University Senate passed a similar resolution seeking to delay the fee until fall 2013. A separate amendment proposed by Dodds, to make SGA members ineligible for SGA-awarded study abroad scholarships, failed. Dodds said 11 of the 125 such scholarships and grants awarded that year had gone to SGA members, which he called a conflict of interest.

executive.name: Cory Dodds
executive.note: Also served as student regent under the merged offices.

executive.name: Keyana Boka
executive.note: Elected uncontested alongside Dodds in March 2012; went on to be elected 2013-14 president, spelled "Keyanna" in that year's coverage. Spelling unverified between the two forms.

executive.name: Cain Alvey
executive.note: Ran unsuccessfully for president in the April 2013 election as outgoing administrative vice president.

officers.name: Christopher Costa
officers.note: Did not seek another term; Paige Settles was elected to succeed him in April 2013 for 2013-14.

committees.name: Legislative Research
committees.note: Wrote the teaching assistant evaluation bill Dodds campaigned on.

committees.name: Campus Improvements
committees.note: Postponed the annual campus safety walk to April 2013.

senate.note: Constitutional amendments passed 26 Feb 2013 replaced class-year senate seats with college-based representation and added guaranteed seats for the Glasgow and Owensboro regional campuses.

leaders.name: Keyanna Boka
leaders.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index as student regent, 2013. Plaque spells the first name KEYANNA; the archives index reads Boka, Keyana - confirm which is correct.
profile: Boka, the outgoing executive vice president, was elected 2013-14 SGA president on 4 April 2013 with 626 votes (47 percent), beating administrative vice president Cain Alvey (419 votes) and Austin Wingate (300). Five days later the Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify her after Alvey, the runner-up who stood to become president if she were removed, complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at her request. Boka appealed to Howard Bailey, WKU's vice president for Student Affairs, who reinstated her; the Judicial Council declined to contest his ruling in an emergency meeting on 16 April, with Chief Justice Seth Church calling the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and Boka countering that the council itself had conflicts of interest.

In office, Boka's fall 2013 senate created a new international student senate seat for Navitas/ESL students and finalized a $125,000 budget, part of which sent her and executive vice president Mark Reeves on a Washington, D.C. higher-education lobbying trip. She fielded student anger over new two-tier priority registration rules at a November open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie, and announced the permanent closure of Thompson Complex North Wing, long slated for demolition. A senate attempt to reverse SGA's support for the Talisman's student fee was struck down by the Judicial Council as unconstitutional, as was the underlying 2005 policy.

In spring 2014 Boka organized a Frankfort rally against a $1.8 million state budget cut to WKU and opposed a senate amendment stripping the president's sole power to appoint Judicial Council justices, which was sent back to committee after the council found too few senators had been present to pass it. At the year's final meeting she announced a 4.8 percent tuition increase for the coming year, and the senate passed a resolution backing a Good Samaritan policy to protect students who called 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

events.title: Priority registration complaints spurred open forum
events.body: Student complaints over new two-tier priority registration rules, including a 16-credit-hour cap during the priority period, pushed SGA to schedule a Nov. 12 open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie. Honors College seniors told senator Tyler Scaff some were considering dropping the honors major over the change. Boka said she had no official stance yet, though SGA had earlier approved the change through Reeves's vote at University Senate.

events.title: Thompson Complex North Wing set to close permanently
events.body: Boka announced at the Tuesday SGA meeting that Thompson Complex North Wing, home to the biology and chemistry departments, would close permanently the next semester because the building could not be maintained over the winter. The building had been labeled for demolition since 2005, and its demolition along with renovation of the Center Wing was the university's top capital priority before the Kentucky General Assembly.

events.title: Judicial Council voided Talisman fee stance reversal
events.body: After the yearbook's budget was cut to $127,000, senator Chris Costa moved at the Nov. 19 meeting to revoke SGA's stance supporting a $9 student fee for the Talisman that students had approved on a 2005 ballot, and two-thirds of SGA voted to reverse the stance. The Judicial Council ruled Costa's motion unconstitutional on Nov. 21, and also ruled the original 2005 policy unconstitutional because it was never passed according to SGA policy. Talisman editors then met with Boka and SGA members to discuss long-term funding options.

events.title: SGA reconvened, planned Frankfort rally against budget cuts
events.body: At the first spring meeting, Boka announced a planned trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million state budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Reeves warned that tough budget cuts were coming, and the body reviewed a proposal to revise the change-of-major advising process. Five members had resigned the previous semester, leaving the legislative research and public relations chairs among the vacant seats.

events.title: Final meeting passed Good Samaritan resolution, funding bills
events.body: At the last meeting of the semester, Boka announced students would face a 4.8 percent tuition increase, about $209 more per semester for most, alongside a $4.2 million increase in student financial assistance. The Senate suspended its bylaws to pass a slate of bills funding Summer Term assistance, student organizations, student research and an Earth Week planting party. Resolution 6-14-S passed in support of adopting a Good Samaritan Policy protecting students who call 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

events.title: Senate passed international student seat amendment
events.body: President Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves authored a constitutional amendment adding a senate seat for Navitas or English as a Second Language international students. The Judicial Council had ruled an earlier version unconstitutional, but after a revision in an emergency meeting the Senate passed it with only two votes against. Boka said it would make WKU's SGA the first student government in the state with an international senate seat.

events.title: Presidential debate drew full field of candidates
events.body: Ahead of the spring 2013 election, outgoing president Cory Dodds opened a debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium among presidential candidates Cain Alvey, Keyana Boka and Austin Wingate, plus executive vice presidential candidates Brad Cockrel and Mark Reeves and administrative vice presidential candidate Nicki Seay. Boka said SGA members needed better training in their roles, Alvey said the presidency's responsibilities went beyond the constitution, and Wingate, a former Speaker of the Senate, called for better representation across student groups.

events.title: Executive Council floated plus/minus grading, set fall calendar
events.body: At the Executive Council's weekly meeting, Executive Vice President Mark Reeves reported that the University Senate Council had discussed reviving a plus/minus grading system and that Provost Gordon Emslie was interested in SGA's support. The council set a Nov. 9 Picnic with the President for the presidents' council and deans, and swore in Samantha Johnson to an executive cabinet seat vacated by the resignation of Keith Watson.

events.title: SGA reviewed 24-hour dining, grading and registration proposals
events.body: SGA gave first read to a proposal for a 24-hour on-campus dining option, with the Organizational Aid Committee sponsoring the resolution and assistant vice president for auxiliary services Gary Meszaros set to attend the next meeting. Reeves told senators Provost Gordon Emslie was reviving a plus/minus grading proposal and had brought priority registration and major-declaration changes to University Senate.

events.title: Judicial Council strikes down the international senate seat amendment
events.body: SGA announced that the Judicial Council had ruled unconstitutional a constitutional amendment proposed by President Keyana Boka and Executive Vice President Mark Reeves. The amendment would have changed the senate's composition by adding one seat for an international student. The ruling was reported to the senate at its second meeting of the semester.

events.title: Emergency Judicial Council meeting clears reworded international seat
events.body: SGA called an emergency Judicial Council meeting to review revisions to the amendment the council had rejected on Aug. 29 for violating WKU's non-discrimination clause. Boka and Reeves changed the wording from "one international student senator" to a Navitas or English as a Second Language international student seat. Boka said the emergency session was routine protocol for any meeting outside the council's regular schedule.

events.title: Herald editorial questions SGA's handpicked approach to diversity
events.body: A Herald editorial examined the proposed permanent senate seat for an international student, ruled unconstitutional on Aug. 29 and then revised and approved in a six-minute emergency meeting. The editorial said it supported SGA's effort to expand representation but questioned whether a designated seat was the most effective means. Boka and Reeves had said their intention was to better represent WKU's international student population.

events.title: Student petition for 24-hour dining collects 700 signatures for SGA
events.body: Bowling Green sophomore Nick Conrad, a McCormack Hall resident assistant, gathered more than 700 signatures in about a week on a petition asking for a 24-hour dining option on campus, with a stated goal of 5,000. Conrad said he studied late and knew many students on similar schedules. He had met with SGA representatives who were interested in the petition.

events.title: Senate funds transcript vouchers with $300
events.body: SGA passed a bill allotting $300 to the Transcript Voucher Program fund, letting students collect vouchers from the SGA office instead of paying the $7 transcript fee. Academic Affairs committee head Megan Skaggs, who wrote the bill, said students already paid a great deal in tuition and fees. Funding for the long-running program had to be renewed by senate vote each time more money was needed.

events.title: Resolution targets the internet policy behind WKU's FIRE red light rating
events.body: A resolution by Director of Public Relations Laura Harper received its first read, supporting amendment of university internet usage policies that the Foundation for Individual Rights in Education had deemed a violation of free speech. FIRE had given WKU a red light rating because at least one handbook policy violated the First Amendment. Computing Policy 12-13, covering email content likely to be perceived as offensive or disparaging, was the specific cause.

events.title: Internet policy resolution and ID voucher bill pass at a short meeting
events.body: With attendance thinned by a home football game where SGA ran a Safe Ride promotional booth, the senate passed Resolution 3-13-F on internet usage policies and Bill 2-13-F funding identification vouchers. Two further bills went into first read, one on organizational aid and one funding six winter term scholarship sessions. Laura Harper introduced the internet policy resolution.

events.title: SGA spends $1,598 on five charging stations with the libraries
events.body: SGA and WKU Libraries agreed to buy five KwikBoost phone and laptop charging stations for $1,598, each with eight charging attachments. President Keyana Boka said Dean of University Libraries Connie Foster brought her the idea. Three stations were planned for the Educational Resources Center, Helm 100 and Helm 2, with the other two going to the Glasgow and Owensboro campuses.

events.title: Provost and registrar face students at SGA's priority registration forum
events.body: SGA hosted an open forum on priority registration during its weekly meeting, with Provost Gordon Emslie and University Registrar Freida Eggleton answering questions. The policy, already in effect for spring registration, split priority registration into a need tier and a benefit tier and capped qualifying students at 16 credit hours until open registration. Seniors and graduate students still registered first and were not subject to the cap.

events.title: South Campus forum turns on the closing of the campus store
events.body: SGA held its weekly meeting at South Campus as an open forum and President Keyana Boka asked those present to discuss the recent closing of the South Campus WKU store. Senators debated the lack of communication between the officials who closed the store and South Campus students. Executive Vice President Mark Reeves said the same thing had happened the previous year when the food court closed, calling it part of a broader failure to consult South Campus students.

events.title: Talisman brings its funding shortfall to SGA
events.body: Talisman representatives met President Keyana Boka and Brad Cockrel on Nov. 29 to discuss long-term options for paying for the yearbook. The previous May the Talisman had faced a proposed $93,000 cut, 47 percent of its $198,000 budget, before an alumni-backed "Save the Talisman" campaign reduced the cut. Its budget stood at $127,000, including $45,000 in one-time university funds.

events.title: Student on crutches brings a bus stop bench proposal to the senate
events.body: Covington senior Logan Eckler went before SGA on Nov. 19 to propose benches at campus bus stops after several days on crutches following a judo injury. He said the bus system was invaluable for students who had difficulty walking but that few stops had seats. Eckler said the same problem affected pregnant students and people with disabilities, and that SGA senators he knew had recommended he bring it forward.

events.title: SGA plans a Frankfort rally over WKU's $1.8 million budget cut
events.body: At the first spring meeting President Keyana Boka announced SGA would organize a trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Executive Vice President Mark Reeves outlined the two-year state budget then being voted on and said students needed to be involved. Boka also reported talks with dining services about 24-hour dining, with Einstein's Bagels under consideration for its location in a 24-hour study area.

events.title: SGA unanimously backs taking the Campus Pride Index
events.body: An SGA proposal that WKU take the Campus Pride Index, a survey measuring campus friendliness toward LGBT students, passed unanimously and was submitted to the Administrative Council. Student Identity Outreach president Andrew Salman first proposed it to the Office of Diversity, and senator Nicki Seay carried it into SGA. Salman said the index would diagnose areas where the university was not meeting the needs of its queer students, and Seay said WKU had never taken it before.

events.title: Turnout falls to 908, down 555 votes from the previous year
events.body: A Herald editorial reported that SGA voter turnout for the spring election was 908, down 555 votes from the year before. The editorial called turnout below 1,000 pathetic and said the student body could and should do better. It noted that the SGA president represents students at the Board of Regents and that SGA funds organizational aid and extended library hours.

events.title: SGA suspends its bylaws to clear bills at the last meeting
events.body: At the final meeting of the semester SGA suspended its bylaws to pass multiple bills on first read, beginning with Bill 17-14-S allocating $1,817.10. President Keyana Boka reported a 4.8 percent tuition increase that would cost most students about $209 more per semester, along with a $4.2 million increase for student financial assistance and a one percent faculty salary adjustment. Speaker Paige Settles said one remaining scholarship bill would be handled at a short meeting during the end-of-year banquet.

events.title: Safe Ride ran a booth at Homecoming tailgating
events.body: SGA members staffed a Safe Ride promotional booth during tailgating for the home football game on 15 October 2013 and gave a presentation at halftime. Attendance at that evening's senate meeting was lighter than usual as a result, and the meeting was cut short, though a resolution on internet usage policy and a bill funding identification vouchers both passed.

src.label: Herald, 17 Oct 2013 - "SGA passes bills for ID vouchers funding"

events.title: SGA opened Earth Week by planting the community garden
events.body: SGA and the Office of Sustainability kicked off Earth Week on 21 April 2014 with a planting party in the community garden behind the sustainability house at 503 Regents Avenue. President Keyana Boka said she was glad SGA could support the garden, which SGA's campus improvement committee then took on maintaining, growing tomatoes, squash, sunflowers and peppers. Garden coordinator Beth McGrew said the aim was to build community through sustainability and strengthen students' connection to their food.

src.label: Herald, 21 Apr 2014 - "SGA and Office of Sustainability Kick-Off Earth Week"

events.title: Campus-wide safety walk from Centennial Mall
events.body: SGA held a campus safety walk starting at Centennial Mall at 6:30 p.m. on 24 April 2014, inviting students to point out anywhere they felt unsafe, whether dark or unstable. President Keyana Boka said the purpose was to promote safety.

src.label: Herald, 24 Apr 2014 - "SGA hosts campus wide safety walk"

events.title: Executive Council voided the amendment stripping the president's judicial appointments
events.body: An amendment removing the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the council to seven justices passed at the Tuesday meeting, over President Keyana Boka's objection that it bypassed both presidential appointment and the senate. Boka said the president is elected by the student body to make appointments in all three branches and that she was wary of the direction, while Chief Justice Seth Church argued that vesting appointments in the executive branch as a whole created a fairer system. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution, found too few senators had attended for the vote to count and declared the amendment unconstitutional, sending it back to first read. The SGA office had temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens.

events.title: 564 voted in the fall election; referendum created the Navitas/ESL seat
events.body: A total of 564 students voted in the fall SGA election. The referendum creating a Navitas and English as a Second Language international student senate seat drew 426 votes and passed with 310 yes votes, 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, led by Jay Todd Richey with 27 percent, along with two graduate senators, a Gatton Academy senator and an Arts and Letters senator. Most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates.

events.title: Herald editorial faulted SGA over the priority registration policy
events.body: A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority registration policy, which capped students with priority registration at 16 hours on their priority day and exempted seniors and graduate students. The editorial said executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at the University Senate on 10 September without SGA questioning or debating it first. It also faulted SGA for scheduling an open forum for 12 November, after the policy was already set to govern fall registration. Representing students was SGA's one job, the editorial argued, and it had not been done on this issue.

events.title: SGA finalized a $125,000 budget after a planned increase fell through
events.body: SGA finalized a 2013-14 budget of $125,000 drawn from student tuition, after a planned funding increase did not come through. Director of Public Relations Laura Harper said the figure equated to about $6.25 per student. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each, and the executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay, who built the budget, said senate discretionary spending required a senate majority and executive discretionary spending an executive committee majority.

events.title: Mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus
events.body: SGA's mid-year report on its $125,000 budget showed a surplus of $46,883.62. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay said the budget had changed little since December and that she had more funds to allocate back to the student body, and $54,000 had gone to the legislative branch for items such as organizational aid and grants. The senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index. Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart were approved as senators, leaving six senate seats open.

senate.note: Twenty-six student senators were elected in the April 2013 spring election alongside the executive officers. Executive Council minutes for 10 Sept 2013 list cabinet members Sarah Hazelip, Hannah Garland, Paige Settles, Laura Harper and Brad Cockrel alongside Boka, Reeves and Seay; Samantha Johnson was sworn in that night to a seat vacated by Keith Watson's resignation.

leaders.name: Nicki Taylor
leaders.note: The chambers plaque carries two consecutive plates for this year: "Janet 'Nicki' Seay" and "Nicki Taylor." Herald coverage shows one continuous officeholder, not a succession: she opened the year as "Nicki Seay" (Herald, 28 Aug and 25 Sep 2014), was already being called "Nicki Taylor" by the very next issue on 15 Oct 2014, and was still SGA president under that name through the 2 Apr 2015 election that chose her successor - no election, resignation or hand-off for a second officeholder appears anywhere in that span. Treated here as a single president who changed her surname partway through the term.
profile: Nicki Seay had been SGA's Legislative Research Chair in 2012-13 and ran successfully for administrative vice president in the spring 2013 election. She took office as SGA president in August 2014, a Crofton senior, alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles, and named student involvement, retention and graduation her priorities. Her administration opened the year by expanding SGA's summer and winter need-based scholarship program from $6,000 to $21,000.

By the middle of October 2014 the Herald was referring to the same sitting president as Nicki Taylor; no election or resignation separates the two names in the paper's coverage. As Taylor, she presided over a fall senate that voted down a nonsectarian prayer resolution, saw its smoke-free campus resolution vetoed by the Executive Cabinet and sustained on a failed override vote, and passed a resolution backing changes to the campus alcohol policy. She addressed WKU's December 2014 commencement as SGA president, telling graduates, "You have the rest of your life to look forward to."

In the spring semester the senate under Taylor passed a limited-smoking-campus resolution and a resolution backing a $10 million parking garage funded by a new student fee; President Gary Ransdell responded formally to both. She also sat, by virtue of the office, on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking measure because of that seat. Her term ended with the 2 April 2015 election of Jay Todd Richey as her successor.

events.title: An election result challenged and upheld
events.body: Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won.

events.title: SGA opened the year with a $21,000 scholarship program
events.body: SGA began the year under new president Nicki Seay, a Crofton senior, working alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles. The association expanded its summer and winter term need-based scholarship program from the previous year's $6,000 to $21,000, funded in part by an anonymous donation. Seay named student involvement, retention and graduation her first priorities.

events.title: President Taylor addressed December graduates
events.body: SGA President Nicki Taylor spoke at WKU's December commencement, telling graduates to celebrate what they had accomplished: "You have the rest of your life to look forward to." She had opened the year in August under her previous surname, Seay, and was going by Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October.

events.title: President Taylor abstained on smoking vote as a sitting regent
events.body: The Bowling Green Daily News reported that Nicki Taylor, in addition to serving as SGA president, sat on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking-campus proposal because of that seat.

events.title: Limited smoking campus resolution passed 13-11
events.body: SGA passed Resolution 1-15-S, supporting a limited smoking campus, by a 13-11 vote. The resolution would restrict tobacco use to 39 designated areas that the Administrative Council would gradually phase out over three years, while leaving electronic cigarettes and smokeless tobacco unrestricted. Co-author Seth Church said it was roughly the fifth version of the resolution since the smoking debate began the previous semester.

events.title: Jay Todd Richey won the SGA presidency, 874 votes to 524
events.body: Jay Todd Richey defeated senator Brian Chism for SGA president, 63 percent to 37 percent, or 874 votes to 524, with results announced about 20 minutes after TopNet polls closed at 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. Nolan Miles ran unopposed for a second term as executive vice president, and Liz Koehler won the administrative vice president race with 66 percent over J. William Berry. Twenty of 34 senatorial candidates won seats.

events.title: Commuter focus group brings parking fixes to the senate
events.body: Campus Improvements Committee Chair Tyler Scaff reported that a commuter focus group had proposed solutions to campus parking problems, including adding a function to the iWKU app that would list each lot with the number of spaces available. A South Campus park and ride was also proposed. Scaff said the committee was working on other projects including an SGA garden plot at the Office of Sustainability.

events.title: SGA funds an emergency food program for students with frozen accounts
events.body: Bill 10-14-F passed without debate, allocating $500 from legislative discretionary funds toward the $3,600 Emergency Food Pilot Program. The program gave the first 50 students who could show their university account was locked 10 free meals through Fresh Food Company waivers. Author William Berry said it would let those students eat for a few days while they worked on paying their bills.

events.title: Glasgow rewrites its constitution after struggling to keep members
events.body: Amendments to Glasgow's SGA constitution received their first read on the main campus. Chief of Staff Seth Church said Glasgow's constitution had been modeled on the main campus document and that the regional campus had struggled with student involvement and retaining SGA members, so it was decided to change the constitution drastically. Glasgow's SGA had already voted to approve the amendments, leaving the main campus senate to ratify them.

events.title: President establishes a Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee
events.body: SGA created a Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee chaired by Seth Church, who developed the idea for a leadership practicum focused on diversity within SGA and on campus. Church said he collaborated with President Nicki Taylor to create it. Taylor said making SGA more diverse had been an ongoing conversation since her first year and that establishing ad hoc committees was a power she held as president.

events.title: SGA backs limiting smoking to 39 areas and phasing them out
events.body: The senate voted on Resolution 1-15-S supporting a limited smoking campus, restricting tobacco use to 39 designated areas. The resolution called for the Administrative Council to create a plan reducing those areas and gradually phasing them out over three years, and would not have limited electronic cigarettes or smokeless tobacco. The existing policy allowed smoking anywhere on campus at least 30 feet from buildings.

events.title: SGA pursues new student fees; Ransdell calls even $4 difficult
events.body: SGA said it would pursue further fee resolutions after passing one the previous semester supporting a $4 per year fee for the Student Legal Services Clinic, and had begun asking students about a roughly $30 fee to fund an estimated $10 million parking structure. President Nicki Taylor said the ideas grew out of student interest in conversation with President Gary Ransdell. Ransdell said approving even a $4 fee would be difficult and that he would be reluctant to take it to the Board of Regents.

events.title: Breast milk expression resolution passes unanimously without debate
events.body: Resolution 4-15-S, supporting creation and maintenance of private areas on campus where students, faculty and staff could express breast milk, passed unanimously and without debate. Chief of Staff Seth Church, who wrote it, said a non-traditional student who had just had her third child brought the problem to him and found the existing unlocked room in a department hall uncomfortable. Church said he wanted no fewer than three permanent spaces.

events.title: Campaign spending caps range from $350 for president to $50 for senators
events.body: Under the spring 2014 election packet, SGA presidential candidates could not spend more than $350, executive vice president candidates $300, administrative vice president candidates $250 and senatorial candidates $50. President Nicki Taylor said she ran unopposed and did not spend a cent, but pointed to the contested 2013 race between Cain Alvey and Keyana Boka. Taylor said Alvey spent every dollar of his $350 limit.

events.title: Two hours of debate over an African Student Union reimbursement
events.body: Bill 8-15-S, allocating $500 to the WKU African Student Union as reimbursement for attending a conference at the University of Kentucky, passed 12 to four with many senators abstaining, after a meeting that ran two hours and ended with fewer senators present. Acting president Henry Nottinson said the reimbursement would lessen the burden on members who had paid out of pocket. He said the group did not have enough money to keep going.

events.title: Former senator publishes a letter alleging corruption in organizational aid
events.body: Jody Dahmer, who had joined SGA as a freshman, published a letter to the editor arguing that a precedent set during the past session had damaged the organizational aid process. He described the standing system under which organizations could receive up to $500 per academic year, reviewed by the administrative vice president and senators under existing bylaws with forms posted on the SGA website. Dahmer wrote that organizations met the committee outside the senate and that reports were then forwarded and voted on quickly.

events.title: SGA funds a $825.95 surveillance camera for the DSU ATMs
events.body: Bill 10-15-S allocated $825.95 to buy and install a surveillance video camera on the ground floor of the Downing Student Union near the ATMs, passing 15-5 after debate. Author J. William Berry said a camera would be far cheaper than relocating the ATMs to an area with more foot traffic. Campus improvements committee chair Tyler Scaff questioned the plan, and Berry noted DSU closes at midnight.

events.title: Richey posts the SGA budget publicly and says he has no figures
events.body: President Jay Todd Richey used social media to be, in his words, "very transparent with the WKU Student Government Association budget." SGA had not yet received its budget for the coming fiscal year, and the Executive Cabinet controlled the budget over the summer. Richey said he had not been given a concrete amount of how much money remained from that year.

events.title: Downing Student Union celebrated its community opening
events.body: WKU held a ceremonial community opening for Downing Student Union after a two-year, $49 million renovation; the building had opened to students the week before. Students paid $36 million of the cost through a $70-per-semester fee, and the renovation began as an SGA initiative in 2011. SGA President Nicki Seay attended alongside President Gary Ransdell and other officials.

events.title: Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators
events.body: SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union, before a crowd of about 15 people. There were 742 voters and 17 senators elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive and said not everyone who ran won a seat. The senators-elect were sworn in at the 30 September meeting.

events.title: Senate failed to override the smoking veto and passed an alcohol resolution
events.body: At the final meeting of the fall semester, which ran two and a half hours, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free campus resolution. President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement, which cited enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly.

events.title: Senate defeated the nonsectarian prayer policy resolution
events.body: After more than 20 minutes of debate the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. Chief of Staff Seth Church explained that a nonsectarian prayer differs from a sectarian one referring to a specific deity. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways, among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all, and that the division sank the resolution. The same night senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity.

events.title: SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 per semester tuition rise
events.body: SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a $10 million parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build, and the resolution suggested a temporary gravel lot on the site of Tate Page Hall after its anticipated demolition. President Nicki Taylor said the structure had been before the parking and transportation committee for the whole academic year. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out the regional campuses.

events.title: Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution hours after it passed
events.body: The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, and the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued a ban was unfair to students required to live on campus for two years, while author William Berry said he left the location of any smoking areas to the administration and that the ban infringed no student's rights. Senator Haley Jones countered that smoking is legal and that students over 18 can buy tobacco. The policy would not have covered other tobacco products or electronic cigarettes, and senators kept the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote.

events.title: Ransdell answered four SGA resolutions in an email to faculty and staff
events.body: President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions, on limited smoking, amending the alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct for students over 21, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. On smoking he announced a six-person ad hoc committee of students, faculty and staff to recommend how to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017. On alcohol he said a restaurant facility would be built in the Garrett Conference Center where beer, and possibly wine, could be served in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval.

executive.name: Nicki Taylor
executive.note: Took office in August 2014 as Nicki Seay; called Nicki Taylor in coverage from mid-October 2014 on.

senate.note: 17 senators were elected in the September 2014 fall election out of 742 votes cast; the spring 2015 election filled 20 of 34 contested senate seats.

leaders.name: Jay Todd Richey
leaders.note: Won amid anonymous complaints that he had breached election codes on poster placement. The Judicial Council warned him but confirmed the result stood.
profile: Richey opened his first term in fall 2015 "leaving behind the Postergate controversy" of the spring election, saying he had "about a hundred things" he wanted to do. His priorities included MyCampusToo, a campaign initiative to bring underrepresented students into SGA, more outreach to international students and the regional campuses, and stronger communication between the executive cabinet and senate. He also oversaw a student competition to name the new pub coming to the Garrett Conference Center, a product of the alcohol-policy change SGA had supported the previous year.

In September he championed the senate's resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building was approved, writing in a letter to the Herald that the contract was signed in China before the Board of Regents voted and that many controversial details were never disclosed. He rejected warnings that the vote made "powerful enemies," saying he hoped it sent a message that "accountability and transparency should always be top priorities" at WKU, while noting he respected Ransdell and would keep working with him.

In April 2016 Richey won reelection with 1,497 of 2,341 presidential votes, becoming a two-term president in a high-turnout election announced after midnight in the Downing Student Union senate chambers. "It's a tremendous honor to be elected the first time," he said, "but a second time is verification of promises kept." His running mate Kate Hart won executive vice president and MyCampusToo chairwoman Hannah Neeper won administrative vice president, keeping his allies in the executive branch for 2016-17. A March 2017 Herald profile noted the win made him WKU SGA's first two-term president since 1988 and one of only three since 1974.

events.title: Chief Justice resigned after censure hearing backlash
events.body: The Judicial Council unanimously declined to censure senator John Winstead, whom it had investigated over an "impeach Ransdell" sign and a mocking Facebook post about President Ransdell, ruling his actions were protected free speech. Winstead called the fact he was investigated at all "the problem I'm objecting to." Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell then announced she would step down at the end of the semester, saying the council had been publicly ridiculed and lacked support from fellow SGA members.

events.title: Ransdell announced retirement amid state budget cuts
events.body: President Gary Ransdell announced he would step down as WKU's ninth president on June 30, 2017, triggering a presidential search. The announcement came the same week new Gov. Matt Bevin ordered an immediate 4.5 percent cut to WKU's state funding and proposed a 9 percent cut, with future funding shifted to a performance-based pool. The changes framed much of SGA's advocacy for the rest of the year.

events.title: Senators lobbied legislators in Frankfort
events.body: SGA members traveled to Frankfort to lobby against state budget cuts that could slash WKU funding by as much as 9 percent, meeting with eight state officials. Senators pressed for smaller cuts and restoration of need-based aid, citing figures that about 15,000 students were denied need-based financial aid the prior year. Both chambers of the General Assembly recognized SGA for its participation.

events.title: Ransdell declined SGA's meningitis vaccine mandate
events.body: Richey read aloud a letter from Ransdell responding to Resolution 6-15-F, passed the previous semester, which supported requiring meningitis vaccinations for incoming freshmen living on campus starting with the class of 2020. Ransdell wrote that the university would highly recommend vaccination but "stop short of requiring it," citing a $143.77 cost for uninsured students at the Graves-Gilbert Clinic.

events.title: Senate passed guidelines for WKU's tenth president
events.body: The senate approved a resolution by John Winstead and Richey outlining what students wanted in WKU's tenth president, which Richey planned to use in his role on the presidential search committee. After debate, senators amended the sustainability clause to target improving WKU's AASHE STARS rating and voted to remove language about Jonesville "reparations" entirely, after disputing whether reparations or restitution was the right term.

events.title: Richey reelected in one of highest-turnout elections
events.body: Students reelected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president with 64 percent of the vote over Braxton Powell, in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history with 2,442 voters. Kate Hart, an Academic Affairs chairwoman and Richey's running mate, won executive vice president. Richey called the win "verification of promises kept."

events.title: Richey outlined fall goals, MyCampusToo launch
events.body: Opening his first term, President Jay Todd Richey said he wanted more executive-cabinet and senate communication and more outreach to international students and regional campuses, and confirmed his campaign initiative MyCampusToo would launch that semester. Executive Vice President Nolan Miles said he would push senators to sit on university committees and revive the Dine with Decision Makers event.

events.title: Senate backed meningitis vaccine requirement, amended bylaws
events.body: The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 6-15-F supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, and unanimously passed Bill 10-15-F amending SGA's bylaws. Richey reported that his fall listening tours of the regional campuses had gone well and turned up how different those campuses were from main campus.

events.title: SGA tables Confucius Institute resolution, creates sustainability committee
events.body: The senate tabled Resolution 1-15-F, which would have concurred with the University Senate in asking President Gary Ransdell to revisit WKU's contract with Hanban, citing uncertainty about the contract terms. At the same meeting Bill 1-15-F recognizing an Elizabethtown/Fort Knox student body association and Bill 2-15-F supporting the MyCampusToo initiative both passed unanimously, as did an executive proposal creating a sustainability committee. President Jay Todd Richey said of the Hanban contract that it was "definitely one sided."

events.title: Regents decline to revisit Confucius contract, closing SGA debate
events.body: Richey told the senate the Board of Regents had decided at its Sept. 25 meeting not to revisit the contract for the Confucius Institute building, and said he wished to close SGA's debate on the matter. "Just to clarify, it's a done deal, the building will be built," he said. In the same report he told senators state appropriations had fallen from 47 percent of WKU's operating budget in 1998 to 18 percent for 2015-16.

events.title: SGA cabinet pulls 'Spirit Masters' from pub-naming ballot
events.body: The executive cabinet removed the name "Spirit Masters" from the Dub the Pub ballot after administrators said it demeaned WKU's student ambassador group, though the name was in second place at the time. Topper Tavern won with 480 of 2,132 votes cast. Senator Chase Coffey said Richey closed the issue without letting senators speak and objected that "Topped Off" had been left on the ballot.

events.title: Senate backs meningitis vaccine requirement for on-campus freshmen
events.body: Resolution 6-15-F, supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen living in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, passed unanimously. Bill 10-15-F amending the SGA bylaws also passed unanimously. Richey reported back from listening tours at the Glasgow, Owensboro and Elizabethtown/Fort Knox campuses, saying a full-time security officer was Glasgow's top priority.

events.title: Judicial Council strips funding from physics and art departments
events.body: The Judicial Council ruled Bills 8-15-F and 9-15-F unconstitutional under Bylaw 6.1, which stated SGA may allocate funds solely to students, voiding $1,500 for the physics department and up to $759 for the art department. Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell said money given to departments benefits faculty and staff as well as students. The council encouraged the student League of Sculptors to apply instead for $500 in organizational aid.

events.title: Judicial Council declines to censure senator over 'impeach Ransdell' sign; chief justice resigns
events.body: The Judicial Council voted unanimously not to censure Senator John Winstead, who had been investigated over a sign at the homecoming game and a Facebook image mocking President Gary Ransdell, finding his conduct protected by the First Amendment. Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell resigned effective the end of the semester. Winstead said the process was "fundamentally flawed" and objected to being investigated at all.

events.title: SGA refuses to enforce the campus smoking phaseout
events.body: After hearing from a University of Kentucky representative who explained UK pays ambassadors to enforce its tobacco ban and requires them to report violators, SGA declined to assemble the enforcement corps Ransdell's email had described. "SGA has no intention on actually being the group that enforces this," Richey said, adding that he personally disagreed with the ban but would adhere to it. The policy proceeded as voluntary compliance backed by signage.

events.title: Senate refuses to vote on Judicial Council's new election codes
events.body: The senate declined to vote on election codes drafted by the Judicial Council that would have cut senate campaign spending from $50 to $25 and limited candidates to three pieces of campaign material per building, placed only on bulletin boards. Richey, absent from the meeting, called the changes "too much red tape" and over-regulation. Chief Justice Amber Daniel scheduled a separate meeting for senators to propose changes.

events.title: Senate strips reparations language from presidential-qualities resolution
events.body: Resolution 2-16-S, outlining recommended qualities for WKU's tenth president, passed after amendment. A clause on the displaced Jonesville community originally asking the next president to "offer solutions for how reparations can be made" was debated, changed to "restitution," then removed entirely by majority vote. A sustainability clause seeking a zero-emissions campus was also softened to a goal of raising WKU's AASHE STARS rating.

events.title: Final meeting passes eSports, recycling and vegetarian dining resolutions
events.body: At its last meeting of the year the senate passed Resolution 3-16-S supporting recycling in the Downing Student Union, Garrett and Tower food courts, Resolution 4-16-S supporting creation of an eSports program and dedicated space, and Resolution 5-16-S supporting vegetarian options on the DSU meal plan. Bill 15-16-S allocated $600 to keep Helm-Cravens Library open until 2 a.m. during finals week. Nathan Cherry was elected speaker of the senate for 2016-17.

events.title: SGA paid half the fare for a Latino leadership keynote
events.body: On 15 September 2015 the senate unanimously passed Bill 4-15-F, allocating $200 from legislative discretionary funds for the seminar "Si, Se Puede: Leadership in the Latino Community." The money covered half the estimated travel costs of keynote speaker Johana Lopez, a WKU alumna and Houston-based leadership coach, with the Hilltopper Organization of Latin American Students covering the rest. The same meeting passed $1,200 for study away scholarships.
events.money: $200 toward the keynote speaker's travel; $1,200 in study away scholarships

src.label: Herald, 17 Sep 2015 - "SGA allocates funds to study away scholarships"

events.title: Planning began for SGA's fiftieth anniversary
events.body: President Jay Todd Richey told the Herald in October 2015 that SGA's fiftieth anniversary would fall in 2016 and that a gala was among the ideas being discussed, along with inviting alumni and former members back to see what had changed. No date had been fixed and Richey said the plans were still in the idea phase and would be opened to all members and interested students. SGA had last marked itself in 2006, for the fortieth.

src.label: Herald, 13 Oct 2015 - "SGA plans to celebrate 50th anniversary"

events.title: SGA budget fell by $19,500
events.body: SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the previous year, largely because a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut another $4,500 in reallocations. Organizational funding took the hardest hit, losing $9,000, and the Academic Affairs and Student Affairs scholarship pools each fell by more than $5,000. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss. The Herald noted WKU's SGA budget stood at $138,500 against the University of Louisville's $1.2 million.

events.title: Senate voted 21-4 to disapprove the Confucius Institute approval process
events.body: The senate passed Resolution 2-15-F by 21 votes to 4, disapproving of the nontransparent procedure by which the Model Confucius Institute building was authorized, after President Gary Ransdell signed the contract in China in December 2014 and the Board of Regents, including the student regent, voted on it more than a month later without full details disclosed. Several senators argued the institute was an asset to WKU and Bowling Green, while Campus Improvement Chairman Zachary Jones backed the resolution as an expression of student opinion. Richey wrote separately that the vote was not meant to set a precedent beyond ensuring the Board had full information, and that some senators had warned it would make "powerful enemies" for SGA.

src2.label: Herald, 24 Sep 2015, letter to the editor from the SGA president

events.title: Administration overrode the student vote on the Garrett pub name
events.body: Richey announced that administrators had renamed the future Garrett Conference Center pub Topper Grill and Pub. The Herald reported that the student body had voted for Topper Tavern in SGA's "Dub the Pub" contest and that the name previously settled on for the eatery was the compromise Topper Tavern and Grill. Richey said former Student Affairs vice president Howard Bailey told him he had made the decision and that President Ransdell wanted to downplay the alcohol theme; he called himself very disappointed and said it made SGA question how much the administration listens to students. The same meeting introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

events.title: Senate opposed the state tuition-freeze bill
events.body: The senate approved Resolution 2-16-S, opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75, which would have frozen resident tuition at 2015-16 levels for four years, after debate. Richey argued such freezes were dangerous risks that could wreck universities and cost students more in the long run. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, a loss of $1,301.27. Richey also told senators appointments should be more democratic, noting that he had appointed 42 percent of the sitting senate.

executive.note: Also served as student regent under the merged offices.

officers.note: Listed among non-voting officers in attendance at the 1 Dec 2015 executive cabinet meeting.

senate.note: At the 1 Dec 2015 executive cabinet meeting, Miles and Koehler disagreed with then-Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell's call for a separate Judicial Council adviser; Luttrell resigned two days later.

documents.title: Executive Cabinet meeting minutes, 1 December 2015
documents.summary: The Richey administration's own record of a fall 2015 cabinet meeting: the voting and non-voting officers then serving, a discussion of a possible independent Judicial Council adviser two days before Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell's resignation, and routine business including finals-week library-hours funding and an early suicide-awareness discussion.
