leaders.name: Jay Todd Richey
leaders.note: Re-elected. In office for Resolution 6-17-S, the reparations resolution, which passed 19-10-1 on 18 April 2017 and drew national coverage. Richey publicly framed it as a conversation starter; President Gary Ransdell stated within days that WKU would not adopt it.

sources.label: Bowling Green Daily News, Apr 2017 (archived copy)

profile: His re-election made him WKU SGA's first two-term president since 1988 and one of only three since 1974. Over his two terms he led the creation of three new committees, Sustainability, MyCampusToo and SAVES (Standing Against Violence and Ending Self-harm), revamped SGA's website, authored nine bills and resolutions, and represented students on the Board of Regents, the University Senate and the presidential search committee that chose WKU's 10th president. A Herald profile in March 2017 described a president who arrived late to office hours from overrun meetings, fielded budget questions and calls from the chief of police, and admitted he still struggled with low self-esteem.

In a farewell letter published as his term ended, Richey wrote that fighting for college affordability had been a personal priority: SGA rallied at the Kentucky Capitol and lobbied the General Assembly against university budget cuts, and he chaired the Board of Student Body Presidents of Kentucky. He cited expanded services for military and veteran students, the Rave Guardian safety app, WKU's first eSports program, an SGA Voter Empowerment Initiative that registered hundreds of voters, new SGA scholarships including one for students with disabilities, and helping select president Tim Caboni. His successor Andi Dahmer took the oath of office on May 2, 2017.

events.title: Resolution 6-17-S passes 19-10-1
events.body: Senators Andrea Ambam and Brian Anderson wrote a resolution supporting reparations for Black students, calling for full and free access to WKU for all Black people and asking for a task force on test-optional and geographically weighted admissions. Modelled on a resolution passed at Wisconsin-Madison earlier that year.

events.title: President Ransdell rejects the resolution
events.body: National wire coverage followed, along with a Tucker Carlson interview with Ambam and a wave of fabricated headlines claiming WKU had granted free tuition. Ransdell stated within days that it was not a university position. Both authors described it as a conversation starter.

events.title: Richey re-elected SGA president in high-turnout election
events.body: WKU students re-elected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president and elected Kate Hart as executive vice president in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history, with 2,442 voters. Richey defeated opponent Braxton Powell with 64 percent of the overall vote. Powell was elected a junior senator and his running mate Zach Jones a senior senator.

events.title: Senate rejected 2.0 GPA bill, backed housing diversity
events.body: SGA rejected a bill that would have let students vote to lower the organization's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0, a change supporters said would make the body more representative; a Twitter poll found 61 percent of respondents opposed it. The senate also approved a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to address the lack of diversity in on-campus housing under the university's 10-year housing plan.

events.title: SGA created Jonesville scholarship fund
events.body: The senate created a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the African American community founded by freed slaves in the 1870s that stood on land now occupied by Smith Stadium, Nick Denes Field and Downing Student Union until WKU bought and demolished it in the late 1960s. Senators debated whether the award should go only to African American students as repayment for Jonesville's condemnation or be opened to all minority students.

events.title: SGA backed prioritizing faculty raises over construction
events.body: The senate passed a resolution supporting future faculty salary increases, written to mirror a concurrent resolution headed to the Faculty Senate and proposed by Administrative Vice President Hannah Neeper and Chief of Staff James Line. The resolution urged that salary increases be prioritized over future construction or renovation projects, citing WKU's second-to-last ranking in faculty pay among its 19 benchmark institutions in 2015 and a survey in which 57 percent of faculty rated their morale as poor or very poor.

events.title: Andi Dahmer elected to succeed Richey
events.body: Louisville sophomore Andi Dahmer, a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was elected the next student body president, winning 930 of 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans's 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry won executive vice president and administrative vice president. Dahmer said she would start with legislation on study abroad affordability and sensitivity training to improve retention among marginalized groups.

events.title: Ransdell condemns racist incidents after notes, vandalism
events.body: In the weeks before, racist notes had been left in a WKU assistant dean's office and a racial slur was scratched into a student's car following a parking dispute. President Gary Ransdell called the acts "cowardly" and "heinous," said they did not reflect the university's values, and called for campus dialogue on intolerance.

events.title: Senators raise campus racism at first fall meeting
events.body: At the third meeting of the 15th Senate, student speakers Jeb Veeck, Francisco Serrano and Spencer Wells addressed the recent racist incidents on campus. Veeck suggested a Q&A session on the issue and Serrano urged senators to help end racism on campus.

events.title: Two SGA members resign amid racism complaint; investigation nullified
events.body: After Chief Justice Cody Cox told the Oct. 11 senate meeting he had received a complaint that several SGA members made racist remarks, senator Braxton Powell and justice John McKinney resigned the next morning, citing scheduling conflicts and personal reasons respectively; neither confirmed, denied, nor acknowledged any link between the resignations and the complaint. The Judicial Council's planned investigation was dropped because the students in question had already left SGA, and the organization never released the identities of the accused or the nature of the alleged remarks. President Richey and MyCampusToo chair Helen Vickrey issued a statement the next day condemning the alleged acts.

events.title: Student regent publishes dissent from Medical Center partnership
events.body: Jay Todd Richey, serving as student regent, wrote an open letter to students explaining his vote against the Board of Regents' 6-4-1 approval of a partnership with the Medical Center to construct a building housing an athletics practice facility and the Department of Physical Therapy. He argued the deal would tie WKU to a single health care provider for up to 99 years and place the university inside a long-running competition among Bowling Green providers. He wrote that although bound to uphold the board's decision, he believed it was a bad deal for WKU.

events.title: SGA raises its own student office workers to $10.10 an hour
events.body: Richey told the senate SGA office workers would be paid $10.10 an hour, saying the raise reflected the rising cost of tuition. "SGA is making a stand and saying that students deserve this wage," he said. Chief facilities officer Bryan Russell also briefed senators that Parking Structure 3 in the Creason lot would add more than 500 spaces, with construction running from September to August 2017.

events.title: Senate funds first disability scholarships after student testimony
events.body: Bill 4-16-F, creating scholarships for students with disabilities, passed unanimously after sophomore Brendan Ward told senators his ADHD and dyslexia had cost him merit scholarships and that he was at WKU "only by loans and the government." The bill drew $500 each from the football tabling and food lines of the SGA budget. Two other students, Cheyenne Mitchell and Francisco Serrano, addressed the senate about racist vandalism and discrimination on campus.

events.title: Senate seat left vacant all summer by an uncorrected election error
events.body: Speaker Nathan Cherry told the senate that eleven at-large seats should have been filled the previous spring but only ten were, leaving SGA one senator short through the summer. "I failed to catch that," Cherry said. Lucas Knight was selected to fill the seat, and Richey said he was exploring a hybrid arrangement letting students question anonymous presidential candidates online during the closed search.

events.title: SGA creates SAVES committee on sexual assault and suicide prevention
events.body: The senate created the Standing Against Violence and Ending Self-harm special committee to work on sexual assault prevention, suicide prevention and expanded mental health resources with the Counseling and Testing Center. Senator Francisco Serrano was named chair and described his own recent experience of having water thrown at him and racial slurs shouted while walking outside Downing Student Union. Freshman Ryan Linton told the senate WKU's harassment policy did not explicitly protect gender identity.

events.title: Senate rejects GPA change again, approves housing diversity resolution
events.body: A bill to let students vote on lowering SGA's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0 was rejected, with Senator Kaycee Gibson saying representatives "are expected to be elitist" and Public Relations Chair Alex Sergent saying "we're the cream of the crop." An SGA Twitter poll had found 61 percent of respondents opposed the change. The senate did approve a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to integrate honors and international students across Southwest and Northeast halls rather than segregating them.

events.title: Kentucky student body presidents demand restoration of the 'Powerball Promise'
events.body: Richey, as chair of the Board of Student Body Presidents of Kentucky, co-signed a published letter with the student presidents of nine other Kentucky institutions calling on Gov. Matt Bevin and the legislature to stop diverting lottery money from need-based College Access Program and Kentucky Tuition Grant aid. The letter cited Kentucky Center for Economic Policy figures that underfunding had limited scholarships for 15,000 to 20,000 qualifying students in 2016. It named Bevin's veto of House Bill 10 as having blocked restoration of the funding.

events.title: SGA launches SafeWalk and makes diversity and sustainability committees permanent
events.body: The senate approved bills making the Sustainability and MyCampusToo committees permanent standing committees under the constitution, and renamed MyCampusToo the Committee for Diversity and Inclusion after some found the old name "offensive and not inclusive." SGA also launched SafeWalk, a call line pairing students who felt unsafe with student escorts, and extended office hours so students had a place to go. Resolutions supporting an elevator in Gordon Wilson Hall and removal of styrofoam from WKU dining also passed.

events.title: Senate creates Jonesville Memorial Scholarship after debate over eligibility
events.body: SGA allocated $750, matched by $100 from the Center for Citizenship and Social Justice, for a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the Black community WKU bought and displaced in the late 1960s for under $200,000. Senators debated opening it to all minority students, but the bill passed in its original form restricting it to first-year African American students from Warren County or Bowling Green schools. Senator Dillon McCormick called it "a kind of symbolic gesture to atone for the wrong that we did."

events.title: Safe Ride bus service cut on Thursdays as ridership collapses
events.body: SGA ended Thursday operation of its Safe Ride Purple Line after ridership fell to about one rider per hour, against twenty per hour on Saturdays. Total ridership had dropped from roughly 5,000 in fall 2015 to nearly 1,500 in fall 2016, which Richey attributed to Uber's arrival in Bowling Green. He said the service would not be discontinued entirely without a replacement.

events.title: SGA creates regional ambassadors, requires senator office hours, raises campaign spending caps
events.body: The senate passed a bill creating non-voting regional ambassador positions for each regional campus and designating one senator as a South Campus liaison, and a second bill requiring every senator to keep one office hour per week. Speaker Nathan Cherry said the office-hour requirement would make senators feel more connected and more willing to write legislation. Senators also approved revised election codes raising campaign spending allowances, with presidential candidates permitted $300.

events.title: Executive Council vetoes a unanimously passed resolution; author resigns
events.body: Senator Chase Coffey's resolution allowing former senators who resigned in good standing to attend SGA's end-of-year banquet passed the senate unanimously, then was vetoed by the Executive Council, which held it unconstitutional. Coffey resigned the same night over a conflict with a night class. The meeting also opened applications for the Jonesville Memorial Scholarship and SGA's first two $500 scholarships for students with disabilities.

events.title: Housing office omits SGA's diversity resolution from its 10-year plan
events.body: Housing and Residence Life's 10-year plan made Southwest Hall honors housing in fall 2017 and Northeast Hall international housing in fall 2018, with no mention of the integration SGA had endorsed 27-1 the previous October. Senator Jody Dahmer said the resolution was deliberately written without detail so HRL could work out specifics. An SGA Twitter poll had found about 83 percent of respondents supported merging the two populations.

events.title: SGA votes 17-9 to require a nondiscrimination pledge before funding student groups
events.body: Bill 20-17-S, requiring student organizations to reaffirm a nondiscrimination statement including gender identity before receiving SGA organizational aid, passed 17-9-1. It was written in response to Kentucky Senate Bill 17, which let student groups exclude members over political or religious views. Richey said "SGA is not going to subsidize discrimination," while Senator Zach Jones argued the bill hampered diversity of opinion.

events.title: GPA requirement lowered to 2.0 by exactly the required margin
events.body: After failing twice in the previous year, a bill lowering SGA's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0 passed 24-7, receiving exactly the 24 votes needed from the 36-member senate, and went to the student body for ratification. Senator Brian Anderson called the opposing argument "paternalism that I don't think this organization should stand for." A separate bill to move committee chair appointments from the president to the speaker of the senate failed.

events.title: Judicial Council exemptions turn the presidential race into a three-way contest
events.body: The Judicial Council granted constitutional exemptions under Article 2.2.5 to Lily Nellans and Kenan Mujkanovic, both of whom had served less than one semester, allowing them to run against Andi Dahmer for president. A Herald editorial argued the rulings set a precedent letting candidates with no SGA experience seek the presidency and the accompanying seat on the Board of Regents. Only Dahmer had been eligible under the constitution as written.

events.title: Dahmer elected; all six referendums pass
events.body: Andi Dahmer won the presidency with 930 of 1,579 votes cast, ahead of Kenan Mujkanovic at 305 and Lily Nellans at 212, with Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry elected to the vice presidencies. Students ratified all six referendums, making the SAVES, MyCampusToo and Sustainability committees permanent, lowering the GPA requirement to 2.0, creating regional campus ambassadors and requiring more accessible executive discretionary spending reports.

events.title: Senate unanimously asks WKU police to take diversity and sexual assault training
events.body: A resolution written by Francisco Serrano and Senator Brian Anderson after an increase in racially motivated incidents passed unanimously, asking that all WKU Police officers and staff receive diversity, hate crime and sexual assault training. Serrano said it was not an attack on the department. A second unanimous resolution asked that outdoor events booked through Campus and Community Events be listed on WKU's online calendar, written after graphic genocide-themed demonstrations in Centennial Mall.

events.title: SGA co-sponsored the International Diplomats' Home Away From Home
events.body: Bill 7-16-F allocated $250 from senate discretionary funding to International Enrollment Management for the International Diplomats' charity event Home Away From Home, held on 29 September 2016 at the Honors College and International Center. The event was built so international students could meet American students and Bowling Green organisations, with all proceeds going to the International Center of Kentucky and a small prize for whoever donated most. The bill passed unanimously on 27 September.

src.label: SGA Bill 7-16-F, Funding for the International Diplomats Event "Home Away From Home"

events.title: Earn-A-Computer gave away its first desktop
events.body: SGA presented the first computer under its Earn-A-Computer programme on 4 October 2016, an iMac awarded free to Nashville junior Bobby Scott after he completed 35 hours of community service. Scott worked with the Intercultural Engagement Center and with children at Warren Elementary School. A computer information technology major whose own machine had recently died, he told the senate he had badly needed it. SGA ran the programme with WKU Resource Conservation.

src.label: Herald, 10 Oct 2016 - "SGA awards first desktop in computer program"

events.title: Ride To Vote drove students to the polls
events.body: SGA ran a Ride To Vote service on election day, 8 November 2016, driving any WKU student without transport to and from the polling stations. The programme was discussed at the senate meeting of 1 November alongside the Board of Student Body Presidents' letter to Governor Matt Bevin asking that lottery money be kept in need-based student financial aid.

src.label: Herald, 2 Nov 2016 - "SGA discusses Ride To Vote, financial aid"

events.title: SGA paid to keep the library open later during finals
events.body: Bill 19-16-F allocated $1,200 from legislative discretionary funding to extend Helm-Cravens Library's hours during finals week in autumn 2016 and spring 2017, keeping it open until 2 a.m. Sunday through Thursday instead of midnight. The bill recorded that SGA had a standing tradition of paying for extended library hours each year, and that the library's signage would credit the sponsorship. It passed on 15 November 2016.

src.label: SGA Bill 19-16-F, Funding for Extended Library Hours

events.title: Love Has No Borders answered the travel ban
events.body: Bill 6-17-S allocated $100 for Love Has No Borders, held at the Faculty House on 10 February 2017 and co-sponsored with the International Diplomats, to celebrate WKU's international students after the executive order restricting entry from seven countries. The bill noted that 22 WKU students came from the affected countries and had asked for an event showing support from the student body. A further $100 came from executive discretionary funding and $138 from the public relations budget.
events.money: $100 from senate discretionary, plus $100 executive and $138 public relations

src.label: SGA Bill 6-17-S, Funding for the SGA and International Diplomats Event "Love Has No Borders"

events.title: Power UP political forum funded for Black History Month
events.body: Bill 5-17-S passed 30-0 on 14 February 2017, allocating $200 to the Intercultural Student Engagement Center for the Power UP Political Forum, a non-partisan student forum held on 20 February in DSU 2004 from 5:30 to 7 p.m. Planned topics included the origins of Black History Month, constitutional free speech guarantees and the demographic makeup of American legislatures. The money paid for refreshments and an honorarium for a guest speaker.
events.money: $200, covering refreshments and a speaker honorarium

src.label: SGA Bill 5-17-S, Funding for the Power UP Political Forum

events.title: Jonesville and disability scholarships opened for applications
events.body: SGA said on 21 February 2017 that applications for the Jonesville Memorial Scholarship and the Students with Disabilities Scholarship would go on its website within days. The Jonesville award, approved the previous autumn, totalled $850 and was funded with the Center for Citizenship and Social Justice for first-year African American students from the Warren County or Bowling Green school systems. It memorialised Jonesville, the Black community WKU displaced when it bought the land to expand in the late 1960s.

src.label: Herald, 22 Feb 2017 - "SGA offers new scholarships for marginalized groups"

events.title: Big Red Bikes kept running on SGA money
events.body: The senate approved funding on 28 February 2017 for the Big Red Bikes free bicycle-lending programme and for the Community Farmers Market Double Dollars scheme. The bill gave Big Red Bikes just over $800 for brake pads, chains and locks after the Paula Nye Memorial Education Grant that had supported it ran out. Mechanic Colton Turley said the programme had 40 usable bicycles with 35 already rented out, 15 needing repair and 70 more donated but not yet ready.

events.title: Textbooks for Troops got $300 from the senate
events.body: Bill 15-17-S passed 29-0-1 on 21 March 2017, allocating $300 to WKU Military Student Services for its Textbooks for Troops programme, half from senate and half from executive discretionary funding. The programme, set up in 2011 for unemployed National Guard soldiers, lent textbooks for a full semester to military students, veterans and dependants not already receiving a book stipend. Military Student Services reported that more than 171 students had been helped in spring 2017 alone.

events.title: Miss World Fest WKU Pageant funded with $550
events.body: Bill 17-17-S passed 25-4 on 28 March 2017, allocating $550 from senate discretionary funding for the Miss World Fest WKU Pageant on 20 April. The pageant was added to WKU's World Fest by CISO with the International Student Office and MyCampusToo to promote cultural awareness and let international students present their own cultures. The money covered promotional materials, posters, tiaras and sashes.

src.label: SGA Bill 17-17-S, Funding for the Miss World Fest WKU Pageant

events.title: SGA co-sponsored Take Back the Night
events.body: Bill 23-17-S passed 27-3 on 4 April 2017, allocating $250 to the WKU Counseling and Testing Center to co-sponsor Take Back the Night. The event was held on 20 April at 6 p.m. at First Christian Church and consisted of a march through downtown Bowling Green followed by a candlelight vigil for survivors of sexual assault. The bill tied the sponsorship to SGA's creation of the SAVES committee.

committees.note: By mid-October 2016 Helen Vickrey was reported as MyCampusToo committee chair; the record does not show when or why the chair changed.

senate.note: This was the 15th Senate. Chief Justice of the Judicial Council was Cody Cox; Associate Chief Justice was Annalicia Carlson.

leaders.name: Andi Dahmer
leaders.note: Took office alongside incoming university president Timothy Caboni, who began 1 July 2017.

Bowling Green Daily News, 3 Feb 2024, "WKU, ex-SGA president settle lawsuit"

profile: Andi Dahmer, a Louisville sophomore who had served as a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was announced as the next student body president shortly after midnight on April 19, 2017, winning 930 of the 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans' 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry were elected executive vice president and administrative vice president, and Dahmer entered office already drafting legislation aimed at improving retention, making study abroad more affordable and supporting sensitivity training.

Her year in office was marked by internal division. The senate saw longer debates, more than 15 proposed constitutional amendments compared with about 10 the year before, and an emergency Judicial Council meeting on Jan. 29, with contention peaking around the DACA debates of October and November 2017, when the senate failed a clean DREAM Act resolution before passing a resolution supporting DACA students. Dahmer said the year had become "almost toxic in nature" and blamed partisan ideologies brought into what was supposed to be a nonpartisan organization.

In April 2018 Dahmer told the Herald she had endured months of harassment as president and student regent, including senators cursing at her in the SGA office, a group message thread of eight people called the "Justice Friends" that wished her physical harm, and a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 that prompted a police report. Of the note she said, "That's when I really started fearing for my life on this campus." Her residence hall director reported her case to the Title IX office, which found it did not meet the legal standard for harassment; it was processed instead through the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators, and she did not seek reelection.

In 2018 Dahmer, whose full name is Loandria "Andi" Dahmer, sued WKU, university president Timothy Caboni, director of student activities Charley Pride and assistant general counsel and Title IX coordinator Andrea Anderson, alleging sex-based discrimination and harassment by fellow SGA members, negligence by the university in responding to it, and that Caboni retaliated against her by declining to write a letter of recommendation for a Rhodes Scholarship application. U.S. District Judge David Hale granted the defendants summary judgment in March 2021, finding WKU had not been deliberately indifferent and that the incidents were not severe enough to constitute actionable harassment; the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals partially revived the case in 2022, directing the district court to consider whether student-on-student harassment had occurred before February 2018. The parties settled in January 2024, with WKU's insurance carrier paying Dahmer $10,000 and the university's attorney describing the payment as nominal and made without any admission of wrongdoing.

events.title: First senate meeting passes constitutional amendments
events.body: SGA held its first senate meeting of the year and approved three of five proposed constitutional amendment bills, which then went to the student body for a vote in the fall elections. The passed bills added constitutional review duties to the Judicial Council, made the chief justice backup speaker of the senate, and required senators to post one office hour per week. Senators also debated Bill 5-17-F, which proposed limiting the legislative powers of the executive branch.

events.title: Dahmer condemned a blackface Halloween incident at senate meeting
events.body: President Andi Dahmer opened the eighth meeting of the Senate by telling members that a student had worn blackface to a Halloween party the previous weekend and that it was not acceptable. She also hosted student body presidents from other Kentucky universities on campus that weekend and reminded senators that Herald reporters were allowed into all university committee meetings.

events.title: SGA members rally in Frankfort for higher education
events.body: About 20 WKU SGA members joined roughly 100 students from Kentucky's public universities at the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents' annual Rally for Higher Education on the Capitol steps in Frankfort on Feb. 6. Dahmer said the board of student body presidents had been working consistently since August to plan the rally.

events.title: LGBTQ activists address senate after senator's remarks
events.body: Several LGBTQ student activists spoke to the senate on April 3 after Senator Dallas McKinney had cited the Bible on March 27, reading verses saying the "wicked" deserved death, as his reason for voting against Bill 13-18-S, which funded $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ graduates. The bill passed in the senate, and speakers including SGA member Brigid Stakelum and Diversity and Inclusion Committee Chair Mark Clark called the remarks dehumanizing and discriminatory.

events.title: Mayer wins presidency after disqualification reversed
events.body: Stephen Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent, with Garrett Edmonds as executive vice president and Harper Anderson as administrative vice president. Their MEA ticket had been disqualified on April 16 after a complaint over a Pepe the Frog meme in a campaign chalk drawing, but the Judicial Council reversed the disqualification to a suspension before results were announced. Mayer won 35 percent of the 2,378 votes cast in the presidential race, ahead of Conner Hounshell with 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic with 32 percent.

events.title: Dahmer details months of harassment
events.body: In a Herald investigation, Dahmer said members of SGA had cursed at her, called her derogatory names and exchanged group messages in a GroupMe called the "Justice Friends" wishing her harm over the fall and spring semesters, and that a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 led her to file a WKU police report and avoid her residence hall for two weeks. Her case was reported to WKU's Title IX office, which told her the conduct did not meet the legal standard for harassment, and it was processed instead by the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators.

events.title: Judicial Council censured PR committee chair over election-discrepancy complaint
events.body: At an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council took up a complaint public relations committee chair Will Hurst had raised at the Jan. 23 senate meeting, alleging the executive board failed its constitutional duty to advertise the fall election and citing a discrepancy in vote totals between constitutional amendments that passed and failed. The council found the executive board had complied with the constitution and issued a censure against Hurst; Dahmer said she was pleased the council had upheld the board's conduct. The censure was confirmed at the Feb. 6 senate meeting.

events.title: Dahmer joined national solidarity letter after Charlottesville
events.body: President Andi Dahmer was one of more than 120 college student body presidents nationwide who signed an open letter backing the University of Virginia after the violent Charlottesville protests, and said developing campus-wide "cultural competency training" was a goal for the semester.

events.title: Senate backed LGBTQ health curriculum, chair swap on Diversity committee
events.body: The senate unanimously passed a resolution supporting integrated LGBTQ health curriculum in WKU's medical education programs, co-authored by diversity and inclusion chair Mark Clark, chief of staff Conner Hounshell and administrative vice president Kara Lowry. Clark was approved as the committee's new chair after Corey Newsome stepped down over scheduling conflicts.

events.title: Dahmer announced she would not seek reelection
events.body: Citing tension in the senate that she called "almost toxic in nature" and that she attributed to partisan ideology in a body meant to be nonpartisan, Dahmer said in a Facebook post she would not run again and endorsed Conner Hounshell for president alongside Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry, seeking reelection to their executive vice president and administrative vice president seats.

events.title: Caboni announced Title IX review after Dahmer harassment report
events.body: University president Timothy Caboni said he would convene a faculty-staff-student committee, co-chaired by sociology professor Lauren McClain and counseling official Karl Laves, to review WKU's Title IX, Equal Employment Opportunity and Office of Student Conduct processes following the Herald's report on the harassment Dahmer said she experienced. President-elect Stephen Mayer called Dahmer "a super strong woman" and said he did not stand for harassment or sexual assault.

events.title: Senate rejects bid to strip the executive branch of legislative power
events.body: At the first meeting of the year the senate considered five proposed constitutional amendments. Bill 5-17-F, written by Public Relations Chair William Hurst to bar the executive branch from writing legislation, failed 4-8 after Hurst argued it "limited the chances" for senators to gain drafting experience. Bills adding constitutional review duties to the Judicial Council, making the chief justice acting speaker, and requiring one office hour per week from senators all passed.

events.title: SGA funds legal observer training for student demonstrators
events.body: Bill 3-17-F allocated $200 from senate discretionary funds to facilitate legal observer training run in partnership with the Nashville chapter of the National Lawyers Guild, covering flyers, food and a gift for the trainers. Senator Dylan McCormick told the senate that "in this political climate" it helped to have people with those skills on hand. The bill was approved unanimously.

events.title: Senate votes 12-2 to sponsor Bowling Green's first Pride festival
events.body: Bill 9-17-F committed $250 from senate discretionary funds, matched by $250 from the executive budget, to make SGA a green sponsor of the inaugural Bowling Green Pride Festival hosted by BG Fairness. Senator Jordan Tackett questioned whether SGA was ready to face backlash, while Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell called the event "a celebration of identity." Senator Lucas Knight tied the bill to the city commission's failure to pass a Fairness Ordinance.

events.title: Resolution backing a clean DREAM Act fails 12-17
events.body: Resolution 2-17-F, urging Congress to pass a clean DREAM Act after DACA was rescinded, failed with 12 votes in favor and 17 opposed. Senator Alex Sergent said it was not the university's place to "put our political hat in a ring," and William Hurst said "we serve the majority." Legislative Research Chair Lily Nellans countered that senators are meant to vote for their constituents' interests, "which oftentimes means protecting marginalized minority communities."

events.title: Senate backs a Bowling Green Fairness Ordinance 34-2
events.body: Resolution 7-17-F, standing with those asking the Bowling Green City Commission to pass a Fairness Ordinance, passed 34-2. Bill 32-17-F, which would have removed the first reading requirement to speed up legislation, failed for lack of a motion to approve. A resolution supporting a recycling program for Greek housing passed unanimously, and Bill 34-17-F funded posters for a series collecting sexual assault survivors' stories.

events.title: Senate postpones an appointment over fall election irregularities
events.body: The senate postponed confirming Stephen Mayer to a vacant seat after William Hurst objected that the executive board had failed its constitutional duty to advertise the referendum and called the nomination of "another fraternity man" hypocritical given the board's stated concern about Greek over-representation. Senator Alex Sergent said many senators did not feel confident in "the results of such an odd election," while stressing his objection was not to Mayer personally.

events.title: Judicial Council holds emergency meeting on whether the fall referendum was valid
events.body: The Judicial Council convened an emergency meeting on whether Director of Public Relations Amy Wyer had violated constitutional sections 2.7.3 and 2.7.5 by not advertising the fall referendum. Wyer argued a referendum is not an election and that the office had never advertised referendums; Hurst pointed to a discrepancy between the 119 votes on the amendment that failed and the 117 and 116 on those that passed. Emily Houston countered that if the duty applied, the whole public relations committee had failed it equally.

events.title: Senate unanimously backs LGBTQ content in medical education curriculum
events.body: A resolution supporting integrated medical education curriculum on lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender health passed unanimously, citing health disparities arising from discrimination and inadequate provider knowledge. It was co-authored by Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark, Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell and Administrative Vice President Kara Lowry. Clark was also confirmed as Diversity and Inclusion chair after Corey Newsome stepped down.

events.title: SGA opposes Aramark dining fee rising to $350; new senate seats bill fails 14-18
events.body: Resolution 3-18-S passed unanimously, supporting renegotiation of the 20-year Aramark contract signed by Ransdell in March 2017, under which the per-semester dining fee for full-time students not on a meal plan would climb from $75 to $150, then $300, then $350, adding up to $2,800 over four years. Dahmer said the contract was never brought to SGA or the full Board of Regents. A separate bill replacing at-large and graduate seats with first-generation, transfer, non-traditional and ISEC senators failed 14-18 with one abstention.

events.title: SGA funds a $1,200 first-generation student scholarship
events.body: Bill 7-18-S passed unanimously, allocating $1,200 to create a scholarship for full-time students whose parents hold no bachelor's degree and who show significant financial need. Co-authors Senator Dallas McKinney and student Olivia Parker were both first-generation students. SGA members and the bill's authors were made ineligible to apply.

events.title: Lavender Graduation funding passes 28-5 over an unexplained objection
events.body: Bill 13-18-S allocated $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ and ally graduates, passing 28-5. Senator Dallas McKinney spoke against it without giving his reasoning. The same meeting saw Public Relations Chair Will Hurst absent and his seat occupied by vice chair Alex Sergent; asked whether Hurst had been removed, Dahmer said "nothing is official."

events.title: Senator cites Bible verses to explain vote against LGBTQ funding
events.body: Senator Dallas McKinney told the senate he had voted against the Lavender Graduation stoles because of "a certain interpretation of the King James Bible," reading verses from Romans; Queer Student Union President Jeremy McFarland walked out during the speech. Senators Noah Moore and Olivia Simpson gave speeches condemning voting on WKU's interests from scripture. A bill to move committee chair appointments to the speaker failed 26-2, with Speaker Ryan Richardson saying "I 100 percent do not support this bill."

events.title: Herald documents a year of escalating internal conflict in SGA
events.body: The Herald reported more than 15 proposed constitutional amendments during 2017-18 against about 10 the prior year, alongside longer debates, an emergency judicial council meeting and a walkout by former Public Relations Chair Will Hurst. Dahmer said the year "has become almost toxic in nature" and attributed it to partisan ideology entering a nonpartisan body. Senator Alex Sergent disagreed that the friction was harmful, comparing it to a storm.

events.title: Dahmer declines to seek a second term
events.body: Andi Dahmer announced on Facebook that she would not run for re-election as student body president and student regent, and endorsed Conner Hounshell, Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry for the executive board. The announcement followed Herald reporting on months of internal conflict in the senate. Election applications closed the same day, with voting set for April 16 and 17.

events.title: Senate votes 28-2 for LGBTQ-friendly housing application questions
events.body: A resolution asked Housing and Residence Life to make the sexual orientation and gender identity question optional on housing applications and to add a mandatory question asking whether an applicant is comfortable rooming with an LGBTQ student. Co-author Noah Moore said it would also serve students uncomfortable with an LGBTQ roommate, and noted WKU stood at 2 out of 5 on the Campus Pride Index. The senate also unanimously renamed the ESL international student senator seat to international student senator.

events.title: Judicial Council disqualifies two campaigns mid-election over a Pepe the Frog meme
events.body: In an emergency meeting the Judicial Council disqualified the Mayer-Edmonds-Anderson presidential ticket and senate candidate Anna McAvoy for using a Pepe the Frog image in campaign chalkings, finding a violation of election code 3.4.10.1, and suspended Kenan Mujkanovic's campaign for a separate violation. Chief Justice Annalicia Carlson said Garrett Edmonds had been told the image was a hate symbol and chose not to remove it. The MEA campaign called it a "secret meeting"; Carlson said it had been advertised to those involved.

events.title: Outgoing executives describe the year as 'absolute hell'
events.body: In their final officer reports, Executive Vice President Savannah Molyneaux called the year "awful" and an "absolute hell" and said sexism and misogyny persisted in the senate, citing the threatening note left on Dahmer's car and derogatory names used in the SGA offices. She also denied the board opposed Greek life, noting she was president of Sigma Kappa. Director of Public Relations Amy Wyer disclosed that she had become "a statistic, a victim and a survivor" during the year.

events.title: SGA paid for legal observer training with the National Lawyers Guild
events.body: Bill 3-17-F allocated $200 from senate discretionary funding for a Legal Observer Training event on 19 October 2017 in DSU 3024, run in partnership with the Nashville chapter of the National Lawyers Guild. The training was free to students and qualified them to serve as legal observers in Kentucky and across the United States. The bill passed on first reading on 28 August 2017.

src.label: SGA Bill 3-17-F, Funding for the SGA event "Legal Observer Training"

events.title: Thirty dollars of chalk for Mission: Thank You Veterans
events.body: Bill 17-17-F allocated $30 from senate discretionary funding to promote and stage Mission: Thank You Veterans on 9 November 2017 at 8 p.m. The WKU College Republicans and the WKU Young Democrats jointly wrote messages of support to veterans in chalk across campus, and the money bought the chalk. It is among the smallest event allocations SGA has recorded.

src.label: SGA Bill 17-17-F, Funding for the event Mission: Thank You Veterans

events.title: DACA Day of Action funded at $100
events.body: The senate unanimously approved Bill 21-17-F on 31 October 2017, giving $100 for a DACA Day of Action hosted by the Hilltopper Organization of Latin American Students with the Center for Citizenship and Social Justice. The all-day event had students write to legislators urging passage of a clean DREAM Act, and the money bought paper, pens, pencils, food, drinks and posters. Bowling Green junior Francisco Serrano co-authored it with President Andi Dahmer.

src.label: Herald, 1 Nov 2017 - "SGA funds 'Day of Action' to engage students with legislation"

events.title: The No Shave November beard contest flopped
events.body: SGA launched its first No Shave November beard-growing contest in 2017 to raise money for cancer prevention, funded by a sustainability committee bill passed on 26 September. Sustainability chair Ian Hamilton, who had taken part in the observance himself, said participants would donate what they saved by not buying shaving supplies. Entries were low, and Hamilton said SGA needed more discussion about what the month was for and how the effort could actually help people with cancer.

src.label: Herald, 9 Nov 2017 - "SGA hosts beard contest, raises money for cancer"

events.title: SGA flew in a producer for a Karenni refugee documentary
events.body: Bill 28-17-F passed on 14 November 2017, allocating $350 from senate discretionary funds toward the travel costs of executive producer Ansley Sawyer for a screening of the short documentary "Like We Don't Exist," about Karenni refugees from Burma. No Lost Generation WKU co-sponsored the 16 November showing, followed by a panel with Sawyer, members of the Karenni community and WKU film professor Ted Hovet. Sawyer travelled from California for the screening and a second showing at Warren Central High School two days later.

src.label: SGA Bill 28-17-F, Funding for the Showing of the Refugee Documentary "Like We Don't Exist"

events.title: Counselling voucher programme covered the registration fee
events.body: Bill 1-18-S allocated $500 from senate discretionary funds to create a voucher programme with the Counseling and Testing Center, providing 25 vouchers covering the centre's one-time $20 registration fee. That fee bought a student unlimited counselling sessions for as long as they attended WKU, and the bill argued that some students could not afford even the $20 to get in the door. It had its second reading on 30 January 2018.

src.label: SGA Bill 1-18-S, Funding for a Counseling and Testing Center Voucher Program

events.title: SGA's sustainability committee ran a spring film series
events.body: Bill 4-18-S allocated $50 from senate discretionary funding to promote the 2018 Spring Movie Series run by the SGA Sustainability Committee. Three films were scheduled at 5:30 p.m.: "The Dark Side of Chocolate" on 22 February, "Chasing Coral" on 22 March and "Bag It" on 19 April, the night of the Earth Day Festival. The money paid for posters and popcorn.

src.label: SGA Bill 4-18-S, Funding for the 2018 Spring Movie Series

events.title: Earth Day Festival with the Redshirts and the Treblemakers
events.body: Bill 10-18-S allocated $50 from senate discretionary funding to promote the 2018 Earth Day Festival, which the SGA Sustainability Committee held on 19 April from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Local vendors were booked and the entertainment was WKU's own a cappella groups, the Redshirts and the Treblemakers. The bill described the festival as the culmination of the committee's year.

src.label: SGA Bill 10-18-S, Funding for the 2018 Earth Day Festival

events.title: First Campus Safety Panel replaced the safety walk
events.body: SGA held its first Campus Safety Panel on the second floor of Downing Student Union on 28 February 2018, with campus officials taking questions from students. Campus improvements chair Garrett Edmonds said he had proposed a panel because it had been too cold to hold a safety walk since he took office. Parking director Jennifer Tougas was among the panelists; President Andi Dahmer asked what could be done about hate crimes on campus, and Chief Diversity Officer Lynne Holland answered that students had to hold each other accountable.

src.label: Herald, 1 Mar 2018 - "SGA hosts panel to discuss campus safety"

events.title: First women in leadership forum drew about twenty people
events.body: SGA held its first forum on women in leadership on the evening of 19 March 2018. The panel was Ogden College dean Cheryl Stevens, history professor Patti Minter, faculty regent and former provost Barbara Burch, and Educational Talent Search director Martha Sales, and about 20 students and Bowling Green residents attended. Minter described the psychic energy it took to deal with assumptions about female professors day in and day out. The idea came from the women on SGA's executive board, including Andi Dahmer, Savannah Molyneaux, Kara Lowry and Amy Wyer.

src.label: Herald, 20 Mar 2018 - "SGA hosts first women in leadership forum"

events.title: Holi Festival on South Lawn funded at $900
events.body: Bill 14-18-S allocated $450 from senate discretionary funding, matched by $450 from executive discretionary, to buy materials for the WKU Indian Student Association's Holi Festival on South Lawn on 25 March 2018. The money paid for colours, water bottles, tables and chairs, and SGA's name and logo appeared on the promotional material. The bill described Holi as the first spring festival celebrated in India.

src.label: SGA Bill 14-18-S, Funding for the WKU Indian Student Association Holi Festival

events.title: SGA bought the stoles for Lavender Graduation
events.body: Bill 13-18-S allocated $250 from senate discretionary funding, matched by $250 from executive discretionary, to buy stoles for the Lavender Graduation held on 8 May 2018 at the Augenstein Alumni Center. The ceremony recognised LGBTQ and ally graduates, and SGA's name and logo appeared on the programme. The measure had passed the senate 28-5 the previous day over an objection its author declined to explain.

events.title: SGA funds Hidden Hacks of the Hill
events.body: SGA passed Bill 20-17-F at its meeting on 31 October 2017, approving $200 for fliers and refreshments for Hidden Hacks on the Hill, an event set for 14 November in DSU Nite Class to help minority and underrepresented students find campus resources. The Herald reported that WKU hosted it that Tuesday morning in Downing Student Union, with the Writing Center, the Counseling and Testing Center and the WKU Food Pantry represented, and that SGA senator Divya Gangavelli spoke on the White, Red and Purple bus lines and on riding the Grise Hall lift to the top of the Hill.

events.title: Narrower DACA solidarity resolution passed 32-1
events.body: At its 7 November meeting the senate passed, by 32 votes to 1, a resolution co-authored by President Andi Dahmer and former senator Francisco Serrano standing in solidarity with WKU students who were DACA recipients. It was a revision of the clean DREAM Act resolution rejected the previous week, reframed to address only the WKU student community rather than call on legislators, which Dahmer said kept it within "a jurisdiction that we do have." Dahmer noted WKU was one of the last schools in Kentucky to pass a measure of this kind. The same meeting unanimously funded the Go With the Flow program, allocating over $580 for free menstrual products in five campus buildings.

events.title: Senate voted 29-1 for a required sexual assault course in the Colonnade
events.body: Resolution 1-17-F, supporting the addition of a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to Colonnade requirements for first-year students, passed 29-1 with two abstentions at the Tuesday night meeting. It was co-authored by public relations chair William Hurst, S.A.V.E.S. chair Ashlyn Jones and three other members, and argued that existing options such as HAVEN and Green Dot carried no penalty for skipping them. Hurst said a student could pass four years at WKU without any sexual assault training, calling that "a disgrace, to say the least." Senator Alex Sergent described the resolution as closing holes in an existing net rather than adding a graduation hurdle, and the same meeting funded a No-Shave November beard contest and fixed the timing of constitutional-amendment elections in the bylaws.
