leaders.name: Stephen Mayer
leaders.note: Confirmed by an independent WKU record outside the plaque: the University Senate's Nov. 15, 2018 meeting agenda lists him under reports as "SGA President: Stephen Mayer."

sources.label: WKU University Senate meeting agenda, 15 Nov 2018

profile: Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent in April 2018 on the MEA ticket with Garrett Edmonds and Harper Anderson, taking 35 percent of 2,378 presidential votes against Conner Hounshell's 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic's 32 percent; 2,447 students voted overall. His ticket won only after the Judicial Council reversed a disqualification it had imposed days before the election over the campaign's use of a Pepe the Frog meme chalked on campus sidewalks, downgrading the penalty to a campaign suspension.

A biology and chemistry double major who had served three semesters as a senator and studied at Harlaxton College, Mayer opened his term in September 2018 promising greater transparency from both the Board of Regents and SGA, and required senators to log a weekly office hour. As student regent he was an outspoken critic of WKU's fee structure, especially the $450 online academic fee, and opposed that year's 4 percent tuition increase, saying he did not see the need to put the financial burden "on the students' backs."

events.title: Senate rejected first Judicial Council nominee of the term
events.body: The senate voted 8-7-1 against confirming Wood Brown, a Pike fraternity member and law clerk, as associate justice of the Judicial Council, after Mayer said his constitutional duty required him to appoint whom he judged best despite recusing himself from the interview process; senators argued the Judicial Council's own top-ranked applicant, not Brown, should have been chosen. Mayer's next nominee, Alex Rivera, was confirmed the following week.

events.title: Academic and Student Affairs directorship filled after two failed tries
events.body: The senate confirmed Aubrey Kelly as Director of Academic and Student Affairs 24-3-4, three weeks into the term. Initial nominee Ashley Cox was not confirmed at the first meeting after senators questioned her committee attendance, then withdrew when a family member was hospitalized; her replacement, Anna McAvoy, failed confirmation 6-9-1 on Sept. 11 after a senator raised concerns about her scholarship-grading experience.

events.title: First Year Village housing plan presented to SGA
events.body: Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds presented plans for a freshman First Year Village of two new pod-style residence halls at the bottom of the Hill, replacing Bemis Lawrence and Barnes-Campbell halls on the site of the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot. The senate also approved Bill 6-18-F, funding a sustainability film festival, by a 21-4 vote with one abstention.

events.title: SGA created a first-generation student scholarship
events.body: The senate passed a bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr creating a recurring $2,000 scholarship for first-generation college students, approved 31-1. It also passed organizational aid Bill 11-18-F, sending $1,400 to Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club, and allocated $100 to advertise the Campus Safety Walk.

events.title: Contested appointment and Identity Evropa denouncement ended the fall term
events.body: President Stephen Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of a former SGA adviser, to a vacated senate seat sparked about 90 minutes of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions. The senate then passed Resolution 10-18-F, supporting denouncement of the white nationalist group Identity Evropa and its attempts to recruit on campus, 28-0, and allocated $430 to the Black Leadership Academic Conference through Bill 24-18-F.

events.title: Resolution passed to relocate Confederate marker
events.body: After lengthy debate, the senate passed Resolution 1-19-S by a 29-1 vote with one abstention, calling for the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky to be relocated to a display inside the museum. Authors Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin argued the marker was a reminder of oppression against people of color, and Mayer said the resolution would go to the WKU Administrative Council. The senate also allocated $1,000 to send the Mock Trial team to a national tournament.

events.title: Mayer declined to seek re-election as election codes were set
events.body: Mayer announced he would not seek re-election because he was applying to medical schools, and the senate approved the spring 2019 election codes 31-1, with campaigning to begin April 1 and voting on TopNet April 15-16. Chief Justice Jacob McAndrews announced he would resign from the Judicial Council to run for elected office. The senate also passed four spending bills, rejected a change to senator office-hour rules and tabled a bill creating a first-generation senate seat.

events.title: No-confidence vote and provost's resignation shook the university
events.body: After Snyder was asked to resign as Potter College dean on March 26, protests from faculty, staff and students led the University Senate to an unprecedented vote of no confidence in Provost Terry Ballman on April 4, and she resigned the next day. Ogden dean Cheryl Stevens was named acting provost, and days later the Comprehensive Academic Program Evaluation committee recommended suspending 101 of WKU's 380 academic programs.

events.title: WGK ticket won the spring executive elections
events.body: The ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, defeating the ticket of Asha McWilliams, Jacob McAndrews and Symone Whalin. Harris was elected student body president to succeed Mayer, Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president, and Mujkanovic defeated Whalin for administrative vice president, with results announced at SGA's election party on April 16.

events.title: Former SGA president sues WKU, Caboni and two administrators
events.body: Andi Dahmer filed suit against WKU, President Timothy Caboni, Assistant General Counsel Andrea Anderson and Director of Student Activities Charley Pride, citing verbal, mental and emotional abuse and alleging sex discrimination and failure to follow the university's Discrimination and Harassment Policy. The university called the allegations "maliciously untrue" and said it would vigorously defend the claims. WKU said its Title IX office found no Title IX violation but did find Student Code of Conduct violations, for which students were sanctioned.

events.title: Senate votes down both of the new president's executive nominees
events.body: Stephen Mayer's nominees were rejected in his first confirmation votes: Wood Brown for associate justice failed 8-7 with one abstention and one exemption, and Anna McAvoy for director of academic and student affairs failed 6-9, both short of the required two-thirds. Senators questioned Mayer's ability to judge candidates when he had been sequestered from the Judicial Council's interviews. The 2018-19 budget of $100,000, a $15,000 reduction from the prior year, passed 13-4.

events.title: WKU denies Dahmer's claims in court filing
events.body: WKU filed its response on Sept. 19 denying that Dahmer suffered a hostile educational environment or sexual harassment during her presidency, and stating she never reported to the Office of Student Conduct or the Title IX coordinator but instead told her residence hall director, who triggered the investigation. The university said the investigation found Student Code of Conduct violations by certain SGA members, who were sanctioned. It argued the GroupMe messages were never intended for Dahmer and so caused her no harm. Dahmer is seeking $75,000 in damages.

events.title: Bill to cut off Greek organization funding postponed 17-15
events.body: Bill 10-18-F, written by Senator Amy Wyer and Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark to bar SGA funding to Interfraternity Council and Panhellenic Council chapters, was pulled from the agenda and postponed to Oct. 16 on a 17-15 vote because of its content. Two funding bills moved forward the same night, giving $150 to the student ID voucher program and $1,500 to the Office of Study Away.

events.title: Greek defunding bill fails by one vote after long debate
events.body: Bill 10-18-F was defeated 16-17. Author Amy Wyer, herself a member of Alpha Gamma Delta, cited the University of Alabama's Machine coalition and said only one non-Greek member had been elected to that student government since 1914, warning "I fear we have the potential to move in this direction." Former senator Alex Sargent argued against telling students who pay the same tuition that their social needs matter less. A motion to table failed 21-14, short of two-thirds.

events.title: Senate creates a recurring $2,000 first-generation scholarship
events.body: A bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr establishing a $2,000 scholarship awarded once per academic year to first-generation students passed 31-1. The Herald cited a 2017 WKU Fact Book study finding an estimated 34.8 percent of first-year, first-time students in fall 2016 were first-generation. Two organizational aid bills also passed, including $1,400 split among Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club.

events.title: Colonnade textbook library tabled amid questions about the bookstore
events.body: Bill 18-18-F, allocating $1,000 to stock a used-textbook library for Colonnade courses in the SGA offices, was tabled 24-3 with one abstention after debate over funding and over whether the collection would stay current as Colonnade courses change. Senator Amy Wyer asked why the WKU Bookstore was "making us buy books they can't resell." Two bylaw amendments passed the same night, one adding flexibility in appointing regional ambassadors and one adding protection against discrimination on the basis of gender identity.

events.title: Senate votes 30-0 to defend transgender student protections
events.body: Resolution 7-18-F, written by Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark in response to reports that the Trump administration was considering narrowly redefining sex, pledged to preserve and improve protections for transgender and nonconforming students regardless of federal action. It passed 30-0. Resolution 8-18-F requiring all new campus buildings to meet LEED standards passed 29-0, and Bill 23-18-F tightening executive board appointments to require a two-thirds senate vote passed 28-1.

events.title: Ninety-minute fight over a nominee; senate denounces Identity Evropa
events.body: Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of former SGA adviser Charley Pride, produced roughly an hour and a half of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions; a motion to table failed 8-19-1. Senator Kara Lowry opposed her over her work on Braxton Powell's earlier presidential campaign. Resolution 10-18-F, denouncing Identity Evropa's attempts to recruit on campus, passed 28-0.

events.title: Nine senators forced to step down, leaving the chamber depleted
events.body: SGA opened the spring semester with vacant seats after nine senators were required to step down from their positions. Mayer presented a slate of nominees to fill them, to be voted on the following week. No new legislation was introduced at the meeting.

events.title: Study abroad scholarship bill pulled after five competing motions
events.body: Bill 2-19-S, which would have barred students who had already received an SGA study abroad scholarship from reapplying, was pulled from the agenda after debate produced five motions ranging from amendments to a 30-second cap on further speeches. Author Jayden Thomas said "I don't think it's fair to award scholarships to the same people who get them over and over again." Speaker Asha McWilliams said the debate showed the senate "doing what it is supposed to do."

events.title: Rewritten study abroad bill passes with a first-timer bonus
events.body: Bill 7-19-S replaced the outright ban on repeat applicants with a 15 percent scoring bonus for students who had not previously studied abroad. Senator Josh Zaczek argued during debate that the change was "detracting from a merit-based scholarship" and that applicants' claims could not be verified. Authors Jayden Thomas and Amanda Harder had rewritten the bill after concerns about its exclusionary effect.

events.title: Senate votes 29-1 to move the Confederate capital marker
events.body: Resolution 1-19-S, written by senators Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin, called the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky a reminder of oppression, and passed 29-1 with one abstention. An amendment during the meeting changed the ask from removal to relocation into a museum display. Lowry said that was "a good compromise for people who believe that [the marker] is preserving history." Mayer said the resolution would go to the Administrative Council rather than the University Senate.

events.title: Dahmer adds a retaliation claim, alleging Caboni pulled a Rhodes recommendation
events.body: Dahmer moved to amend her complaint to add retaliation, claiming Caboni withdrew his endorsement of her Rhodes Scholarship application "without any reason or explanation" after she sued. Text messages from Office of Scholar Development Director Audra Jennings indicating Caboni would endorse her were submitted as evidence, along with a later email in which Jennings said "I cannot discuss the matter with you." Dahmer continued to seek $75,000 in damages.

events.title: Mayer will not seek re-election; chief justice resigns to run
events.body: Stephen Mayer told the senate he would not seek re-election because he was applying to medical school. Spring election codes passed 31-1 after every proposed amendment was struck down, with one friendly amendment from Senator John May barring sitting Judicial Council members from running; Chief Justice Jacob McAndrews then announced he would resign to campaign. Bill 19-19-S, which would have let senators substitute tabling for office hours, failed 18-10 for want of a two-thirds majority.

events.title: Senate votes 23-1 for a $5 student fee to fund the Herald
events.body: Resolution 5-19-S endorsed a $5 per-student publications fee to support the College Heights Herald, noting the University of Kentucky charges $2 for the Kernel and Texas State charges $8 for the University Star. Academic and Student Affairs Chair Amanda Harder said SGA had previously backed the Herald in its ongoing lawsuit against WKU. Senators also unanimously amended the constitution to require the SGA website be kept updated and to use gender-neutral pronouns, and elected Nathan Terrell speaker 15-11.

events.title: Judge orders WKU to release records to Dahmer
events.body: A judge ruled in favor of releasing records Dahmer sought in discovery, including complaints relating to Charley Pride, Title IX investigation statements, and records of other SGA members' discrimination or harassment complaints since August 2017. WKU had objected broadly on the grounds that the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act excluded the material as educational records. Dahmer and attorney Lindsay Cordes argued the records were "relevant to prove an atmosphere of discrimination."

events.title: Impeachment hearing for a Judicial Council member called off
events.body: SGA scheduled and then canceled an impeachment hearing for Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson after determining too few senators would attend. The petition accused her of inconsistently listing spring 2019 candidates by preferred or legal name, noting Garrett Edmonds appeared as "James" with his surname misspelled, and of overstepping during Wood Brown's failed confirmation. Carlson, who graduated that week, said legal names were used because a GPA check was required, and called the effort a waste of resources that showed "the pettiness of the organization."

events.title: Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day and to loosen the conduct code
events.body: SGA passed Resolution 5-18-F 15-0, asking the university to cancel classes on 6 November 2018 so students could get to the polls, and Bill 7-18-F, giving $300 to the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote. Francis Wilson of Reg 2 Vote told senators that of 290,000 Kentucky students registered in 2016, only about 13 percent voted. Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike Student Code of Conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings, both passed 14-0. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed.

events.title: Senate passed a transparency resolution 30-2 after the dean's sudden resignation
events.body: A week after Potter College Dean Larry Snyder resigned abruptly, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by 30 votes to 2, saying top university officials must explain major decisions and carry them out in a manner that protects the dignity of those involved. Mayer's renomination of Wood Brown to the Judicial Council was struck down 17-11, short of two-thirds, after Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson said the council preferred Erika Puhakka. A bill creating a senate seat for first-generation college students passed 33-0. A resolution brought by the Transgender Non-Binary student organization, asking WKU to let students' preferred names appear on class rosters, IDs and email addresses, also passed 33-0.

executive.name: Stephen Mayer
executive.note: Also served as student regent under the merged offices.

executive.name: Will Harris
executive.note: Elected student body president for 2019-20 the following spring.

executive.office: Director of Academic and Student Affairs
executive.name: Aubrey Kelly
executive.note: Third nominee for the seat; confirmed 24-3-4 on Sep. 25, 2018 after Ashley Cox withdrew and Anna McAvoy's confirmation failed 6-9-1.

committees.name: Public Relations
committees.note: Rendered "Bridget Stakelum" in the Sept. 25, 2018 minutes and "Brigid Stakelum" in the Oct. 23 and Nov. 13 minutes; spelling unverified.

committees.name: Committee of Academic and Student Affairs (CASA)
committees.note: A Senate committee distinct from the executive Director of Academic and Student Affairs.

senate.note: This was the 17th Senate, called to order each week by Speaker Asha McWilliams. Randall P. Bogard served as SGA's faculty advisor. Minutes for this term were posted by WKU as Word documents rather than PDFs.

leaders.name: Will Harris
leaders.note: From Glasgow. Sworn in as student regent 2 August 2019. His term ran into the March 2020 campus shutdown.

sources.label: WKU News - regents swear in student regent

profile: Harris won the student body presidency in April 2019 at the head of the WGK ticket with Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic, defeating Asha McWilliams. After the results were announced at SGA's election party, he said he looked forward to "making a positive impact for all students here at WKU" and to collaborating with the opposing ticket. He took office at SGA's annual banquet and presided over his first meeting the following Tuesday.

The defining controversy of his fall semester was Resolution 4-19-F, the senate's push to punish Alpha Xi Delta after a video showed members singing a racial slur. Harris abstained when his executive board vetoed the resolution 4-0, explaining that the discrimination claim would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and that no violation had been noted by the Office of Student Conduct. When senators suggested his position as a knight of Alpha Xi Delta motivated him, he rejected the charge and said he wanted to reach an amicable outcome with the resolution's authors.

events.title: Harris-led WGK ticket wins SGA executive election
events.body: The WGK ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, with Harris defeating Asha McWilliams for student body president. Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president and Mujkanovic defeated Symone Whalin for administrative vice president. Results were announced at SGA's election party, with the new officers set to take office at the annual banquet; the Herald's results story reported no turnout figures.

events.title: First meeting of the year confirms five executive appointments
events.body: At its first official meeting of the semester, the senate confirmed all five of President Will Harris's executive branch nominees: Aubrey Kelley as chief of staff, Ashlynn Evans as chief of public relations, Abbey Norvell as director of academic and student affairs, Paul Brosky as director of information technology and Josh Zaczek as Legislative Research Committee chair. Appointees outlined plans including wider use of counseling center fee vouchers and a revival of the need-based Earn-a-Computer program.

events.title: Senate blocks budget over special projects fund
events.body: The senate refused to pass the year's budget over a $6,500 special projects fund the executive branch wanted for a sand volleyball court and hammock space at the First Year Village green space. Senators including Anthony Survance objected that the allocation cut into scholarship money, with Survance calling the motion "slimy", and the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships. The executive branch pulled the budget, forcing a week's wait before a revised version could be voted on.

events.title: Go With the Flow feminine hygiene bill passes unanimously
events.body: Bill 1-20-S, funding the Go With the Flow program that supplies feminine hygiene products in campus restrooms, passed the senate unanimously. The bill, carried forward by Campus Improvement Chair Matthew Barr, doubled the program's budget from $588, and a floor amendment from Senator Symone Whalin raised the final amount to $1,300 from senate discretionary funds. Products were to be placed in Grise Hall, DSU, Preston Center, Gary Ransdell Hall and Snell Hall, including gender neutral bathrooms.

events.title: WKU extends spring break, moves classes online amid COVID-19
events.body: WKU announced it would extend spring break by one week and transition to "alternative delivery formats" for classes amid growing coronavirus concerns, with President Tim Caboni recommending that students who could safely return home do so. The announcement came after the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville suspended in-person classes. In-person instruction never resumed that semester, upending the rest of SGA's spring calendar.

events.title: Spring elections postponed until fall as SGA moves to Zoom
events.body: With campus closed by COVID-19, SGA postponed its spring elections until at least September so voting could happen in person, and added an "emergency clause" constitutional amendment allowing cabinet terms to be extended until the following election with judicial oversight. The cabinet continued meeting over Zoom every Tuesday. Harris said that after scholarships were awarded, the remainder of SGA's budget would be donated to the WKU Opportunity Fund and Emergency Relief Fund, and SGA gave its remaining food bank goods to the Office of Sustainability for redistribution.

events.title: SGA deadlocks over budget, executive branch pulls the bill
events.body: The senate and executive branch failed to pass a budget at their second meeting, splitting over a $6,500 special projects allocation for a sand volleyball court and hammock spaces at the First Year Village. Senator Anthony Survance called the motion "slimy" and said it cut money reserved for scholarships; the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its own discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships, and the executive branch withdrew the budget. Rules required a full week before a revised budget could be voted on.

events.title: Senate votes 17-15 to cancel a meeting for a sorority philanthropy event
events.body: A motion by Senator Hope Wells to cancel the Oct. 8 senate meeting for Kappa Delta's Shenanigans passed 17-15 after debate. Senator Anthony Survance argued that given recent controversies with Greek organizations SGA should not signal endorsement, while Senator Brigid Stakelum said the reason was practical, that quorum might not be met. Newly elected senators were sworn in at the same meeting by Chief Justice Isaac Keller.

events.title: Two SGA members organize protest against Alpha Xi Delta
events.body: Senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance organized a protest at the Shenanigans philanthropy event in response to a Twitter video showing WKU Alpha Xi Delta members singing a racial slur. Survance said the vote to cancel the senate meeting for the event helped prompt the protest, and the pair created a Facebook group titled "Demand Alpha Xi Delta's Removal." Whalin said administrative inaction signaled that minority students were not a priority.

events.title: Chief justice tells senate the AXiD resolution would be symbolic; student urges labor committee
events.body: Chief Justice Isaac Keller told senators the resolution would be purely symbolic because SGA cannot direct WKU to defund an organization on grounds of discrimination, and suggested supporters take the matter to the Title IX office or the Kentucky Human Rights Commission. Harris said no student had filed a formal discrimination charge. Former senator Jay Wells addressed the meeting urging SGA to form a labor committee, citing cut student worker hours and the CAPE committee's recommendation to suspend 101 academic programs.

events.title: SGA reports record 398 scholarship applications
events.body: Director of Academic and Student Affairs Abbey Norvell reported 398 scholarship applications, including 132 for winter term, 122 for the first generation scholarship, 81 for study abroad, 31 for scholar development, 10 for ISEC and 22 for the revived Earn-a-Computer program. Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds reported First Year Village construction was on schedule and said a remaining building near the old library site would be torn down if incoming student numbers did not require the beds.

events.title: Senators quietly leave their seats, two committee chairs vacant
events.body: The Herald reported that senators and committee chairs had vacated positions since the fall semester, most leaving to study abroad or over schedule conflicts, weakening the senate's numbers. The SAVES and Sustainability committee chairs were both vacant with no replacements identified, and President Will Harris posted an open SGA application on social media to recruit. The meeting also covered planning for the March Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort.

events.title: Bill 1-20-S more than doubles menstrual product funding to $1,300
events.body: The senate unanimously passed Bill 1-20-S, funding for the "Go With the Flow" program, raising it from $588 the previous year. Campus Improvement Chair Matthew Barr presented the bill at $1,176 before Senator Symone Whalin amended the figure to $1,300, drawn from the senate discretionary pool. Products were to be placed in Grise Hall, DSU, the Preston Center, Gary Ransdell Hall and Snell Hall, including gender neutral bathrooms.

events.title: Contentious senator confirmations turn on legislation records and party affiliation
events.body: Five senators and two committee chairs were confirmed, with Parker Raybourne and Kat Howard drawing scrutiny for having written no legislation and for not having read the 2019-2020 budget. Senator Anthony Survance questioned Raybourne's membership in WKU College Republicans and was cut off by Speaker Nathan Terrell, who said SGA was nonpartisan. Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr defended the nominees, saying committees exist to develop ideas together.

events.title: SGA adds constitutional emergency clause and redirects remaining budget to relief funds
events.body: Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said the postponement of spring elections came with an emergency clause amendment to the constitution allowing cabinet terms to be extended until the following election under judicial oversight. President Will Harris said that after scholarships were awarded the remainder of SGA's budget would go to the WKU Opportunity Fund and Emergency Relief Fund. SGA also donated its remaining food bank goods to the Office of Sustainability.

events.title: Greeks Go Green sustainability contest funded at $75
events.body: Bill 1-19-F allocated $75 from senate discretionary funding for prizes in Greeks Go Green, a competition between WKU's Greek organisations to run the most sustainable chapter house by logging environmentally friendly actions for points. The contest ran from 20 September 2019 through April, with winners announced at the Greek Week convocation. The bill passed its second reading on 10 September 2019.

src.label: SGA Bill 1-19-F, Funding for Greeks Go Green

events.title: Etiquette dinner for the Glasgow campus
events.body: Bill 2-20-S passed unanimously on 18 February 2020, funding a professional etiquette dinner for students at WKU's Glasgow regional campus and subsidising the ticket price, with Glasgow covering the rest. Executive vice president Garrett Edmonds, who brought the bill, said it was aimed at students from small towns who had never faced a table set with several forks and knives, and that to his knowledge it was the only etiquette dinner held at a WKU regional campus.

src.label: Herald, 19 Feb 2020 - "SGA motion to host professional etiquette dinner passes unanimously"

events.title: Senate passed Resolution 4-19-F seeking discipline against Alpha Xi Delta, 24-7
events.body: The senate voted 24-7 for Resolution 4-19-F, authored by senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance, supporting disciplinary action up to suspension from Greek affairs against the Epsilon Kappa chapter of Alpha Xi Delta. The resolution followed an August Twitter video showing chapter members singing a racial slur in a rap song, and the authors said administrative silence signaled the university did not care about minority students, wanting more than "an article from the Herald or an email from Bob Skipper." Before passage a motion struck the call for removal from campus out of the title and a friendly amendment substituted suspension from Greek affairs. Senator Mary Mayo said it was not SGA's job to act as a disciplinary committee, and the resolution was to be submitted to the Faculty Senate.

events.title: Executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F 4-0 and the senate sustained the veto
events.body: The executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F, the Alpha Xi Delta resolution, by 4 votes to 0 with two of its six members abstaining, and the senate confirmed the veto at its Tuesday meeting. President Will Harris, one of the abstainers, said the discrimination claim the resolution invoked would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and that the Office of Student Conduct had noted no violation. Co-author Anthony Survance accused the executive branch of dragging the issue out, and Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek disputed the reasoning. Senators raised Harris's standing as an Alpha Xi Delta knight, which he rejected as grounds for bias.

events.title: Budget passed with spending stipulations and campaign spending caps halved
events.body: All 13 senators approved the yearly budget after a three-part compromise confined the special projects fund to the First Year Village plans and redistributed any money unspent by March 3 back to discretionary and voucher funds. Its passage let Bill 1-19-F, Greeks Go Green, and Bill 2-19-F, funding for Bowling Green Pride, pass unanimously. The senate also amended its election codes to halve campaign spending maximums, which had been $300 for presidential candidates, $125 for vice presidential candidates and $50 for senate candidates. Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds objected, calling SGA turnout awful and estimating 1,500 students voted the previous year, while Senator Symone Whalin said poorer students were less likely to run for executive office.

events.title: Senate approved a $5,000 hammock project after the volleyball court was dropped
events.body: The senate passed Bill 3-20-S, allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to begin planning hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court proposed earlier in the year was judged too expensive. Planned locations included spots near most residence halls and the Valley, and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said he and Harris had run so SGA would be known for more than scantrons and greenbooks. Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek criticized having to vote without seeing budget numbers, said he had met friction getting figures from Edmonds and wanted assurance the money would be spent inclusively. Residence Hall Association President Emily Whitney backed the project and noted RHA's own budget cuts, and the senate kept the power to halt spending during planning.

leaders.name: J. Garrett Edmonds
leaders.note: The COVID year. Almost certainly the most unusual term in the organisation's history and worth a dedicated oral history.
profile: Edmonds, a senior from Island, Kentucky, spent his freshman year as chair of the Campus Improvements Committee, working with Vice President of Student Affairs Brian Kuster on projects including a campus safety walk, before winning election as executive vice president in April 2018 on a ticket with Harper Anderson and Stephen Mayer. He served two years as executive vice president under President Will Harris, pushing for a budget model geared toward campus amenities and recreational life and working to diversify Senate appointments with seats for underrepresented students.

He ran for the presidency in fall 2020 on the Edmonds-Norvell ticket, after his original running mate for administrative vice president, Nathan Terrell, dropped out and was replaced by Abbey Norvell. The campaign centered on a pledge to create a Director of Outreach position to close the communication gap between campus organizations and SGA, and the Sept. 24 Herald town hall covered WKU's COVID-19 response and the summer's Black Lives Matter protests on campus. Voting ran Sept. 28-29 on TopNet; Edmonds defeated senator MJ Mayo, becoming SGA president and, since the two offices had merged by then, student regent on the WKU Board of Regents. Norvell was elected administrative vice president alongside him, with the Herald reporting no decision yet made on a separate executive vice president post.

Taking office amid the pandemic, the senate confirmed Isaac Keller to a vice-president post 29-1 in October after Edmonds said he wanted a deputy willing to challenge him; the Herald's report on that vote first called the office executive vice president, then ran a correction changing it to administrative vice president -- the same title the Herald had given Norvell in September, a conflict the record does not resolve. Matt Barr, Ashlynn Evans, Kody Okert and Paul Brosky rounded out the executive and Shelby Robertson served as non-voting speaker of the senate. Early cabinet business set up officer office hours, an ad hoc outreach committee chaired by Me'Lon Craighead and a push toward inclusive pronoun language in Senate proceedings. That fall SGA petitioned WKU to restore Pass/D/Fail grading for COVID-disrupted students; Associate Provost Rob Hale initially rebuffed the request, calling the university's extended drop deadline sufficient, but by December the petition -- more than 3,500 signatures in three days -- had succeeded, and Edmonds thanked senators for the work behind it at the semester's final meeting alongside bills funding campus safe-driving signage and several student organizations.

In the spring his senate passed the organization's largest-ever organizational aid bill and a resolution seeking a codified vetting process for campus dining vendors after a controversial social media post by a local pizzeria owner, alongside legislation backing WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force in renaming buildings tied to racism, a community garden, and a diversity-event push by DEI chair Fatin Yaro. Near the end of his term he declined to fill the chief justice seat vacated by Erika Puhakka, saying the choice belonged to his successor: "I think that's the only thing that is right in this scenario." He also worried publicly that only 13 students were running for senate in the April election, and closed his term addressing the Class of 2021 at the delayed Fall 2020/Spring 2021 commencement, telling graduates their perseverance through "this past year" had brought them to their day of celebration.

events.title: Town hall debate pitted the sitting EVP against a senator
events.body: SGA held a town hall debate in the DSU auditorium between presidential candidates Garrett Edmonds, the sitting executive vice president, and senator MJ Mayo. Edmonds's original running mate for administrative vice president, Nathan Terrell, had dropped off the Edmonds-Norvell ticket and was replaced by Abbey Norvell; the debate covered WKU's COVID-19 response and the summer's Black Lives Matter protests on campus.

events.title: Edmonds elected president over Mayo
events.body: Garrett Edmonds, the sitting executive vice president, was elected student body president over senator MJ Mayo in balloting held on TopNet Sept. 28-29, succeeding Will Harris. Edmonds had campaigned on creating a Director of Outreach position to link campus organizations more directly with SGA.

events.title: Senate passed the annual budget 28-5 and elected Shelby Robertson speaker
events.body: At the first official senate meeting under the new leadership, Shelby Robertson defeated Brenna Matthews to become speaker of the senate and the budget passed 28-5. Edmonds emphasized a $6,000 Projects Fund, including $1,000 for Housing and Residence Life PPE and an expansion of the Go with the Flow menstrual products program into Pearce Ford Tower. Senator MJ Mayo challenged the balance of stipends; Edmonds said all senate stipends except the top three offices had been cut to feed the Projects Fund.

events.title: Cabinet set office hours, an outreach committee, and pushed inclusive language
events.body: At the executive cabinet's first recorded meeting, Edmonds set up officer office hours and an ad hoc outreach committee for RSO leadership. Speaker Shelby Robertson pushed to connect senators with similar legislative interests, adopt inclusive pronoun language in the chamber, and find a parliamentarian.

events.title: Keller confirmed AVP 29-1; two new committee chairs elected
events.body: The senate confirmed Isaac Keller as administrative vice president 29-1 after Edmonds said he wanted a deputy willing to challenge him when they disagreed. Roderick Maul and Tess Welch were elected committee chairs, and senators voted to form a new Ad Hoc committee chaired by Me'Lon Craighead.

events.title: Presidential task force sought input on slaveholding college namesakes
events.body: WKU's Presidential Task Force on Naming and Symbols, formed by President Timothy Caboni in fall 2020, collected input from students and the community on the namesakes of Potter College and Ogden College, both built on wealth from slave labor. Two Potter descendants said it was time to find a new name. The task force planned to audit names and send recommendations to the administration.

events.title: Largest organizational aid bill passed; chief justice resigned before elections
events.body: Edmonds announced that Chief Justice Erika Puhakka had stepped down and declined to nominate a replacement so close to elections, and warned that only 13 people were running for senate. The senate passed its largest organizational aid bill ever, funding five student groups, and passed 16-0 with two abstentions a bill by Kyle Phillips asking WKU to support a codified vetting process for campus dining vendors after a controversial social media post by the owner of Lost River Pizza.

events.title: WKU relented and allowed pass grades after SGA's P/D/F campaign
events.body: Provost Cheryl Stevens told faculty that students who faced COVID-related problems could opt for a pass grade instead of a B or C, reversing the university's earlier refusal. The Faculty Senate had voted 40-9 in favor and SGA voted unanimously for the option, presenting nearly 20 pages of student testimony; SGA's petition had drawn over 3,500 signatures in three days. Students had to email their professor by Jan. 13, with the final decision left to the faculty member.

events.title: Edmonds addressed the Class of 2021 at the delayed commencement
events.body: As SGA president, Edmonds spoke at WKU's Fall 2020/Spring 2021 commencement ceremony, telling graduates that the class's perseverance through the pandemic year had brought them to their day of celebration.

events.title: Norvell elected administrative vice president; EVP still open
events.body: SGA held a virtual election party over Zoom to announce results. The Edmonds-Norvell ticket defeated MJ Mayo for the presidency, and Abbey Norvell was elected administrative vice president alongside Edmonds. The Herald reported no official decision had yet been made on a separate executive vice president post, with an announcement expected at the next SGA meeting.

events.title: Judicial nominations confirmed; senate revives a Pass/D/Fail request
events.body: The senate unanimously confirmed Edmonds's nominations of Derek Collins and Lexi Mayne as associate justices and Addison McCoun as senator at large. Senators passed a Tess Welch/Eric Barry bill to increase campus accessibility and split funding for SGA-branded masks and hand sanitizer between the senate and SGA's PR team. A closing bill by Tate McClard and Jacob Congleton, with every senator listed as a co-author, asked WKU to restore the Pass/D/Fail grading option it had offered in spring 2020 but declined to bring back that fall.

events.title: Edmonds launched a P/D/F petition
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds released a student petition asking WKU to offer a Pass/D/Fail grading option for the fall semester, citing inconsistent course modalities and the strain of quarantine on students without an online-learning fallback. The petition reached half its 1,000-signature goal within an hour and the target was raised to 5,000.

events.title: Fall semester closed with a safe-driving pledge and organization funding
events.body: At the last meeting of the fall semester, Edmonds thanked senators for the work that led to the new P/D/F option. Senators unanimously passed a Matthew Thomas bill committing SGA's social media to a "Drive Safe Hilltoppers" safety campaign, and unanimously funded a bill supporting HonorsToppers, College Republicans, Zeta Phi Beta and the Sociology and Criminology Club.

events.title: Spring semester opened over Zoom with a late-fee pledge
events.body: At its first meeting of the spring semester, held on Zoom, SGA heard Edmonds say the provost search was in its final stage with interviews starting within weeks, and that he planned to look at changing or removing the late fees charged when a student's financial aid arrives late. Senators unanimously nominated Jamison Moorehead as director of IT and funded Dance Big Red and a Delta Sigma Pi virtual leadership conference.

events.title: Committee chairs set spring priorities
events.body: Legislative Research Chair Dawson McCoun said the shift to remote meetings after March 2020 had made it harder to connect with students and pass legislation. Diversity and Inclusion Chair Fatin Yaro announced a Feb. 24 diversity event and legislation to set consequences for discrimination within student organizations, and Chief of Staff Matt Barr said he would continue the "Go with the Flow" program installing free menstrual-product dispensers on campus. SGA planned a return to masked, socially distanced in-person meetings that semester.

events.title: New senator seated; rally with Gov. Beshear announced
events.body: SGA nominated pre-law sophomore Will Dykeman as a new senator and Edmonds announced a virtual Student Body President rally for March 26 featuring Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, with Edmonds working to add state Rep. Charles Booker. Senators unanimously funded a bill by AVP Isaac Keller supporting Amazing Tones of Joy, Black Women of Western, Queer Student Union and the Business Association for Development, and voted $2,500 for ISEC's Black Magic Masquerade Ball on a bill by Me'Lon Craighead.

events.title: Outreach signage and safe-driving bills pass
events.body: Guest speaker Ethan Logan, vice president of enrollment and student experience, briefed senators on how his office could help SGA. Edmonds pointed senators toward an upcoming provost-search update and urged them to consider running in the April officer elections. Senators unanimously passed a Me'Lon Craighead bill funding 50 laminated, QR-coded outreach signs for campus and a Matthew Thomas bill adding 12 safe-driving signs to campus parking lots; a bill on WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force was held for the following week.

events.title: Constitution amended; Caboni's contract extended
events.body: Edmonds told senators the WKU Board of Regents had extended President Timothy Caboni's contract four years. The senate elected Addison McCoun to head the Legislative Research Committee after Dawson McCoun's resignation, passed a Tess Welch/Erika Puhakka bill amending constitutional wording 19-4, and funded a Sustainability Committee spring photo contest on a bill by Matthew Waninger and Elizabeth DeLozier.

events.title: SGA meets for the first time since April, plans to redirect study abroad money
events.body: SGA held its first meeting since April over Zoom, moving transition guides and election codes to a fully digital format. President Will Harris said the study abroad scholarship money would have flexibility to be reallocated because COVID-19 restrictions blocked travel. Senator Me'Lon Craighead outlined planned diversity legislation including consequences for racial offenses on campus and a mandatory course for students and workers.

events.title: Senate speaker resigns and quits the executive vice president race over slur video
events.body: Nathan Terrell, speaker of the SGA senate and a candidate for executive vice president, resigned after a video showing him using a racial slur was sent anonymously to the Herald. He initially denied being in the video, then confirmed it and issued a statement removing himself from the Garrett-Nathan-Abbey ticket. Terrell asserted the anonymous submitter had a political agenda against him and the ticket.

events.title: Town hall candidates split over conditions in the quarantine dorm
events.body: At the Herald town hall, presidential candidate MJ Mayo said the university had spread misinformation about the quarantine dorm at Barnes Campbell and relayed student testimony about uncleaned rooms, unclean bathrooms and expired vending machine goods. Garrett Edmonds said the university response had been more than adequate and that he was confident after meeting with the Board of Regents that the issues were resolved. Edmonds had told an SGA meeting that 234 quarantined students received 1,273 meals.

events.title: Cabinet slate confirmed; $1,000 of projects fund routed to quarantined students
events.body: Twelve nominations were confirmed, including Will Harris to the Judicial Council, Matt Barr as chief of staff, Fatin Yaro as Diversity and Inclusion chair and Dawson McCoun as head of the Legislative Research Committee. RHA representatives Emily Whitney and Me'Lon Craighead described using the $1,000 SGA projects fund allocation for goody bags, food, hygiene products and PPE for students quarantined in Barnes Campbell. Craighead said the goal was to make quarantined students feel connected to campus.

events.title: Isaac Keller confirmed administrative vice president 29-1; ad hoc committee created
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds nominated Isaac Keller as administrative vice president, saying Keller was willing to challenge him when they disagreed, and the senate confirmed him 29-1. Roderick Maul and Tess Welch were elected committee chairs. Senators also voted to form a new ad hoc committee and elected Me'Lon Craighead as its chair.

events.title: First bill of the year spends $2,334.45 on SGA signage in DSU
events.body: The senate passed the year's first bill 28-2, allocating $2,334.45 for rebranding, printing and installing new SGA signage in the Downing Student Union. Executive Vice President Abbey Norvell appointed Shelby Robertson, MJ Mayo and Kody Okert to the Faculty Senate. Edmonds told senators he had recently been in quarantine and reported the provost search was going well.

events.title: Senate takes up Pass/D/Fail bill and splits mask funding with PR
events.body: Tate McClard and Jacob Congleton authored a bill asking WKU to restore the Pass/D/Fail option for the fall semester, which Edmonds and Addison McCoun wanted every senator to co-author. Senators also passed an accessibility bill by Tess Welch and Eric Barry and agreed to split funding for SGA branded masks and hand sanitizer evenly between the senate and the PR team. Three nominations, including two associate justices, passed unanimously.

events.title: University grants a limited Pass/D/Fail option after SGA campaign
events.body: Edmonds told the final meeting of the semester that students could now request a "pass" if they received a B or C as a final grade, and credited senators and petition signers. The senate unanimously passed a bill pledging SGA support for a "Drive Safe Hilltoppers" campaign, authored by Matthew Thomas. A second bill allocating funds to HonorsToppers, College Republicans, Zeta Phi Beta and the Sociology and Criminology Club also passed unanimously.

events.title: Senate allocates $2,500 to ISEC masquerade ball and funds four organizations
events.body: A bill by Me'Lon Craighead allocating $2,500 to ISEC's Black Magic Masquerade Ball passed with overwhelming consent. A separate bill by Administrative Vice President Isaac Keller funding Amazing Tones of Joy, Black Women of Western, Queer Student Union and the Business Association for Development passed unanimously. Edmonds announced a virtual Board of Student Body Presidents rally for March 26 that Gov. Andy Beshear would attend.

events.title: SGA backs Bottom of the Hill survey as scholarship applications lag
events.body: A bill by Matthew Waninger and Matthew Thomas committing SGA support to the Bottom of the Hill Revitalization Initiative passed unanimously, triggering a campus-wide survey on what should be done with the green space near the First Year Village. Director of Academic and Student Affairs Kody Okert said fewer than 20 applications had been received for the five SGA scholarships then open. A bill funding a book scholarship for international students was held over to the following week.

events.title: Chief justice resigns and 'Vet Our Vendors' resolution passes over president's objection
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds announced Chief Justice Erika Puhakka had stepped down and said he would leave the vacancy to the next president, and reported only 13 people were running for senate. A bill by Kyle Phillips asking WKU to create a vendor vetting committee, prompted by a social media post by the owner of Lost River Pizza, passed 16-0 with two abstentions after Edmonds urged delay and a friendly amendment softened the wording. A separate organizational aid bill by Isaac Keller was described as the largest SGA had passed.

events.title: Five hundred dollars to Dance Big Red over Zoom
events.body: At SGA's first meeting of the spring 2021 semester, held on Zoom on 19 January, the senate passed a bill allocating $500 to Dance Big Red. Delta Sigma Pi also received funding for a virtual leadership conference at the same meeting. SGA planned to return to in-person meetings the following week.

src.label: Herald, 20 Jan 2021 - "SGA discusses Dance Big Red, Provost search, late fees in first meeting of semester"

events.title: Go With the Flow and a diversity event headed the spring plans
events.body: A Herald preview of SGA's spring 2021 programmes reported chief of staff Matt Barr continuing work on Go With the Flow, which put vending machines dispensing free menstrual products in campus buildings. Diversity and inclusion chair Fatin Yaro planned a large diversity event for 24 February and legislation attaching consequences to discrimination within student organisations. Legislative research chair Dawson McCoun said the year had at least given members motivation to address students' problems.

src.label: Herald, 26 Jan 2021 - "Programs to look out for from the SGA this semester"

events.title: QR-code signs and safe-driving signs went up round campus
events.body: On 9 February 2021 the senate unanimously passed a bill by senator Me'Lon Craighead funding 50 laminated signs with QR codes letting students send concerns or ideas straight to SGA. A second bill by senator Matthew Thomas added 12 signs on parking-lot poles reminding students to drive safely. Vice President for Enrollment and Student Experience Ethan Logan was the meeting's guest speaker.

src.label: Herald, 11 Feb 2021 - "SGA focuses on outreach, safe driving initiative in weekly meeting"

events.title: The five scholarships SGA was offering
events.body: A Herald guide of 11 February 2021 set out SGA's five student scholarships: Earn-a-Computer, which gave a free computer in return for logged service; the First-Generation Program for full-time students whose parents held no bachelor's degree; the ISEC Book Scholarship of $100 toward textbooks; the Scholar Development Scholarship of up to $500 for conferences, equipment, research or test preparation; and the Summer Term Scholarship for summer classes.
events.money: $100 book awards and Scholar Development grants of up to $500

src.label: Herald, 11 Feb 2021 - "5 SGA scholarships students can take advantage of this semester"

events.title: Senate backed renaming buildings tied to racism and funded a community garden
events.body: The senate passed legislation by Brenna Matthews and Tess Welch, after debate, offering SGA's support to WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force in changing the names of buildings with ties to racism or injustice. Matthews said ties to slave owning and the Confederate army were not something a public university dedicated to diversity would want on campus. Senators also unanimously funded a community garden outside the Office of Sustainability and allocated $3,500 to four student organizations. Title IX coordinator Deborah Wilkins opened the meeting by reviewing previous SGA legislation that potentially violated Title IX.

events.title: Provost's office rejected SGA's Pass/D/Fail request; computers bill passed 28-3
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds told senators that Associate Provost Rob Hale had defended the university's decision to extend the class drop deadline rather than restore Pass/D/Fail grading, and said he was "deeply disturbed" by the response. Edmonds urged senators to email the Faculty Senate and the provost and to keep circulating his petition, which had passed 3,000 signatures. Senator Brenna Mathews argued the policy left students choosing between attending in person and paying for an extra semester. The senate separately voted 28-3 to fund recycled computers for the SGA office, a number scaled back to meet CDC guidance.

documents.title: SGA Executive Cabinet minutes, 13 October 2020
documents.summary: Minutes from the first recorded fall 2020 executive cabinet meeting under President Garrett Edmonds, covering officer office hours, an ad hoc outreach committee, and Speaker Shelby Robertson's push for inclusive language and a parliamentarian.

The Herald's election story used the same 'administrative vice president' title later given (after a correction) to Isaac Keller, confirmed by the senate that October; the conflict between the two Herald reports is unresolved. As of the 30 Sep 2020 story, no decision had been made on a separate executive vice president post.
