Roderick Maul and Tess Welch were also elected general committee chairs in October 2020; Me'Lon Craighead chaired the Ad Hoc/Outreach committee. Speaker Shelby Robertson announced full committee rosters by Zoom breakout room at the 20 Oct 2020 meeting.

leaders.name: Matthew Wininger
leaders.note: Sworn in as student regent 6 August 2021, at the meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for Margaret Munday, WKU's first African American student to enrol.
profile: Wininger ran for student body president in the April 2021 SGA election, with voting held on TopNet April 12-13. In the Herald's ballot guide he said he wanted to make SGA "the most active and vibrant organization on campus." Me'Lon Craighead, who would serve as his executive vice president, ran for that office in the same election.

As president, Wininger opened the fall semester by welcoming new and returning senators to the second meeting of the 21st Senate. He presided over the unanimous confirmation of senators elected the previous semester and of his executive appointments, including Jamison Moorehead as IT director, Alexis Courtenay as public relations director and Parker Raybourne as chief of staff, and the senate adopted new election codes at the same meeting.

In spring 2022 Wininger welcomed senators back from winter break and announced an initiative to create a student resource handbook aimed particularly at underclassmen, encouraging all SGA committees to pitch in on the project. At that same first meeting of 2022, the senate he led responded to the December tornado disaster by unanimously passing a $1,000 bill to restock the Office of Sustainability food pantry.

events.title: Northeast Hall renamed for Margaret Munday
events.body: Student Regent Matthew Wininger was sworn in at the Board of Regents meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for WKU's first African American student to enrol - the first building on campus named after an African American.

events.title: Cole Bornefeld elected with 49% of 1,448 votes
events.body: Alexis Courtenay took 40% and Olivia Feck 11%. Sam Kurtz and Garrison Reed were elected to the two vice presidencies.

events.title: SGA opened the fall term with confirmations and new election codes
events.body: SGA held its first meeting of the fall semester, the second meeting of the 21st Senate, with President Matthew Wininger welcoming new and returning senators. All senators present were confirmed by unanimous consent and sworn in by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder, along with executive appointments Jamison Moorehead as IT director, Alexis Courtenay as public relations director and Parker Raybourne as chief of staff. New election codes for the next semester also passed with unanimous consent.

events.title: New senators seated and freshman election results announced
events.body: The senate unanimously voted in four new senate members, two judicial council members and Trib Singh as director of academic and student affairs. Speaker of the Senate Tess Welch introduced committees on legislative operations, student experience, mental health, sustainability, campus improvement, diversity and student outreach. That night the fall election results named Addison Falkner, Sam Kurtz and Jenna Wells freshman senators and Arivumani Srivastava the Gatton Academy senator.

events.title: 21st Senate passed its first resolution, on advisor evaluations
events.body: At its Oct. 5 meeting SGA passed Resolution 1.21f, addressing the lack of an advisor evaluation system, by a 21-2 vote, the first resolution of the 21st Senate. Bill 2.21f, barring the speaker of the senate from voting on legislation, passed 21-2, and two bills scrubbing outdated 2007-era bylaws passed by unanimous consent. Parking director Jennifer Tougas discussed a possible monthly parking tag subscription and campus bookstore operations.

events.title: EF-3 tornado struck Bowling Green, killing 11 in Warren County
events.body: An EF-3 tornado with 150 mph winds slammed into Bowling Green early on Dec. 11, killing 11 people according to the coroner and destroying homes and businesses across Warren County. Gov. Andy Beshear signed a state of emergency and President Biden signed an emergency declaration. The disaster shaped SGA relief efforts the following semester.

events.title: First 2022 meeting funded tornado-drained food pantry
events.body: At its first meeting of 2022, SGA passed Bill 1.22s by unanimous consent, providing $1,000 to restock the WKU Office of Sustainability food pantry, whose food and toiletries had been drained by the tornado recovery effort. Wininger announced an initiative to create a student resource handbook for underclassmen. Speaker Tess Welch announced spring election dates of April 18-19.

events.title: Syllabi clause, crosswalk resolutions and Title IX meetings passed
events.body: At its Feb. 15 meeting SGA unanimously passed Resolution 6-22-S to add an SGA-related clause to course syllabi, which the Herald reported would be the first of its kind in SGA history. Three resolutions supported new crosswalks below the Van Meter green space and on Chestnut and Normal streets, and Bill 6-22-S required a committee chair or delegate to meet with the Counseling Center director and Title IX coordinator each semester. The senate also approved a task force for the iWKU app and funding for a financial success workshop.

events.title: Judiciary Council cleared Bornefeld's campaign over student-all email
events.body: After several SGA members complained that presidential candidate Cole Bornefeld's student-wide email about the Swipe Out Hunger initiative violated the election code's ban on self-promotion, the Judiciary Council held a roughly hour-long Zoom hearing on April 13 and voted in favor of his campaign. Speaker Tess Welch argued the signed email constituted self-promotion, while a statement from President Wininger, read by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder, said nothing in the code required executive approval for a student-all email. Senators said the initiative saw a record number of donations after the email went out.

events.title: End-of-year allocations funded scholarships, organizational aid and planetarium donation
events.body: Hours before the 2022 election results were announced, the senate passed a slate of funding bills: $8,000 in organizational aid at $500 per applicant, and $15,500 across five scholarship programs including summer class, study abroad, ISEC book and Scholar Level scholarships, plus $500 to Black Student Alliance scholarships for the first time. The senate also approved $325 for the Hardin Planetarium, $500 for a student worker appreciation event, $300 for the CEC Run/Walk for Autism and $570.02 for an e-waste recycling bin on main campus.

events.title: Senate confirms judicial council members and a new academic affairs director
events.body: The senate unanimously confirmed four senators, two judicial council members and a director of academic and student affairs. Abbey Norvell and Nicole Massarone joined the judicial council, and Trib Singh took the academic and student affairs post. Speaker of the Senate Tess Welch introduced the Legislative Operations Committee and committees on student experience, mental health, sustainability, campus improvement, diversity and student outreach.

events.title: SGA takes up residence hall mold and DSU food lines
events.body: Executive Vice President Me'Lon Craighead told the senate that SGA was working with Housing and Residence Life on mold accumulation in residence halls and had raised long food lines at DSU, saying part of the problem stemmed from a lack of employment. She said plans were in progress to place an SGA senator on a restaurant group committee. Title IX coordinator Deborah Wilkins opened the meeting describing new Title IX training for Greek life, band and athletics students.

events.title: Senate strips the speaker of a vote and passes its first resolution of the term
events.body: Bill 2.21f, barring the speaker of the senate from voting on legislation to avoid bias, passed 21-2. Bills 3.21f and 4.21f, repealing an obsolete 2007 bylaw and outdated staff and faculty senate assignment rules, both passed with unanimous consent. Resolution 1.21f, addressing the lack of an advisor evaluation system, passed 21-2 and was the first resolution passed by the 21st senate.

events.title: State Rep. Patti Minter asks SGA to endorse a student borrower bill
events.body: State Rep. Patti Minter, a WKU history professor, asked SGA to endorse legislation she called the "Student Borrower's Bill of Rights," aimed at predatory student loan companies, and clarified it was not a debt cancellation bill. The senate passed Bill 5.21f initiating a Title IX training module for all SGA senators. Four senate nominees were confirmed with unanimous consent and sworn in by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder.

events.title: Bill to buy senator polos draws contention over cost
events.body: Bill 7.21f, allocating funding for polo shirts for senators to wear at meetings, was contested, with some senators arguing the polos would be uncomfortable in winter months. The Herald reported the bill would consume 10% of the discretionary legislative budget if passed. Assistant Provost Molly Kerby spoke on classroom equity work and a rise in WKU's Campus Pride Index score.

events.title: Senate funds job fair scholarships after long debate
events.body: Bill 12.21f, funding three $250 scholarships at an upcoming job fair sponsored by the Advising and Career Development Center, passed after extended debate. Bill 10.21f amending bylaws and Bill 11.21f funding the Chinese club both passed with unanimous consent, as did Resolution 2.21f providing a gift basket for a Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony. Craighead reported progress creating a new university committee for the WKU Restaurant Group.

events.title: Predatory loan resolution stalls on a 17-16 vote
events.body: Resolution 3.21f, on stopping predatory student loans for first year students and stemming from Rep. Patti Minter's visit, did not pass. By a 17-16 vote the senate rescheduled debate to the following meeting. Bill 13.21f, allocating $350 for a finals stress relief tabling event, passed by an overwhelming margin.

events.title: Loan resolution passes on reintroduction; senate backs campus-wide Title IX training
events.body: Resolution 3.21f passed on reintroduction with 17 in favor, 8 against and 4 abstentions after heavy criticism the previous week. Resolution 6.21f, requiring Title IX training for all enrolled students and WKU faculty, passed by an overwhelming margin. Resolution 7.21f, on the teaching of critical race theory, was introduced but its debate and vote were postponed for time.

events.title: Senate votes $1,000 to restock the campus food pantry after the tornadoes
events.body: Bill 1.22s, providing $1,000 to restock the food pantry in the WKU Office of Sustainability, passed with unanimous consent. The Herald reported the tornado recovery effort had drained the pantry's food and toiletries. Speaker of the Senate Tess Welch set spring election signups to close April 8 with voting April 18-19.

events.title: Senate adds an SGA clause to course syllabi and passes three crosswalk resolutions
events.body: Resolution 6-22-S, adding an SGA clause to course syllabi listing meeting times, office location and the organization's purpose, passed unanimously and was described as the first of its kind in SGA history. Resolutions 3-22-S, 4-22-S and 5-22-S, supporting new crosswalks below the Van Meter green space, in front of 1600 Chestnut St. and near 1566 Normal St., all passed unanimously. Bill 6-22-S, requiring a committee chair or delegate to meet with the Counseling Center director and the Title IX coordinator at least once per semester, was approved.

events.title: SGA approves a meal swipe donation program against food insecurity
events.body: SGA approved a program letting students donate excess meal swipes in the 4th, 8th and 12th weeks of each semester, with the WKU Restaurant Group matching one swipe for every four donated. Students facing food insecurity could request five or 10 meal blocks up to twice per semester, with a pot of up to 1,000 swipes. Senator-at-Large Cole Bornefeld, who pushed the program, said he wanted students to be able to help other students.

events.title: Senate backs LGBTQ+ outreach and training by WKU Police
events.body: The senate voted in favor of Resolution 8-22-S, supporting outreach to the LGBTQ community and training on sexual orientation and gender identity issues by the WKU Police Department. It also unanimously approved Bill 15-22-S allocating $100 for materials for ISEC's Women's History Month tabling. Senators Ataullah Tahiri and Tramaine Hawkins were unanimously confirmed.

events.title: Constitution amended on mental health committee; food insecurity clause added to syllabi
events.body: Bill 22-22-S, amending the SGA constitution to redefine the duties of the Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee, passed unanimously. Resolution 10-22-S, adding a food insecurity clause to course syllabi pointing students to the meal swipe request form and the Office of Sustainability, also passed unanimously. Bill 36-22-S funding an Easter egg hunt benefiting the Kentucky Veterans Brigade was passed with the amount amended upward from $500 to $750.

events.title: Judicial Council clears presidential candidate over a student-wide email
events.body: The Judiciary Council voted in favor of Cole Bornefeld's campaign after SGA members complained his student-wide email about the swipe out hunger initiative violated election code section 3.5 barring self-promotional mail. Speaker Tess Welch argued the signature made it self-promotion, and Administrative Vice President Reed Breunig said the email was not cleared by any member of SGA. Chief Justice Holden Schroeder read a statement from President Matthew Wininger saying no rule required executive cabinet or PR approval for such emails.

events.title: Senate allocates $15,500 in scholarships and $8,000 in organizational aid
events.body: Bill 45-22-S passed unanimously, splitting $15,500 across summer class, study abroad, ISEC book and scholar level scholarships, including a first-ever $500 for Black Student Alliance scholarships. Bill 42-22-S granted $500 to each organization that applied for fall organizational aid, totaling $8,000. The senate cut a requested $1,000 Hardin Planetarium donation to $325 and a $500 autism walk request to $300, and approved $570.02 for an e-waste recycling bin.

events.title: SGA put $1,200 and a mechanical bull into Homecoming
events.body: Bill 8-21-F allocated $1,200 from legislative discretionary funds to the Intercultural Student Engagement Center for its Homecoming 2021 events at Centennial Mall on 27 October, free and open to all students from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. The bill records that the attraction was a mechanical bull, intended to get students socialising after the pandemic had made networking difficult for ISEC. It had its first reading on 26 October 2021.

src.label: SGA Bill 8-21-F, Funding for the ISEC Homecoming 2021 events and activities

events.title: Free teeth cleanings through the dental hygiene programme
events.body: Bill 9-22-S allocated $500 from the legislative discretionary budget to the WKU Dental Hygiene programme to start a voucher system giving students free teeth cleanings. The bill said the $500 would cover 20 cleanings and would also help the dental hygiene students, who needed a set number of patients to complete their studies. It had its first reading on 8 February 2022 and the voucher was still part of SGA's programme four years later.

src.label: SGA Bill 9-22-S, Funding for vouchers for free teeth cleanings through the WKU Dental Hygiene Program

events.title: Love The Earth tabled on Valentine's Day
events.body: Bill 8-22-S allocated $100 from legislative discretionary funds for the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee's Love The Earth tabling event at Downing Student Union on 14 February 2022, from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. SGA handed out snacks and flyers, promoted WKU Recycling and sustainability organisations, and collected student input.

src.label: SGA Bill 8-22-S, Funding for a "Love The Earth" Valentine's Day Event

events.title: Fifteen hundred dollars into the Run on Walmart
events.body: Bill 20-22-S proposed allocating $1,500 from the legislative discretionary fund to the Run on Walmart, an event hosted by Alpha Phi Alpha at 9:06 p.m. on 20 March 2022 with Alpha Omicron Pi, Omega Phi Alpha, Walmart and Omicron Nu Lambda. The money bought vouchers so students could buy goods for donation to First Christian Church, which passed the groceries on. The bill was aimed at homelessness, hunger and tornado relief and had its first reading on 8 March 2022.

src.label: SGA Bill 20-22-S, Funding for the "Run on Walmart" event

events.title: Earth Day tie-dye returned after two years without a celebration
events.body: Bill 41-22-S allocated $125 from legislative discretionary funds for the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee's Earth Day tie-dye tabling event at Centennial Mall on 22 April 2022, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The bill noted that COVID-19 had left WKU without a proper Earth Day celebration for two years, and that the year's theme of sustainable fashion made recycled tie-dye a fitting activity.

src.label: SGA Bill 41-22-S, Funding for an Earth Day Tie-Dye Tabling Event

events.title: SGA's first Mental Health Awareness Week
events.body: SGA ran a mental health awareness week from 25 to 29 April 2022, ahead of Mental Health Awareness Month in May, with an event each day. The week opened with tabling at Centennial Mall from 10:30 a.m. to 2 p.m., with raffled gift cards, music and counselling information, and continued with a Zumba class in the Preston Center on 26 April run with GroupX Fitness. Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee chair Alex Cissell said the point was to reduce the stigma around mental illness.

src.label: Herald, 21 Apr 2022 - "SGA to host Mental Health Awareness events across next week"

events.title: Hilltopper Hunt raised money for a veterans' food charity
events.body: Bill 36-22-S allocated $500 from legislative discretionary funds to Hilltopper Hunt: Egging out Hunger, a donation drive and fundraiser for the Kentucky Veterans Brigade, a charity assisting south central Kentucky veterans facing hunger, homelessness and financial strain. The brigade had opened its doors to the whole Bowling Green community after the December 2021 tornado outbreak. The event doubled as the senior capstone project of four WKU public relations majors.

src.label: SGA Bill 36-22-S, Funding for Hilltopper Hunt: Egging out Hunger for Kentucky Veterans Brigade

events.title: Resolution condemning critical race theory bans passed 16-15
events.body: After weeks of debate and several speeches of affirmation and negation, the senate passed Resolution 7.21f, condemning the banning of critical race theory teaching in postsecondary education. The vote was 16 in favor and 15 against, with two abstentions. Sponsors cited an anticipated bill request in the Kentucky General Assembly, and sponsor Olivia Blackmon said the measure was meant to ensure intellectual freedom in the curriculum rather than politicize classrooms.

events.title: Senate confirmed the year's budget in Bill 1.21f
events.body: At the third meeting of the 21st Senate, on 7 September, SGA passed Bill 1.21f, confirming its budget for the year. Dean of Students Martha Sales opened the meeting on leadership, telling senators they had to learn how to lead and pressing them on their purpose as a student body. President Matthew Wininger announced a planned donor drive in partnership with at least four other student organizations, and Chief of Staff Parker Raybourne announced a Hilltopper Hangout event for 24 September.

leaders.name: Cole Bornefeld
leaders.note: Elected April 2022 with 49% of 1,448 votes. In February 2023 the Speaker of the Senate brought a censure case against him over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram; the Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure, and a Title IX report seeking his removal was filed two days later. Last name currently on the plaque.
profile: Cole Bornefeld came to the presidency by an unusually fast route. He transferred to WKU from Volunteer State Community College as a junior, emailed then-President Matthew Wininger during his first week on campus, and was appointed a senator-at-large at their first meeting. He had not planned to run for president, but after senators urged him to, he formed a ticket the week of the filing deadline and won. He campaigned on programs he backed as a senator, including the Share-A-Swipe meal donation program and growing SGA's scholarship budget, which rose by $3,500 during his presidency. Adjusting to the office, he said it felt like "drinking out of a fire hose," and he sought advice from former student body presidents weekly.

Bornefeld opened the 2022-23 year with an executive retreat on Aug. 29 at the Cliff Todd Center, where his team set three priorities: a one-stop resource guide for students, a push to represent WKU's five regional campuses, which he said was "an area that I really don't think SGA has ever touched," and financial assistance for students as the year's underlying goal. He had met with the director of regional campuses the week before to start that work.

His spring semester was dominated by fallout from anti-LGBTQ Instagram posts he had liked. After the judicial council unanimously declined to censure him, the Queer Student Union removed SGA meetings from its list of campus safe spaces and said it would not associate with SGA until a public apology was released. Addressing the senate on Feb. 21, Bornefeld, who also served as student regent, said he "always commits to loving thy neighbor" but could not commit to always agreeing, tying his position to his Christian values and offering to meet any student over coffee or breakfast to discuss disagreements.

events.title: The Speaker takes the President to the Judicial Council
events.body: Speaker of the Senate Yulia 'Julie' Mishchuk requested a censure hearing against President Cole Bornefeld over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram. Members of the Queer Student Union and both vice presidents attended. The Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure.

events.title: Executive retreat set the year's goals
events.body: SGA's executive team held a formal retreat dinner on Aug. 29 at the Cliff Todd Center to set its agenda for the year. President Cole Bornefeld said the group was building a one-stop resource guide for students and trying to promote SGA at WKU's regional campuses in Elizabethtown, Fort Knox, Glasgow, Owensboro and Somerset. Speaker Julie Mishchuk said the underlying goal of the year was financial assistance for students.

events.title: First meeting filled senate and cabinet vacancies
events.body: At its first meeting of the year on Aug. 30, the senate approved all of President Bornefeld's nominees, including Juan Thomas, Will Hemenover and Sydney Denney as senators-at-large, Aniya Johnson as director of information technology, Donte' Reed as director of enrollment and student experience, and Isaac Kind and Garrett Baum to the judicial council. Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz spoke on the budget and Chief Justice Holden Schroeder swore in the new members.

events.title: Senate approved five nominations and reviewed a shrinking budget
events.body: The senate unanimously confirmed five nominations, including Adan Canizalez as chair of student enrollment and experience and Miles Huff, a track athlete, to the judicial council. Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz urged senators to sponsor more resolutions, which use university funds, because only about $39,460.76 remained of SGA's $100,000 annual budget for bills. Speaker Julie Mishchuk floated a constitutional amendment requiring every senator to sponsor at least one bill or resolution.

events.title: Narcan resolution aimed to put overdose spray in residence halls
events.body: SGA unanimously passed Resolution 2-23-S on Feb. 7 supporting placement of Narcan, an opioid overdose reversal spray, in WKU residence halls. SGA had planned to spend about $1,000 of its own budget, but a University of Kentucky harm reduction specialist helped secure the product through a government grant instead. Housing and Residence Life planned to install the spray in AED-style boxes across its 15 dorms by Aug. 1 to allow time for staff training.

events.title: Menstrual product legislation passed as QSU protested
events.body: At its Feb. 21 meeting SGA passed a resolution supporting menstrual product dispensers on the first floor of every academic building, a $200 bill to distribute 35 menstrual cups at tabling events, and $100 for a community relations survey. Queer Student Union president Alistar Flowers announced QSU had removed SGA meetings from its list of campus safe spaces after the judicial council declined to censure President Bornefeld, and said QSU would not associate with SGA until a public apology was released.

events.title: Senate merged committees and funded Mental Health Awareness Week
events.body: At the April 11 meeting the senate passed Bill 44-23-S, a constitutional amendment merging the Community Relations and Outreach committees starting in 2023-24, which Speaker Mishchuk said would create a stronger committee amid low membership. Senators also unanimously funded a slate of Mental Health Awareness Week events for April 23 through 28, including an Out of the Darkness suicide prevention walk, and passed a $62 terrarium tabling bill. President Bornefeld reported 44 applicants for the upcoming SGA elections.

events.title: Executive retreat sets goals on regional campuses and student resources
events.body: SGA's executive team met at the Cliff Todd Center to set goals for the semester, including a student resource guide and better representation for WKU's regional campuses in Elizabethtown, Fort Knox, Glasgow, Owensboro and Somerset. President Cole Bornefeld said he had met with regional campuses director Derick Strode and called it an area SGA had never touched. Speaker of the Senate Julie Mishchuk said financial assistance for students was the underlying goal.

events.title: Committee chairs installed; vice president serves on governor's higher education committee
events.body: Six committee chairs were installed, including Olivia Feck on student mental health and wellbeing, Elizabeth DeLozier on legislative operations and Ahatali Tahiri on diversity, equity and inclusion. Bornefeld commended Executive Vice President Garrison Reed for his work on Gov. Andy Beshear's higher education committee. Provost Bud Fischer briefed senators on the Quality Enhancement Plan tied to WKU's 2025 accreditation reaffirmation submission.

events.title: SGA presses administrators on Big Red Backpack opt-out default
events.body: Assistant Vice President Jennifer Tougas took SGA feedback on the Big Red Backpack course materials program, which SGA discussions had prompted. Asked why the program defaulted to opt-out, Tougas acknowledged that "schools that use the opt-in approach are far more successful" but said WKU chose opt-out to keep the per-credit-hour cost low. Senators also raised missing textbooks in student orders, and President Timothy Caboni appeared to commend SGA for its role in creating the program.

events.title: Senate sponsors Bowling Green Pride and announces a student veteran scholarship
events.body: A bill by Senator Meghan Pierce allocating $250 from the Legislative Directory to sponsor Bowling Green Pride passed, naming SGA a Rainbow Sponsor and securing tabling space for diversity, equity and inclusion. Director of Enrollment and Student Experience Donte' Reed announced a scholarship for a student veteran in partnership with the Student Veterans Association. Senators also discussed the new campus e-bikes, with suggestions for a Park Street dock and a safety awareness campaign.

events.title: Executives report on a campus listening tour as enrollment chief briefs senate
events.body: Bornefeld said he, Garrison Reed and Sam Kurtz had been holding a listening tour to increase SGA's accessibility to students, citing feedback from the Panhellenic Council. Ethan Logan, vice president of enrollment, told senators WKU's retention rate stood at 76.66% and discussed reaching students who do not speak English as a first language. Senator Salvador León asked whether students could serve as bilingual counselors.

events.title: Appeals court revives part of former SGA president's suit against WKU
events.body: The Sixth Circuit vacated summary judgment on the pre-February 2018 Title IX student-on-student harassment claims of Loandria "Andi" Dahmer, SGA president in 2017-18 and a former student regent, and vacated qualified immunity for SGA faculty adviser Charley Pride. The court upheld dismissal of her remaining claims, including a retaliation claim over President Timothy Caboni declining to write a Rhodes Scholarship recommendation. University spokesperson Jace Lux said WKU would renew its motion for summary judgment on the remaining issue.

events.title: Vice president urges resolutions over spending bills as budget dwindles
events.body: Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz pushed senators to sponsor more resolutions because of the shrinking SGA budget. Five nominations were confirmed unanimously, including Adan Canizalez as chair of student enrollment and experience and Miles Huff to the Judicial Council, filling the vacancy left by Holden Schroeder. Justin Goins was serving as chief justice and nominated Isaac King as associate chief justice.

events.title: Senate passes Narcan resolution; implementation delayed to August
events.body: Resolution 2-23-S, supporting Narcan in WKU residence halls, passed unanimously on Feb. 7 with support from five of seven committees. SGA had planned to spend about $1,000 but obtained the product through a government grant arranged with a University of Kentucky harm reduction specialist, so the resolution became a statement of support. Housing and Residence Life asked to delay implementation to Aug. 1 for training, and director of housing operations Lana Kunkel said no overdose incidents had occurred in a WKU residence hall.

events.title: Queer Student Union removes SGA from its safe space list
events.body: QSU President Alistar Flowers told the senate the organization would no longer list SGA as a safe space and would not associate with it until a public apology was released over the president's Instagram activity. Flowers questioned the fairness of the Judicial Council because most members are nominated by the president. Bornefeld responded in his officer report that he "always commits to loving thy neighbor" but cannot always agree, and the senate passed legislation funding menstrual product dispensers, a community relations survey and Sexual Assault Prevention Month t-shirts.

events.title: Senate funds a trivia night at the Glasgow regional campus
events.body: Bill 38-23-S, funding a trivia night with pizza and prizes at the WKU Glasgow campus, passed unanimously after being presented over Zoom by Glasgow regional ambassador Peyton Hess. Junior Senator Mallory Hardesty said the event would give satellite campus students a real student experience. Adan Canizalez was voted senator of the month for January.

events.title: Constitutional amendment merges two committees for the next school year
events.body: Bill 44-23-S, a constitutional amendment merging the Community Relations committee with Outreach, passed and takes effect in the 2023-24 school year. Speaker Julie Mishchuk said the committees did much of the same work and that low membership meant a merger would strengthen the remaining committees. Bornefeld reported 44 applicants for the election cycle then underway, and bills funding terrariums and Mental Health Awareness Week events also passed.

events.title: WKU dedicated the Commons at Helm Library
events.body: WKU formally dedicated the $35 million Commons at Helm Library, a renovation funded through a partnership with Aramark, and President Timothy Caboni announced early plans for a similar makeover of Cherry Hall. SGA President Cole Bornefeld spoke at the ceremony, saying the building had been full of excitement and community since it opened.

events.title: Afro-Latinidad event funded unanimously
events.body: The senate unanimously passed Bill 40-23-S on 21 March 2023 to fund the Afro-Latinidad event held on 3 April, which featured art displays, presentations, influential Latino figures and culinary displays. Spanish instructor Yertty Vandermolen spoke for the bill, saying people usually picture a tanned Central or Latin American person and forget the African presence in Spanish-speaking countries, and that her students had worked all semester to honour Afro-Latino culture.

src.label: Herald, 22 Mar 2023 - "SGA proposes changes to election process, passes funding for Afro-Latinidad event"

events.title: A former state representative told the senate to get on LinkedIn
events.body: WKU alumnus Jim DeCesare, who spent 14 years in the Kentucky House of Representatives and runs the DeCesare Group, spoke as guest at the senate meeting of 11 April 2023 on the value of LinkedIn for building business relationships and finding work. He told senators he would not do a ten million dollar deal by text and that LinkedIn was a way to make the first introduction. He said Warren County had 7,000 jobs going unfilled.

src.label: Herald, 13 Apr 2023 - "WKU SGA discusses Mental Health Awareness week, combining of committees"

events.title: Fall election turnout doubled and vice president Garrison Reed joined the state postsecondary council
events.body: Fall 2022 election results, announced at midnight, seated Rush Robinson, Callison Padgett and Rhett Helland as freshman senators, Neel Patel for the Gatton Academy, Shy'Ante Williams as graduate senator and Salvador Leon Golib as international student senator. President Cole Bornefeld said the vote total rose from 398 the previous fall to 805. SGA also announced that student body vice president Garrison Reed had been appointed student representative on Kentucky's Council on Postsecondary Education, with a term running through 30 June 2023.

events.title: Title IX complaint against the SGA president sought his removal
events.body: A Title IX report filed with Student Conduct on 19 February 2023 accused President Cole Bornefeld, described in the report as student regent and representative of the student body, of gender-based harassment over four Turning Point USA Instagram posts he liked. The complaint sought his removal, a public statement from WKU and a public apology; the complainant's identity was redacted from the records released to the Herald. Spokesperson Jace Lux said the university does not comment on complaints made to the Office of Student Conduct. Removing an executive who will not resign requires written endorsement from at least 20 percent of the senate, a wait of at least fourteen days and a two-thirds vote of the full senate sitting as a judicial body; the Herald's report of 2 March recorded no outcome.

events.title: Election reform bill failed 19-15; Dance Big Red funding rejected
events.body: Bill 39-23-S, which would have moved the transfer, non-traditional and first-generation senate seats to the fall election and required a two-thirds senate vote before a vacant seat could become an at-large seat, failed 19-15, short of the two-thirds needed. Sponsor Neel Patel, the Gatton Academy senator, called reliance on the president to convert vacancies a dangerous practice for a government organization. Bill 40-23-S, funding an Afro-Latinidad cultural event on 3 April, passed unanimously. Bill 41-23-S, funding Dance Big Red, failed.

events.title: Kurtz ticket elected unopposed
events.body: Sam Kurtz, the outgoing administrative vice president, was elected student body president on a ticket that ran unopposed, with Salvador León as administrative vice president and Annalise Finch as executive vice president. Voting opened on TopNet on 17 April. Fourteen at-large senators were elected, along with the college, class and first-generation seats. Results were read at about 12:30 a.m. in the Downing Student Union senate chambers by Judicial Council Chief Justice Justin Goins.

events.title: Two voucher bills pass unanimously, a poetry night by one vote short of it
events.body: Bill 28-23-S put $500 toward free teeth cleanings at the WKU Dental Health Clinic, amended by committee chair Adan Canizalez to draw on the scholarship programme fund rather than the Legislative Discretionary Fund. Chief of staff Lauren Willett, an author of the bill, said voucher use had risen 660 per cent over the fall semester. Bill 27-23-S allocated $2,000 split 60/30/10 between the ID centre, the Preston Center and the dental hygiene clinic, and both bills passed unanimously. A third bill, $260 for a poetry mic night run with the Talisman, passed on a roll call with senator Ethan Huffaker the only vote against, citing superfluous spending; former SGA president Matthew Wininger had opened the meeting as guest speaker.

src.label: Herald, 1 Feb 2023 - Student Senate passes bills for vouchers, poetry night

leaders.name: Sam Kurtz
leaders.note: Former administrative vice president. Elected April 2023 on an unopposed ticket with Salvador Leon and Annalise Finch.
profile: Sam Kurtz, then the outgoing administrative vice president, was elected student body president in results announced early on April 19, 2023 in the Downing Student Union senate chambers, after voting opened on TopNet on April 17. His KFL ticket, with Annalise Finch as executive vice president and Salvador León as administrative vice president, ran unopposed, and Chief Justice Justin Goins read the results. In a statement, Kurtz said the ticket would "listen to students' concerns, represent their voices, lead with integrity, and promote transparency."

At the 23rd Senate's first fall meeting on Aug. 29, Kurtz nominated Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the Judicial Council from what he called a record number of applicants, and named seven committee heads, including Rush Robinson for Campus Improvements and Sustainability and Karley Solorzano for Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. The Senate's first bill of the year, passed unanimously that September, funded the SGA Pink Walk breast-cancer event. That November the senate backed moving DSU fire drills from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. and funded a Boys and Girls Club toy drive. Speaker of the Senate Sydney Denney wrote or co-wrote several of the year's bills, including a resolution capping student parking fees at $50, a $700 fund to help students pay parking fines, and voucher funding for the Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center. In February 2024 Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donté Reed rolled out a 450-voucher Uber giveaway aimed at student safety and outreach, followed in March by a need-based scholarship awarding Uber vouchers and a Community Builder Excellence Scholarship for incoming Bowling Green-area freshmen; that month the senate also planned a Frankfort trip for the Rally for Higher Education.

The year's fight was internal. In February 2024 the Judicial Council voted 6-0 to censure Administrative Vice President Salvador León after a hearing brought by Denney and the executive cabinet, which alleged León had spent SGA funds - including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit for Neurodiversity Acceptance Week - before the Senate passed the funding bill, in violation of the constitution's clause 2.5.3 requiring the administrative vice president to expend funds only as the Senate authorizes. Chief Justice Isaac King said the cabinet, excluding León, had asked for the censure after León spent the funds despite Kurtz's condition that he wait for Bill 22-23-F to pass, and after he pushed PR Director Preston Romanov to promote the week on SGA social media ahead of the vote, effectively forcing the Senate's hand. León countered that text messages showed Kurtz had signed off on the spending in advance; the council found the spending improper but recommended no discipline beyond the censure itself.

In January 2024 Chief of Staff Lindsey Kelly and enrollment director Donte Reed both resigned, with Reed moving up to chief of staff. That April, Kurtz ran for a second term with Reed as his executive vice president candidate and junior senator Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president; the ticket again ran unopposed on a ballot of more than 60 legislative candidates, and the three were re-elected as the 24th Senate's 34 members were announced the night of April 16-17, 2024. Before that, SGA partnered with WKU Red Wave for a final Red Wave tailgate on April 9, with a student-DJ contest winner earning a $500 scholarship. The 23rd Senate held its last meeting on April 16 with no legislation on the agenda, and Kurtz thanked senators in his final report for what the group had accomplished that year.

events.title: The 23rd Senate corrects its own governing documents
events.body: Three bills from the Legislative Operations Committee: fix references to a 'University Senate' that had since split into separate Faculty and Staff senates, reconcile bylaws language about expelling senators with a constitution that only provides for impeachment, and update committee names that had drifted.

events.title: Fall election winners sworn in
events.body: SGA announced its fall election results on Sept. 20 over an Instagram livestream, electing Savanna Kurtz, Malick Ibrahim and Chloe Ralston as freshman senators, ShyAntye'e Williams as graduate senator, Sim Guan Zhou as international senator and Livi Ray as Gatton Academy senator. Five of the six were sworn in at the following Tuesday meeting. Sophomore senator Rush Robinson received the year's first Senator of the Month award.

events.title: Midyear resignations reshuffle the executive cabinet
events.body: President Sam Kurtz announced the resignations of Chief of Staff Lindsey Kelly and of Donte Reed as director of enrollment and student experience. The senate approved Kurtz's nominations of Reed as the new chief of staff and Sarah Vincent as director of enrollment and student activities. Kurtz also filled vacant transfer/non-traditional, sophomore and graduate senate seats with Sawyer Edmonds, Gabe Jerdon and Elizabeth Gannon.

events.title: Judicial council censures Salvador León
events.body: The SGA judicial council voted 6-0 to censure Administrative Vice President Salvador León after a Feb. 7 hearing on allegations that he spent funds, including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit for Neurodiversity Acceptance Week, before the senate passed the funding bill. León argued text messages showed President Sam Kurtz had accepted the spending, while Kurtz said he asked León multiple times not to spend before the bill passed. The council recommended no further disciplinary action beyond the censure.

events.title: 23rd Senate holds its final meeting
events.body: The 23rd Senate met for the last time with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on senators' final remarks. Kurtz thanked the senate and said in his final report, "We've done a lot of great things this year." Executive Vice President Annie Finch and Administrative Vice President Salvador León also gave closing reports before the 24th Senate's first meeting on April 23.

events.title: Kurtz re-elected unopposed to a second term
events.body: Running with Chief of Staff Donté Reed for executive vice president and junior senator Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president, Kurtz was re-elected without opposition as the 24th Senate's 34 members were announced the same night. More than 60 students had appeared on the ballot for the spring 2024 general election.

events.title: Senate backs a later fire-drill time, funds a toy drive
events.body: At the 23rd Senate's 11th meeting, senators unanimously passed Resolution 6-23-F, backing a change to DSU fire-drill timing from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. after the Mental Health and Wellness Committee argued the earlier hour caused sleep problems and anxiety for students on early schedules or with accommodations. They also unanimously passed Bill 12-23-F, allocating $200 from the legislative discretionary fund for a Boys and Girls Club of Bowling Green toy drive, and swore in newly elected ISEC senator Ashlee Potter.

events.title: Spring committee heads sworn in
events.body: At the spring semester's first meeting, Kurtz appointed Madison Parker Payne as Outreach Committee chair and Sophia Bryant as Mental Health and Well-Being Committee chair; both were approved without contested debate. Executive Vice President Annalise Finch appointed Jaden Marshall to chair the Graduate Advisory Council campus committee and Chloe Ralston to chair the Colonnade General Education committee. Kurtz urged senators to spend down the senate's still-large discretionary budget before the semester's end.

events.title: Cabinet requests censure hearing against León
events.body: Kurtz told the senate the Executive Cabinet had filed a formal report seeking a Judicial Council censure hearing against Administrative Vice President Salvador León. Chief Justice Isaac King said the cabinet's complaint was that León spent project funds before President Kurtz or EVP Finch consented, that he had done so after Kurtz conditioned permission on Bill 22-23-F first passing, and that he pushed PR Director Preston Romanov to promote Neurodiversity Week on SGA social media before the funding bill passed, effectively forcing the Senate's hand. The Executive Cabinet, excluding León, asked for a censure; the hearing was set for Feb. 7.

events.title: Rally trip to Frankfort, new voucher and cleanup plans
events.body: Kurtz previewed a senate trip to Frankfort for the Rally for Higher Education, where SGA planned to meet state Rep. Kevin Jackson and other Kentucky campus governments, and urged senators to seek re-election to preserve institutional knowledge. Chief of Staff Donté Reed introduced a need-based scholarship awarding four Uber vouchers and the Community Builder Excellence Scholarship for incoming Bowling Green-area freshmen. Campus Improvements and Sustainability chair Rush Robinson moved Earth Day from April 22 to April 19 and set a tentative Bowling Green cleanup for March 28.

events.title: SGA closed the year with a Red Wave tailgate
events.body: SGA partnered with WKU Red Wave for the school year's last tailgate before a baseball game against Louisville, featuring winners of a "Battle of the DJs" social-media poll; sophomore Wilson Patterson won the $500 top scholarship prize as "DJ WLZN." Kurtz called the crowd to "savor one last tailgate of the 2023-2024 school year," with SGA grilling food for attendees.

events.title: Spring general election opened with over 60 candidates
events.body: Voting for the spring 2024 general election opened on TopNet with more than 60 students on the ballot for legislative seats. Kurtz, Chief of Staff Donté Reed and junior senator Ethan Taylor ran unopposed for student body president, executive vice president and administrative vice president respectively; the legislative council ballot included three senior, three junior and three sophomore senator seats, six college seats, an ISEC senator, a first-generation senator, a transfer/non-traditional senator and 14 senator-at-large seats.

events.title: Senate rejects Shark Tank grant fund, funds Pride table
events.body: Senators voted 3-21 against Bill 2-23-F, which would have taken $750 from the legislative discretionary budget for grants at a Student Activities "Shark Tank" pitch event. The same meeting passed Bill 3-23-F, spending $30 to sponsor an SGA table at Bowling Green Pride on Oct. 21, by 21-0 with three abstentions.

events.title: Caboni takes senator questions on election day access and buildings
events.body: President Timothy Caboni told the ninth meeting of the 23rd Senate that WKU would use the Historic Railpark's BG Trolley to carry students to State Street polling places on a class day. He also outlined plans to replace Hugh Poland, Douglas Keen and Grise halls and to build a fieldhouse and a new Gordon Ford building. Senators questioned him on accessibility ramps, sustainability partnerships and Living Learning Communities.

events.title: Senate spends $10,000 in organizational aid on 20 groups
events.body: Bill 5-23-F, written by Administrative Vice President Salvador Leon, split $10,000 among 20 registered student organizations at $500 each, including Black Women of Western, WKU Mock Trial, HOLAS and Best Buddies. The meeting also passed a constitutional amendment fixing the title of the Intercultural Student Engagement senator, $120 for World Kindness Day tabling and $600 for a Veterans Day 5K at Kereiakes Park. All four measures passed unanimously.

events.title: Resolution asks WKU to move fire drills from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m.
events.body: Resolution 6-23-F, created by the Mental Health and Wellness Committee, put SGA behind changing residence hall fire drill times from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. The committee argued the 5 a.m. time caused sleep problems and anxiety for students with early schedules, accommodations or emotional support animals. Authors were Geoffrey Aberle, Sophia Bryant and Callison Padgett, and the resolution passed unanimously.

events.title: Eight bills create Honors senate seat and set Judicial Council office hours
events.body: The final fall meeting passed all eight measures unanimously, including Bill 14-23-F creating a Mahurin Honors College senator seat, sponsored by the Judicial Council and written by Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson. Bill 13-23-F raised the chief justice's required office hours from one to five per week and Bill 16-23-F required Judicial Council members to keep two office hours monthly. Leon reported the Senate had spent $1,347.63 of its $9,750 legislative discretionary budget, about 14.87%.

events.title: Chief of staff and enrollment director resign, Reed elevated
events.body: Kurtz announced the resignations of Chief of Staff Lindsey Kelly and Director of Enrollment and Student Experience Donte Reed at the first meeting of the spring semester. Kurtz then nominated Reed as chief of staff and Sarah Vincent to the vacated enrollment post, and both were approved. Sawyer Edmonds, Gabe Jerdon and Elizabeth Gannon were appointed to vacant transfer, sophomore and graduate senate seats.

events.title: Executive cabinet files censure complaint against vice president Leon
events.body: Kurtz told the Senate the executive cabinet had filed a formal report to the Judicial Council seeking a censure hearing against Administrative Vice President Salvador Leon. Chief Justice Isaac King said Leon spent project budget funds without the approval of Kurtz or Executive Vice President Annalise Finch, had SGA's public relations director promote Neurodiversity Week before its bill passed, and thereby forced the Senate's hand on Bill 22-23-S. Leon responded that the matter was not personal and said he would explain more at the hearing.

events.title: Judicial Council censures Leon 6-0 with no further discipline
events.body: At a Feb. 7 hearing, Speaker of the Senate Sydney Denney presented three allegations, including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit paid on Feb. 1 from the executive project and legislative discretionary budgets before Bill 22-23-S reached the Senate on Feb. 6. Leon countered with text messages in which Kurtz replied "sweet" and "bet sounds good" to his spending plans, and said he was paying a fee and doing his job. The council voted 6-0 to censure him, recommended no further action and called the episode a learning experience.

events.title: Senate backs a $5 per semester sustainability fee
events.body: Resolution 26-23-S, written by Sophomore Senator Rush Robinson, put SGA behind charging students a $5 sustainability fee each semester with the proceeds going to the Office of Sustainability. Robinson also authored Bill 25-23-S, giving that office $500 from the legislative discretionary budget for the food pantry, scholarships and an Earth Day event. Both passed unanimously.

events.title: Borrow-a-Calculator program created after student survey
events.body: Bill 2923-S set up a program letting students check out TI-84 calculators from the SGA office for a week at a time. Authors Kaison Barton and Donte Reed cited a survey finding 17% of students surveyed owned no calculator and 93% had taken a class requiring one. Assistant Provost Marko Dumancic spoke for the bill and said the Center for Innovative Teaching and Learning would fund 10 more calculators, bringing the total to 15. The Senate also passed Resolution 2132-S seeking awnings or benches at Topper Transit stops.

events.title: Student group confronts SGA over silence on Rittenhouse visit
events.body: Avery Wells and members of the student advocacy group "For the People" told the Senate that SGA was the only major organization not to oppose Turning Point USA bringing Kyle Rittenhouse to campus, and called the response they got from the executive board unacceptable. Wells also said 40% of the Senate belonged to Greek life and that SGA had a disconnect with cultural communities on campus. Kurtz replied that as an apolitical organization SGA's role was to ensure all voices could be heard, and said he did not control who chose to run. Senators voted the same night on 13 constitutional amendments, including renaming the executive posts, raising senate and cabinet GPA floors to 2.5 and 2.75, and allowing removal from office after two censures in one year.

events.title: Every executive candidate runs unopposed at spring town hall
events.body: At an Executive Town Hall in the senate chambers, Chief Justice Isaac King questioned the three executive candidates, all of whom were unopposed: Kurtz for student body president, Donte Reed for executive vice president and Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president. Kurtz said the ticket intended to create more voucher programs modeled on the February Uber vouchers and to keep grilling at SGA events for students who were food insecure. Reed said students did not have to be in SGA to write a bill or resolution.

events.title: 24th Senate opens with Vincent as speaker and Henderson as chief justice
events.body: Sarah Vincent defeated Sophia Bryant for Speaker of the Senate at the first meeting of the 24th Senate. Anne-Marie Wright was appointed chief of staff and Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson was appointed chief justice, all sworn in by outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King. Kurtz announced the Chief Communications Officer post, formerly Director of Public Relations, was open.

events.title: Pink Walk held with Panhellenic and the Interfraternity Council
events.body: SGA, the Panhellenic Society and the Interfraternity Council together held the Pink Walk on 5 October 2023, a guest-speaker event honouring those affected by breast cancer. The first bill passed by the 23rd Senate, on 20 September, had funded it. The walk became an annual SGA fixture, repeated in October 2024.

events.title: Abby Nash Creativity Scholarship opened
events.body: SGA opened the Abby Nash Creativity Scholarship in March 2024, honouring a senior graphic design and marketing major who died on 13 December 2023. It gave two students $500 each, aimed at those in creative departments such as art and design, marketing, English, media and communication, music and theatre and dance, though anyone could apply. Authored by CEBS senator Kayla Distler with Jack McCoun and Mckenna Fleshman, it was non-renewable unless a later senate wrote a bill to change it.

src.label: Herald, 12 Mar 2024 - "SGA opens Abby Nash Creativity Scholarship"

events.title: DEI Week ran a different theme every day
events.body: Bill 34-23-S allocated $150 from the legislative discretionary budget for SGA's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Week from 25 to 28 March 2024, with a themed tabling initiative each day. Mental Health Matters on 25 March brought Humane Society dogs and Talley Family Counseling Center material; Multicultural Day followed on 26 March with a prize wheel on campus demographics; Safe Sexual Health on 27 March was run with Health Education and Promotion and handed out free HIV testing information; and 28 March covered deaf awareness and hearing education.

src.label: Herald, 13 Mar 2024 - "SGA passes 4 bills to fund upcoming events"

events.title: Two hundred dollars for a book drive and a raffle basket
events.body: Bill 55-23-S passed unanimously on 11 April 2024, allocating $200 from the legislative discretionary budget for a book drive collecting donations in the SGA office and at tabling events from 15 to 26 April for local schools and programmes. Fifty dollars of that funded a "book lovers" raffle basket of books, pens and snacks to encourage donations, with raffle tickets given for each book donated.

src.label: Herald, 12 Apr 2024 - "SGA holds weekly meeting, passes 1 resolution, 3 bills"

events.title: First bill of the 23rd Senate funded the Pink Walk
events.body: At its fifth meeting the 23rd Senate passed its first piece of legislation, Bill 1-23-F, allocating $500 from SGA's scholarship budget to the SGA Pink Walk, an October breast cancer awareness event for students and the Bowling Green community. The money covered bracelets, ribbons, water and raffle prizes. The bill was written by Donte Reed, Rush Robinson and Anne-Marie Wright and passed unanimously, 28-0.

events.title: SGA launched an Uber voucher program and moved against parking fees
events.body: President Sam Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donte Reed announced 450 Uber vouchers worth $10 each, given out through weekly social media giveaways, senate meeting attendance, SGA events and need-based scholarships. Resolution 18-23-S, written by Speaker of the Senate Sydney Denney and Reed, put SGA on record supporting a $50 cap on student parking fees, noting citations ranged from $10 to $600. Bill 19-23-S set aside $700 from the legislative discretionary budget to pay citations for financially vulnerable students, excluding tickets for disability, safety zone or fire lane violations. Bill 23-23-S allocated a further $1,045 for Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center vouchers, and all the legislation passed unanimously.

events.title: Kurtz seated a five-member Judicial Council and seven committee heads
events.body: At SGA's first meeting of the fall semester, the senate approved President Sam Kurtz's nominations of Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the 2023-24 Judicial Council. Kurtz said a record number of students had applied and were interviewed over the summer before the field was narrowed to five. He also announced seven committee heads, among them Rush Robinson for Campus Improvements and Sustainability and Karley Solorzano for Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. The new appointees took the oath of office at the meeting.

events.title: Four bills fund a month of events, and one of them takes a fight
events.body: At the 23rd Senate's twentieth meeting, on 12 March 2024, four funding bills passed. Bill 34-23-S gave $150 to an SGA Diversity, Equity and Inclusion week of tabling from 25 to 28 March, a different initiative each day: mental health, campus demographics, safe sexual health, and deaf awareness. Bill 35-23-S gave $450 to an SGA Spring Fling on the South Lawn, a cookout with kickball and cornhole tournaments and raffles for Uber vouchers, its proceeds going to the Kids Cancer Alliance; after debate among senators over the amount it passed 28-2, the only bill of the four not carried unanimously. Bill 36-23-S gave $280 to a Hope Harbor Denim Day event on sexual assault awareness and Bill 38-23-S gave $650 to the annual Mental Health Week in April.

executive.name: Salvador León
executive.note: Censured 6-0 by the Judicial Council on 7 Feb 2024 over premature spending.

committees.name: Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee

senate.note: The 2023-2024 Judicial Council was Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed, nominated by Kurtz from a 'record number' of applicants (Herald, 30 Aug 2023). Justin Goins, chief justice of the outgoing Judicial Council, read the April 2023 election results. Isaac King is confirmed as chief justice by 6 Feb 2024, explaining the Executive Cabinet's censure complaint against León (Herald, 6 Feb 2024), and was still chief justice at the April 2024 town hall; exactly when he succeeded Goins between Aug 2023 and Feb 2024 is not established in available sourcing.

leaders.name: Sam Kurtz
leaders.note: Re-elected unopposed. Warned the Senate repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber meant the 2025 election mattered more than usual.
profile: Kurtz opened the 2024-25 year presiding over the 24th Senate, which passed SGA's $100,000 budget at its first meeting on Aug. 27. Sitting down with the Herald editorial board alongside his executive cabinet, he described SGA as "a vessel for good" and a group of 45 to 50 people advocating for students, and credited President Caboni with keeping the budget untouched for several years.

Through the spring he presided over a run of student-welfare legislation, including the Gordon Wilson Hall elevator resolution and a resolution seeking 24/7 library hours during finals week. In February he announced a POLLapalooza push to raise election participation, telling the Senate, "My goal is that 3,000 students vote in our election."

Kurtz closed his term at the 24th Senate's final meeting on April 15, having served as student body president for two years and holding executive branch positions for most of his college career, and prepared to graduate at the end of the semester. He received a standing ovation after his last report, and his parting words to senators were "Please be for the students."

events.title: A mental health survey, and a warning about the election
events.body: The Senate passed Bill 4-25-S funding a DEI Committee tabling event to gather anonymous mental health survey responses. Dean of Students Martha Sales told the Senate 'you cannot isolate and educate at the same time'. Kurtz warned repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber made the spring election matter more than usual.

events.title: Rush Robinson elected on a turnout of 966
events.body: Elected alongside class, college, transfer, first-generation, Intercultural Student Engagement Center and Honors College senators - constituencies the 1966 constitution had no concept of.

events.title: Senate passed $100,000 budget at first meeting
events.body: At its first meeting of the year on Aug. 27, the SGA Senate passed a $100,000 budget for 2024-25, including $20,000 for organizational aid, $23,500 for scholarships and $10,705 in legislative discretionary funding. Executive leaders told the Herald editorial board they intended to spend the full allocation, and President Sam Kurtz credited WKU President Caboni with keeping the budget level for several years.

events.title: Fall election winners sworn in, school safety bill passed
events.body: Five senators elected in the fall election, three freshman senators plus an international and a Gatton Academy senator, were sworn in at the Oct. 1 meeting. The Senate passed three bills, including Bill 4-24-F to make school safety training mandatory for WKU professors and require posted emergency exits in classrooms, and two bills backing a Spooktober fundraiser for the Potter Children's Home Initiative.

events.title: Three senators removed for excessive absences
events.body: Senators Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty were removed from their seats at a Nov. 6 censure meeting after each accumulated at least six unexcused absences from weekly senate meetings. The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove them under a constitutional provision requiring removal of any senator censured twice, calling the decision a matter of accountability rather than an attack on character.

events.title: Trump DEI order prompted constitutional review
events.body: Chief Justice Morgan Gammons said the SGA Constitution might require amendment to its diversity, equity and inclusion provisions after President Trump's executive order directing federal agencies to end DEI mandates. Gammons said the Judicial Council would meet to decide whether an amendment was needed, noting that WKU receives federal funding as a public university. The Senate also filled several appointed positions at the same meeting.

events.title: Resolution backed Gordon Wilson Hall elevator
events.body: The Senate passed Resolution 2-25-S supporting installation of elevators in Gordon Wilson Hall, prompted by wheelchair user Kiersten Washington, whose dance appreciation class was scheduled on the building's third floor. It also passed Resolution 1-25-S supporting 24/7 hours at The Commons at Helm Library during finals week, and Kurtz announced a POLLapalooza effort with a goal of 3,000 voters in the April election.

events.title: Resolution supported mental health advisory board
events.body: The Senate passed Resolution 4-25-S supporting the formation of a Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Advisory Board to advise upper-level administration on student mental health policy, with Dean of Students Martha Sales planned to oversee its creation. Co-author Emma Harris, the Resident Staff Association president, said Counseling Center staffing shortages had pushed students to rely on resident advisors. The Senate passed eight bills at the same meeting.

events.title: Students ratified DEI amendment with 88% of vote
events.body: In the spring election, the student body approved Bill 21-25-S, the constitutional amendment renaming the DEI Committee to the Action and Opportunity Committee, with 88% of votes in favor. Committee chair Megan Farmer said the committee at its core was not changing and the rename was meant to better communicate its actions. Results for 31 senate seats were announced the same night.

events.title: 24th Senate held final meeting
events.body: The 24th Senate met for the last time on April 15 with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on farewells. President Sam Kurtz, Vice President Donte Reed and Chief Financial Officer Ethan Taylor each received a standing ovation, and the Senate recorded 295 spring scholarship applications, far above the roughly 40-applicant average of past years.

events.title: 24th Senate installed: Vincent elected speaker, Henderson named chief justice
events.body: At the 24th Senate's first meeting, newly elected senators were sworn in and Sarah Vincent, College of Health and Human Services senator, was elected Speaker of the Senate over Sophia Bryant. Senior senator Anne-Marie Wright was appointed Chief of Staff, and Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson was appointed Chief Justice. Outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King swore in the new officers, officially opening the 2024-25 term.

events.title: Committee chairs and Judicial Council approved at fall opener
events.body: At the 24th Senate's first fall meeting, the Senate unanimously approved Kurtz's nominations of Aziz Umarov, Madison Payne, Neill Kane and Sam Dorris to the 2024-25 Judicial Council, and confirmed six committee chairs: Hannah Evans (Legislative Operations), Savanna Kurtz (Student Experience and Enrollment), Ryan Dilts (Outreach and Public Relations), Megan Farmer (DEI), Sophia Bryant (Student Mental Health and Wellbeing) and Annie Finch (Community Relations). President Timothy Caboni addressed the Senate on campus building renovations, the Mahurin Honors College restructuring and WKU's push for R2 research status.

events.title: Student regent presses administrators over student worker funding
events.body: At the Board of Regents retreat, Student Regent Sam Kurtz said a friend working in the biotechnology center had been told some 2023 funding for student jobs would not return in 2024. Kurtz raised the concern during a budget model presentation as units across WKU were being ordered to cut 7.5% of their approved spending and absorb a 10% overhead charge on self-generated revenue. He asked the room, "Isn't that the point of why we're all here, to look out for the students?" and afterwards told the Herald the answers he got were cookie-cutter.

events.title: 24th Senate approves $100,000 budget and seats first Honors senator
events.body: The Senate unanimously approved Chief Financial Officer Ethan Taylor's $100,000 budget, which raised legislative discretionary and office worker spending and cut public relations spending. Five senators were appointed, including Caden Lucas as the first Mahurin Honors College senator, along with a four-member Judicial Council. Caboni gave the university report and closed on meal plans, saying orange chicken had become a meal swipe.

events.title: Executives break down the SGA budget for the Herald editorial board
events.body: Taylor told the Herald Editorial Board the 2024-25 budget included $20,000 for organizational aid, $23,500 for scholarships and $10,705 in legislative discretionary funding. Kurtz said the total had stayed at $100,000 for several years and credited Caboni with keeping it untouched. Chief Justice Ellen Henderson said the Senate would vote on election codes at its Sept. 3 meeting and stressed the Judicial Council's independence from the Senate and cabinet.

events.title: Senate passes bill declaring SGA nonpartisan
events.body: Bill 50-23-S reaffirmed that SGA represents the student body rather than acting as a political group and stated its duty to put forward only nonpartisan legislation. It passed unanimously. The same meeting named Rush Robinson chair of the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee, swore in Hadley Whipple as Secretary of the Senate and added Hailey Stapleton to the Judicial Council.

events.title: Vice president pushes for an on-campus polling place
events.body: Student Body Vice President Donte Reed told the Senate he was working with a student advocacy group to get a polling center on campus, saying he otherwise had to drive about three hours home to vote. Kurtz said SGA should find ways to calm tensions after the November election and remind students where to get help. Dean of Students Martha Sales spoke on stress and belonging and told senators to check on their strong friends.

events.title: Fall ballot draws 20 freshman candidates and none for graduate seat
events.body: Chief Justice Ellen Henderson reported that 20 students were running for freshman senator, one for Gatton Academy senator, one for international senator and none for graduate senator, with voting set for Sept. 26 and 27 on TopNet. The Senate also passed Resolutions 1-24-F and 2-24-F backing a semester-long fundraising drive to raise $2,000 for Potter Children's Home, beginning with a Jump Air Zone event where 40% of proceeds would go to the fund.

events.title: Bill seeks mandatory school safety training for professors
events.body: Bill 4-24-F, authored by Senator Annalise Finch, called for school safety training to be made mandatory for all WKU professors and for emergency exits to be posted in every instructional classroom. Finch noted the training was not then mandatory and that K-12 rules do not transfer directly to college. Professors would be able to opt out for mental health reasons. The bill passed, and five senators elected in the fall race were sworn in.

events.title: Three senators removed from the Senate after second censure
events.body: The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty for excessive unexcused absences, each having accumulated at least six. Section 2.2 of the bylaws allows three unexcused absences a semester, and Section 4.6.12 of the constitution requires removal after a second censure; all three had already been censured once and given extra office hours. The council's minutes said senators cannot represent students they are not present to serve. Petty later told the Herald her absences were due to medical issues.

events.title: Senate funds food pantry and swears in a new chief justice
events.body: Bill 17-24-F gave $500 to the Office of Sustainability to restock its food and resource pantry, with Director of Sustainability Leslie North telling senators the office had given away 16,000 items the previous semester. Bill 16-24-F funded 40 Fresh Food Company meal vouchers for the Dean of Students office, and two more bills funded a finals week tabling event and a Boys and Girls Club toy drive. Chief Justice Ellen Henderson swore in Associate Chief Justice Morgan Gammons as chief justice before graduating.

events.title: Heat press bill revived after failing in the fall
events.body: Bill 19-24-F, allocating $240 for a heat press for the Fashion Merchandising Department, passed unanimously after failing at the last meeting of the fall semester and being carried over. Author Jenna Wells said the department had overspent in the past and lacked excess funds. Kurtz said several senators had resigned over the break and Judicial Council members had graduated, requiring him to make appointments, and he pressed senators to build the coming election.

events.title: Chief justice says SGA constitution may need a DEI amendment
events.body: Chief Justice Morgan Gammons told the Herald after the weekly meeting that the SGA Constitution's diversity, equity and inclusion provisions might need amending after President Donald Trump's Jan. 20 executive order directing federal agencies to end DEI mandates. Gammons said the Judicial Council would meet to decide whether to send a constitutional referendum to the Senate, noting WKU receives federal funding and had to reevaluate. Four senators were appointed to new positions and Gavin Grawe was voted associate chief justice.

events.title: Senate backs Gordon Wilson elevator and a 24-hour finals study space
events.body: Resolution 2-25-S, written by wheelchair user and honorary SGA member Kiersten Washington, supported installing an elevator in Gordon Wilson Hall after she was scheduled for a third-floor class in a 1927 building with no elevator. DEI Chair Megan Farmer said students cannot get the full range of an education if they cannot enter the space. Resolution 1-25-S, by senators Jakob Barker and Cayden Bailey, sought 24-hour hours at the Commons at Helm Library during finals week, noting WKU offers no 24-hour student space.

events.title: Student body ratifies DEI committee amendment with 88% support
events.body: Bill 21-25-S, renaming the DEI Committee the Action and Opportunity Committee, passed the campus-wide constitutional vote with 88% in favor. Rush Robinson was elected student body president unopposed on a ticket with Savanna Kurtz and Gabriel Jerdon, and 31 senators were named. DEI Committee Chair Megan Farmer said the committee's core work was not changing and that the new name better communicated its actions.

events.title: Scholarship applications reach 295 as the 24th Senate closes
events.body: At the final meeting of the 24th Senate, Student Experience Officer Savanna Kurtz reported 295 scholarship applications in the spring semester alone, against an average of about 40 in past years. No legislation was on the agenda. Kurtz, Reed and Taylor each received a standing ovation after their final reports.

events.title: Faculty Senate endorses two SGA resolutions
events.body: The Faculty Senate voted to endorse SGA Resolution 2-25-S on the Gordon Wilson Hall elevator and Resolution X-22-S on extending Commons at Helm Library hours during finals week. The library resolution recorded Dean of WKU Libraries Joshua Vossler's position that staffing made 24-hour service unworkable and that student use would not justify the cost, so the Faculty Senate endorsed finding an alternative 24-hour space instead. Senate Chair Gordon McKerral said Provost Bud Fischer told them the elevator was already a top priority.

events.title: Whipple elected speaker as the 25th Senate convenes
events.body: Hadley Whipple won the Speaker of the Senate vote over Caden Lucas and Sophia Bryant at the first meeting of the 25th Senate. President Rush Robinson appointed Maggie Yelton chief of staff and Amelia Tucker senator-at-large, and Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins kept his post for a second year. Former Speaker Sarah Vincent swore in the new Senate.

events.title: Gordon Wilson elevator scheduled for construction
events.body: Chief Facilities Officer Bryan Russell told the Herald that Facilities Management and Planning, Design and Construction would jointly install an elevator in Gordon Wilson Hall, with a project goal of starting construction in fiscal 2026. The project followed Washington's February resolution and the Faculty Senate's April endorsement. Russell also said two Cravens Library elevators would be modernized, the first finishing in September and the second in December.

events.title: Robinson reappoints Jenkins chief communications officer
events.body: In one of his first acts after taking office, Robinson reappointed Preston Jenkins as chief communications officer; the Senate later confirmed the pick unanimously.

events.title: Borrow-A-Calculator went live
events.body: Chief of Staff Anne-Marie Wright told the senate on 3 September 2024 that the Borrow-A-Calculator programme had started, run with the Center for Innovative Teaching and Learning, the Department of Mathematics and Ogden College. Students could borrow a new TI-84 graphing calculator free for one week and renew it, on presentation of a valid student ID.

src.label: Herald, 3 Sep 2024 - "SGA passes bill, details Borrow-A-Calculator program"

events.title: Hill-O-Ween drew just over a hundred students
events.body: SGA held Hill-O-Ween at Centennial Mall on 29 October 2024, handing out sweets and running activities with the Hilltopper Organization of Latin American Students and the Accessibility Ambassadors. Students painted succulent pots and made candy apples. Junior senator Rush Robinson, who organised it, counted just over 100 people. At the meeting that evening the senate allocated $325 for a Pack the Pantry food drive run with WKU ROTC through November.

events.title: First Topper Chef cooking class
events.body: SGA held the first Topper Chef cooking class on 4 November 2024 in Academic Complex room 202, where students cooked pork and vegetable tacos, beans, elotes and guacamole from 4 p.m. and ate together until 7:30. Senior Jenna Wells pitched it from her seat on the Student Mental Health and Well-being Committee, saying students needed to look after themselves outside the classroom and that basic cooking and cooking safety were useful skills. She cited a grease fire in Pearce-Ford Tower the previous year.
